jobs.title: PhD in Materials Science
jobs.department: ITN - Department of Science and Technology
jobs.description_html:
Join us in developing next-generation, machine-learning accelerated computational models to understand and predict coupled ionic and electronic transport in organic materials for sustainable energy technologies.

Your work assignments

The doctoral student will develop multiscale simulation methods to understand how ions and electronic charge carriers move through organic functional materials. Coupled ionic and electronic transport is central to the operation of many emerging energy technologies, including organic batteries, mixed ionic-electronic conductors, and electrochemical devices. While atomistic simulations can provide detailed information about molecular structure and dynamics, establishing direct links to charge and ion transport across experimentally relevant length and time scales remains a challenge.

This PhD topic falls within the area of computational materials science and focuses on the development of a multiscale modeling framework that combines atomistic simulations with charge transport models. The work will involve the implementation of a delocalized kinetic Monte Carlo method that integrates coupled electronic and ionic transport on parallel high-performance computing infrastructures. Machine-learning techniques will be implemented to accelerate the computation of transition rates and the prediction of rare events. Structural and electronic information feeding the kinetic Monte Carlo model will be generated from molecular dynamics simulations.

  • Develop and implement delocalized kinetic Monte Carlo models for electronic charge transport in organic materials.
  • Couple charge-transport simulations to molecular dynamics of ion motion and structural dynamics.
  • Implementation of the model on high-performance computing infrastructure.
  • Investigate the interplay between molecular structure, morphology, ionic transport, and electronic transport across multiple length and time scales
  • Develop machine-learning models to accelerate rate calculations and rare event sampling.
  • Collaborate with experimental and theoretical groups within LOE and its partners

As a doctoral student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in (Applied) Physics, Materials Science, a related field, or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in a relevant area. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

We are looking for candidates with a strong interest in interdisciplinary research at the interface of physics, materials science, scientific programming, and energy technologies. Experience in one or more of the following areas is considered an advantage: Scientific programming in C++, Fortran, or related languages; scientific machine learning; Monte Carlo simulations; molecular dynamics simulations.

The successful candidates have strong problem-solving skills, are able to work effectively in a multidisciplinary and international team, and demonstrate excellent communication abilities.

Great emphasis will be placed on personal qualities and suitability.

Your workplace

Join us at the Laboratory of Organic Electronics (LOE) at Linköping University, a world-renowned center for groundbreaking research in bioelectronics, energy devices, printed electronics, and nanooptics using organic materials. Our innovative work focuses on the dynamic coupling of ion and electron movement. At LOE, you’ll be part of a vibrant community of over 150 researchers, including professors, senior and junior scientists, and fellow PhD students. Our collaborative environment is multidisciplinary, fostering creativity and innovation. ( http://liu.se/loe). You will work within the Materials Science group, part of the Theory & Modelling unit.

Read more: https://wise-materials.org

The employment

When taking up the post, you will be admitted to the program for doctoral studies. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University.

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan. 

Starting date during Winter 2026/2027 or by agreement.

This recruitment is connected to the Wallenberg Initiative Materials Science for Sustainability (WISE, https://wise-materials.org). WISE, funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, is the largest-ever investment in materials science in Sweden and encompasses major efforts at Sweden’s foremost universities over the course of 12 years. The vision is a sustainable future through materials science.

All early-stage researchers recruited into the WISE program will be a part of the WISE Research School https://wise-materials.org/research-school/ an ambitious nationwide program of seminars, courses, research visits, and other activities to promote a strong multi-disciplinary and international network between PhD students, postdocs, researchers, and industry.

Salary and employment benefits

The salary of doctoral students is determined according to a locally negotiated salary progression.

As an employee of Linköping University, you are entitled to the following benefits:

  • Paid vacation (28 workdays per year, corresponding to 5 ½ weeks)
  • Free access to the Swedish health-care system (full health-care coverage)
  • Paid maternity / paternity leave (up to 390 days per child)
  • Accrued pension. During your work time in Sweden, you accrue income pension, paid by the employer, which is payable also if you leave Sweden

More information about employment benefits at Linköping University are available at  https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/employee-benefits. More information on the Swedish social insurance benefits system can be found at https://www.forsakringskassan.se/english/moving-to-working-studying-or-newly-arrived-in-sweden/social-insurance-system

jobs.title: PhD student in optimal motion planning for drone swarms
jobs.description_html:
The Division of Automatic Control is now seeking a PhD student to work in the new national Center for Heterogeneous Adaptive Swarm Systems (CHASS) funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF) at the Department of Electrical Engineering (ISY).

Your work assignments

The multidisciplinary center for heterogeneous adaptive swarm systems (CHASS) is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI, autonomous systems, robotics, and swarm intelligence to develop novel solutions for autonomous heterogeneous swarm systems for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a leader in intelligent, adaptive, and trustworthy swarm systems by pioneering autonomous heterogeneous collectives of space, aerial, ground, surface, and underwater platforms that can operate as a unified intelligent entity with minimal human intervention. The research program focuses on six key themes: Drone Design, Adaptation, & Production; Perception, Sensing, & Communication; Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation; Coordination, Self-Governance, & Self-Improvement; Human Swarm Interaction; and Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. The PhD position in this announcement focuses on the research theme Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation.

CHASS will drive world-class research in autonomous swarm systems through a strong, stimulating, and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. CHASS will also serve as a national hub for autonomous swarm systems, promoting education, knowledge sharing, innovation, and policy development.

The position focuses on uncertainty-aware, optimization-based motion planning at the control and planning layer. You will develop scalable trajectory optimization and real-time Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategies that use the swarm’s belief state to ensure safety, maximizing information gain, and achieving reliable goal completion. Working within a collaborative and cross-disciplinary consortium, you will help bridge the gap between high-level swarm autonomy and robust physical motion execution in demanding GNSS-denied environments, such as those encountered in search-and-rescue and environmental surveillance.

Collaboration across areas within the center is strongly encouraged. As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have been awarded a degree at advanced level in Electrical Engineering, Engineering Physics, Computer Science, Engineering Mathematics, or have completed courses totaling at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 higher education credits are at advanced level as specified above, or have otherwise acquired essentially equivalent knowledge. The degree requirement must be fulfilled no later than the time when the decision on employment is made, i.e., when the employment contract is signed.

We are looking for someone who works purposefully, takes responsibility for their tasks, and maintains high quality in their work. You take initiative, are self-reliant, and have strong analytical skills with a scientific approach. Furthermore, you should have the ability to place your research in a broader context and relate your work to the overall goals of the project and the subject area. You work in a structured manner and can prioritize among tasks. This position also requires the ability to communicate your message clearly, both in academic settings and in collaboration with others. As our operations are conducted in an international environment, you must also have a good ability to communicate in English, both orally and in writing.

Your workplace

The Division of Automatic Control offers a vibrant, internationally oriented research environment with a strong balance between theory and real-world applications. The division conducts high-quality research, doctoral education, and undergraduate teaching in key and rapidly evolving areas such as autonomous systems, data-driven modeling, learning-based control, optimization, complex networks, and sensor fusion.

Research at the division is characterized by close integration of methodological development and practical applications. We maintain extensive collaborations with industrial partners as well as with leading research groups worldwide, providing doctoral students with excellent opportunities for international exposure and impactful research.

As a PhD student, you will join an open, collaborative, and intellectually stimulating environment that values scientific curiosity, independence, and teamwork. More information about the division is available at: https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/isy/rt.

For more information about working at ISY, please visit: https://liu.se/en/article/open-positions-at-isy.

The employment

When taking up the post, you will be admitted to the program for doctoral studies. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University.

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan. 

To learn more on working as a PhD student at ISY, please contact: isyphdcouncil@groups.liu.se.

jobs.title: PhD student in sustainability transformations and international business development
jobs.department: IEI - Department of Management and Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Why do some biogas projects develop into viable businesses and stimulate wider adoption, while others stall or fail?

Your work assignments

You will conduct research within the Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC), in a doctoral project funded by the Swedish Energy Agency. The project investigates how international projects contribute to the establishment and diffusion of biogas systems, with particular attention to business development in urban contexts. Although biogas technologies are established and organic waste resources are available in many places globally, developing viable businesses remains challenging. The research will examine how companies and their partners address these challenges, why projects succeed or fail, and under what conditions individual initiatives contribute to the wider adoption of biogas systems. It will connect sustainability transitions research with international business development from a company perspective.

The research will address questions such as:

  • How do business models, partnerships and local institutional conditions influence the establishment and long-term viability of biogas projects?
  • How can collaborations enable market entry and create opportunities for biogas companies?
  • How can individual biogas projects support wider diffusion of biogas systems?

The empirical work will focus primarily on projects outside Sweden. Global South is an intended study context, complemented by a context in the Global North to be selected during the project. You will develop a structured mapping of relevant initiatives and transparent criteria for selecting a small number of cases for in-depth study.

The study will combine following ongoing projects over time with retrospective analysis of completed, discontinued or stalled initiatives. Cases will include projects involving Swedish companies and projects led by actors from other countries. This approach will support international comparison and learning while providing access to cases with established outcomes.

Your work will include literature reviews, interviews, document analysis, international fieldwork and comparative case analysis. Active collaboration with companies and other stakeholders is an integral part of the research. Alongside academic publications and your doctoral thesis, you will translate findings into practical insights for BSRC partner companies on international business development.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in industrial engineering and management, sustainability engineering and management, environmental management, sustainability studies, innovation studies, business administration or another relevant field, or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in a relevant field. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way. The requirement for a degree must be met no later than the time the employment decision is finalized, which occurs when the employment contract is signed.

As a person, you are analytical, self-motivated, and able to work both independently and collaboratively. Excellent written and spoken English is a requirement. Competence in Swedish and other international languages is an advantage.

Experience with qualitative research methods, particularly interviews and case studies, is a requirement. Knowledge of international business, business models, interorganisational collaboration or technology diffusion is meritorious, as is experience related to biogas, renewable energy, waste management or urban infrastructure.

You should be able to engage professionally with companies and other stakeholders, approach unfamiliar contexts with openness and sensitivity, and critically assess evidence from different perspectives. The position involves international travel and fieldwork.

Your application should include a statement of motivation of one page, explaining how your academic background and experience prepare you for this position.

Your workplace

You will join the Division of Environmental Technology and Management at Linköping University and conduct your doctoral research within the Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). The research environment connects sustainability, technology, business development and societal change.

The project involves collaboration with researchers, companies and other organisations engaged in biogas systems. You will contribute to BSRC’s work on internationalisation and develop knowledge relevant to Swedish companies seeking to establish and expand biogas-related business activities abroad.

jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student in Medical Science

Your work assignments

We are seeking a motivated and curious PhD student to join our research team exploring the modulation and pharmacology of proton-activated chloride channels (www.heusserlab.com). These ion channels have recently emerged as promising drug targets for e.g. ischemic stroke, cancer, and viral entry. Our goal is to better understand how the channels function and how small molecules can modulate their activity, ultimately contributing to the development of new therapeutic strategies.

The work includes molecular manipulation and expression of ion channels in different cells, functional characterization of channel activity using electrophysiology and fluorescence-based techniques, and screening of potential modulatory compounds. The project involves collaborations with computational research groups and integrates both manual and automated electrophysiological approaches.

As part of your training, you will develop the project, learn and apply the scientific approaches, and analyze your data. You will communicate your findings in scientific conferences and publications.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in biology, biomedicine, pharmacology or a related field with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses in cell biology or related topics. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

The following education, experience and expertise are required:

  • Experience with molecular biology techniques including mutagenesis, PCR, and DNA/RNA purification
  • Basic knowledge of ion channels or membrane protein biology
  • Ability to plan, organize and document experiments independently
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills

 Priority will be given to candidates who have a strong background knowledge of ligand-gated channels and practical experience in the key experimental approaches:

  • Electrophysiological techniques, such as patch-clamp or two-electrode voltage clamp
  • Expression of ion channels in Xenopus laevis oocytes
  • Knowledge of peptide design, synthesis, or purification
  • Experience with compound screening or drug discovery workflows

Emphasis will also be placed on personal qualities and suitability.

Please include a letter of intent clarifying how you fulfill the above requirements in your application.

Your workplace

Our group is part of the Linköping University Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, the Department of Biomedical and Clinical Sciences (BKV) and the Division of Cell and Neurobiology (CNB), which carries out research, undergraduate and postgraduate education within Medical Science. We are also members of the prestigious Wallenberg Center for Molecular Medicine, which focuses on the interface between science, medicine and technology.

The employment

Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan. 

Starting date upon agreement.

The salary of PhD students is determined according to a locally negotiated salary progression. The starting salary is SEK 33,700 per month (2026 salary level). jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student in Medical Science.

Your work assignments

Treatment resistance is the main cause of relapse in many forms of leukemia and constitutes a significant obstacle to long-term cure. Resistance can be primary, where cells are insensitive to treatment from the time of diagnosis, or acquired, where resistant cell clones are selected during treatment. The biological mechanisms behind treatment resistance are complex and largely still unknown in many forms of leukemia. A deeper understanding of the molecular and cellular processes that drive resistance is therefore crucial for the development of more effective treatment strategies, biomarkers for risk stratification, and individualized therapies that can improve patients' survival and quality of life. To understand how treatment resistance arises and changes over time in different patients and between cell populations, we study this using advanced single-cell genomics and computational biology.

We are looking for a highly motivated person with a passion for driving research development forward. The ideal candidate has a solid background in data analysis, excellent problem-solving skills, and thrives in a collaborative and interdisciplinary environment.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part of. A typical workday might involve writing and running code to process sequencing data on a computer server, applying statistical models and machine learning algorithms, and performing downstream data analysis, including statistics and visualization, as well as writing scientific texts summarizing the results. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20% of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have completed an advanced degree in Medical Biotechnology or completed courses of at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits at advanced level in bioinformatics or mathematical modeling or have otherwise acquired essentially equivalent knowledge.

You must be proficient in both oral and written communication in English and have good teamwork skills.

Documented experience with Unix command-line interface (CLI) and Bash coding as well as skills in another programming language such as Python or R for analysis and visualization of single-cell RNA sequencing is a requirement. Knowledge of statistics, AI/ML, mathematical modeling is highly desirable. Knowledge of AML and treatment resistance as well as single-cell deep learning frameworks such as scVI are desirable.

Personal qualities, such as creativity, curiosity, accuracy and a structured approach to problem solving are essential.

Your workplace

The Department of Biomedical and Clinical Sciences is one of the university’s largest departments, with operations mainly in the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences. Our aim is to engage in medical and biomedical education and research of high international standing. At undergraduate level the department is responsible for most of the medical program, the speech and language pathology program and the biomedical program. For more information about the Department of Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, please follow: https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/bkv

The Department of Cell and Neurobiology (CNB) comprises 100% of the workplace where we conduct research as well as undergraduate and graduate education in bioinformatics. You will also be part of the SciLifeLab & Wallenberg National Program for Data-Driven Life Science (DDLS), a 12-year initiative aimed at recruiting and educating the next generation of data-driven life scientists and creating globally leading capabilities in computational and data science within life sciences in Sweden. Through this program, you will participate in the national DDLS research school and join a dynamic community of doctoral students and postdocs from both academia and industry. You will also have access to extensive training and resources in computational science, including high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. For more information about the DDLS program, see here.

The employment

In connection with your admission to the doctoral program, your employment as a PhD student is handled. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University.

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. 

Starting date by agreement.

The salary of PhD students is determined according to a locally negotiated salary progression. The starting salary is SEK 33,700 per month (2026 salary level). The salary is reviewed annually as part of the regular salary review process and is also adjusted upon completion of 30% and 60% of the PhD studies.

jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student in Environmental Science to conduct qualitative, social science research on sustainable transitions in Swedish agriculture. The research focuses on how different stakeholders understand and communicate about sustainable financing, and how they collaboratively develop solutions in this area.

Your work assignments

Would you like to contribute to developing the financing solutions of the future for sustainable transformations in the agricultural sector? We are looking for a PhD student interested in working with interactive, co-creative and dialogical methods to strengthen the validity of sustainability communication.

As a PhD student, you will join a skilled, open and welcoming research group at Linköping University. Our researchers come from a range of backgrounds—including the social sciences, natural sciences and engineering—and we value diversity in experiences and perspectives. Together, we develop and apply innovative methods for environmental research, often in collaboration with other universities and a range of societal stakeholders.

The VERIFARM project, funded by Formas, is an interdisciplinary research project addressing the financing of and investment in the agricultural sector’s sustainable transformations. The project brings together expertise from the social and natural sciences within the broad field of environmental science, combined with industry knowledge from the banking sector and farmers’ professional expertise.

Your work will include investigating how different stakeholders understand, value and use information about the climate and biodiversity impacts of agriculture in relation to financing and investment. You will plan and conduct empirical studies, for example through interviews, focus groups, workshops and other dialogical and participatory methods. You will also carry out analysis as part of a larger interdisciplinary project team, in collaboration with farmers and representatives from the banking sector. The work will involve both collaborative and independent research.

The specific focus of your doctoral research will be developed within the overarching research questions of the project and in dialogue with the project team. The research questions, empirical material and methodological choices of your thesis will also be partly shaped by the knowledge, expertise and experience that you, as a PhD student, bring to the project. Depending on your background, your research may, for example, focus on sustainability reporting and ESG, financing and investment decisions, dialogue and collaboration between different stakeholders, or how environmental and sustainability information is generated, communicated and used in practice. Across these areas, the common focus is on how knowledge and dialogue can contribute to effective financing solutions for the agricultural sector’s climate transition and the promotion of biodiversity.

You will write scientific articles, present results at conferences, and participate in research education. As a PhD student you work on your thesis in the associated research project. Additional assignments such as teaching or other department tasks may be included up to a maximum of 20% of full time. 

Your qualifications

You have completed a degree at an advanced level, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 higher education credits are at the advanced level, or otherwise acquired substantially equivalent knowledge. You meet the specific entry requirements if you demonstrate knowledge equivalent to 90 higher education credits (ECTS) in a subject of central importance to the field of Environmental Science. Relevant educational backgrounds for the advertised position include environmental science, environmental communication, business administration, or equivalent.

We are looking for someone who is motivated, curious and able to take responsibility for their own work, while also enjoying collaboration. Good command of both Swedish and English, both spoken and written, is required. As the position involves fieldwork, a valid category B driving licence is an advantage.

The following documented qualifications are required:

  • Experience in data collection and analysis using qualitative research methods
  • Knowledge of climate or sustainability transitions
  • Strong scientific writing skills

The following documented qualifications are considered particularly advantageous:

  • Experience with dialogical, co-creative and/or participatory methods, particularly focus groups or workshops, involving multiple types of stakeholders
  • Knowledge of climate and/or sustainability transitions in agriculture
  • Knowledge of biodiversity
  • Knowledge of and/or experience with sustainability reporting, ESG, CSRD, corporate responsibility, or sustainability regulations
  • Knowledge of financing, investment and the banking sector
  • Experience of collaboration between academia and societal stakeholders
  • Strong ability to communicate with people in international environments

Selection will be based on independent study projects or reports, certificates of professional experience, academic grades and interviews. In addition, the applicant should submit a preliminary outline of a potential doctoral research project within the framework described above (maximum 1 page). This outline will also form part of the basis for assessment, and applicants who are invited to an interview will be given the opportunity to further develop it.

Your workplace

Environmental Change carries out research and education on the interaction between environmental and society in an analytically innovative way. The Division offer PhD, Master and Bachelor studies specialising in environmental science, as well as stand-alone courses and teacher-training courses in environment science, thematic natural science and geography.

The employment

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan. 

 

 

Start date is January 2027/as soon as possible, based on agreement.

jobs.description_html:
We are looking for a PhD student in Medical Science, AI and Bioinformatics.

Your work assignments

This project aims to develop AI foundation models for integrative single-cell and multi-omics analysis to better understand how molecular and cellular processes are coordinated across cells, tissues, and organ systems in human health and disease. You will be responsible for developing and applying advanced AI and bioinformatics approaches to large-scale single-cell and multi-omics datasets. The project will focus on integrating these data to investigate cellular and tissue-specific signalling, molecular communication, and systemic molecular networks, and to identify how these processes change across physiological and disease states. Through this work, you will develop predictive and biologically interpretable models that connect molecular patterns across multiple scales of human biology.

The project lies at the interface of artificial intelligence, computational biology, systems medicine, and precision health, and will involve close interaction with researchers from both computational and biomedical disciplines. In addition to the core project, the successful candidate will have opportunities to develop related research questions based on their interests and emerging findings. Through this, you will develop broad expertise in AI and multi-omics analysis and grow as an independent researcher prepared for a future career in academia, biotechnology, or data-driven precision medicine.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications 

You have graduated at Master’s level in AI, Bioinformatics, Systems Biology, or related discipline, or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

In addition, the following are requirements for the role:

  • Strong programming and quantitative skills, particularly in Python and/or R.
  • Experience in deep learning, machine learning, or large-scale omics data analysis.
  • A high level of self-motivation and independence, good problem-solving skills, and the ability to work collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment.
  • The ability to communicate fluently in English, both written and spoken.

The following qualifications are not essential but are considered highly beneficial:

  • Experience with foundation models, transformers, generative models, or representation learning.
  • Experience analysing large-scale single-cell omics data.
  • Experience with integrative multi-omics data, such as genomics, proteomics, or metabolomics.
  • Experience with relevant machine-learning frameworks, such as PyTorch, and high-performance computing (HPC) environments.
  • Knowledge of molecular and cellular biology, systems biology, or precision medicine.

Finally, a letter of intent should be attached to the application describing how your background, skills, and research interests make you a good match for the project on AI foundation models for integrative single-cell and multi-omics analysis. In the same document please also briefly describe a research question or direction within AI, single-cell biology, multi-omics, or systems medicine that you would be interested in exploring during your PhD.

Your workplace

You will be employed in the research group led by Associate Professor Wen Zhong, fellow in the Swedish national program for Data-Driven Life Science (DDLS). The group is located in the Division of Cell and Neurobiology (CNB), at the Department of Biomedical and Clinical Sciences (BKV), Linköping.  

The research group focuses on integrative multi-omics, the interplay between genetic variation and human phenotypes, and the development of AI-driven approaches to better understand human biology and disease and to translate these insights into data-driven strategies for precision health.

jobs.description_html:
We are now looking to appoint a PhD student in Ionic Thermoelectrics and Electrochemistry for Thermal Energy Harvesting, placed at the Department of Science and Technology, Campus Norrköping.

Research area

The present position is part of the European Research Council (ERC) Starting Grant project “High-Efficiency Thermal Energy Harvesting via Ionic Thermoelectric–Electronic Bridging (HEAT-BRIDGE)”, which seeks to establish new routes for efficient conversion of low-grade heat into electricity.

Low-grade heat is abundant in our surroundings—from the human body and electronics to industrial processes—yet remains difficult to harvest efficiently with existing technologies. HEAT-BRIDGE addresses this challenge by bringing together ionic thermoelectrics, electrochemistry, mixed ionic–electronic materials, and soft electronics to explore new approaches to thermal energy conversion. The project spans fundamental materials and transport phenomena, advanced functional materials, and deformable energy-harvesting devices.

The successful candidate will focus on ionic thermoelectric materials and electrochemistry, developing and investigating advanced electrolyte and redox-active material systems for next-generation thermal energy harvesting.

We are announcing two doctoral positions within the HEAT-BRIDGE project, but you may apply for only one of the two positions.

Your work assignments

As a PhD student, you will principally devote yourself to your research studies. Your work will include:

  • Development and characterization of quasi-solid-state ionic thermoelectric materials, including polymer-based gel electrolytes.
  • Investigation of ion–polymer interactions, ionic transport, and thermoelectric properties.
  • Selection and electrochemical characterization of redox-active materials for thermal energy conversion.
  • Integration of developed materials into soft and deformable thermal energy-harvesting devices.
  • Characterization and optimization of the thermoelectric, electrochemical, and energy-conversion performance of materials and devices.
  • Contribution to scalable fabrication of multi-cell devices and their validation using representative low-grade heat sources.
  • Analysis and interpretation of experimental data, publication of results in scientific journals, presentation at international conferences, and collaboration with national and international research partners.

As a PhD student, you devote most of your time to doctoral studies and the research projects of which you are part. Your work may also include teaching or other departmental duties, up to a maximum of 20 per cent of full-time.

Your qualifications

You have graduated at Master’s level in Chemistry, Electrochemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or another field relevant to the project, or completed courses with a minimum of 240 credits, at least 60 of which must be in advanced courses relevant to the position. Alternatively, you have gained essentially corresponding knowledge in another way.

Required qualifications

  • A strong academic background in chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, chemical engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Knowledge of electrochemistry and electrochemical materials or devices.
  • Hands-on experience with experimental materials preparation and/or electrochemical characterization.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in spoken and written English (all research activities at LOE are conducted in English.).

Meritorious research experience

  • Electrolytes, hydrogels, ionogels, eutectogels, or other polymer electrolyte systems.
  • Redox chemistry, batteries, redox-flow batteries, or other electrochemical energy-storage and conversion systems.
  • Ion transport, ion–polymer interactions, or related transport phenomena in soft materials.
  • Electrochemical characterization techniques, such as cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.
  • Ionic thermoelectrics, thermoelectric materials and devices, or thermal energy harvesting.
  • Fabrication and characterization of flexible, soft, or deformable electrochemical devices.

Personal qualities

We are looking for a highly motivated and curious researcher with a strong interest in electrochemistry, ionic transport, and energy conversion. The project explores a new and challenging device concept, and therefore requires creativity, persistence, and strong problem-solving abilities.

The successful candidate should be able to work independently, take initiative, and collaborate effectively with researchers from different scientific backgrounds. Good communication skills and a willingness to explore research questions across traditional disciplinary boundaries are important.

Great emphasis will be placed on personal qualities and suitability.

Your workplace

The PhD student will work under the supervision of Asst. Prof. Nara Kim at the Laboratory of Organic Electronics (LOE), Linköping University.

Nara Kim’s research focuses on mixed ionic–electronic conductors, thermoelectrics, electrochemical energy devices, and wearable electronics, spanning fundamental materials and charge transport to device development and integration. She has secured major competitive research funding, including an ERC Starting Grant, grants from the Swedish Research Council (VR), and the Wallenberg Initiative Materials Science for Sustainability (WISE).

The Laboratory of Organic Electronics (LOE) at Linköping University is a vibrant, international, and collaborative research environment comprising over 170 researchers and doctoral students across 13 research groups. Research at LOE spans materials synthesis and chemistry, theory and modelling, fundamental materials physics, and device development, with applications in energy, printed electronics, photonics, and bioelectronics. A strong common theme is materials for sustainable technologies. LOE provides state-of-the-art facilities for materials synthesis, characterization, device fabrication, cleanroom processing, printing, and additive manufacturing. LOE maintains close collaboration with the Research Institutes of Sweden (RISE) and has extensive national and international collaborations with academia and industry.

For more information, please visit:

  • Nara Kim (Google Scholar)
  • Laboratory of Organic Electronics
  • Linköping University
  • Information about Norrköping
  • A Beginner’s Guide to Swedish Academia (Young Academy of Sweden)

The employment

When taking up the post, you will be admitted to the program for doctoral studies. More information about the doctoral studies at each faculty is available at Doctoral studies at Linköping University

The employment has a duration of normally four years’ full-time equivalent. Extension of employment up to five years is based on the degree of teaching and institutional assignment. Further extensions may be granted in exceptional circumstances. You will initially be employed for one year, after which your employment will be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time, depending on your progress through the study plan. 

Starting date: February-March 2027, or by agreement.

Salary and employment benefits

The salary of PhD students is determined according to a locally negotiated salary progression.

The starting salary for our PhD students is currently SEK 35,300 per month. The salary is revised annually as part of the salary review process conducted each October and is also increased when the PhD student reaches 30% and 60% completion of their doctoral studies.

As an employee of Linköping University, you are entitled to the following benefits:

  • Paid vacation (at least 28 working days per year, depending on age)
  • Paid maternity / paternity leave (up to 390 days per child)
  • Accrued pension. During your work time in Sweden, you accrue income pension, paid by the employer, which is payable also if you leave Sweden

The Department of Statistics at Umeå School of Business, Economics and Statistics (USBE) is recruiting one to two PhD students in Statistics for the research project “Next-Generation Latent Variable Models for Social Data Science”.  Application deadline: November 4, 2026.

We are seeking one to two PhD students for the research project “Next-Generation Latent Variable Models for Social Data Science”, led by PhD Gabriel Wallin. In many social science applications, the characteristics and outcomes of greatest scientific interest are not directly observable. These may include, for example, ability, attitudes, well-being, or different dimensions of poverty, which instead must be estimated from observed data. The overall aim of the project is to develop statistical theory, methodology, and computational methods for such complex data problems, with a particular focus on models for latent variables and their connections to modern machine learning. The project combines methodological research in statistics with applications to large-scale social science data. The successful candidates will have the opportunity to collaborate closely with external partners, including organisations in digital learning and the charity sector. 

The PhD position is fully funded for the duration of four years. PhD students may be appointed to teaching and/ or consulting duties up to 20% of their time, thereby prolonging the duration of the program to guarantee four years of graduate studies. More information about doctoral studies you can find here: www.umu.se/en/usbe/education/doctoral-studies/statistics/, and www.umu.se/en/faculty-of-social-sciences/education/doctoral-studies/.   

The starting date for the position is January 1, 2027, or upon agreement.

Requirements and qualifications 
Applicants should have a degree awarded at the advanced level with a major in Statistics (or equivalent qualifications). Moreover, the student must have satisfactorily undertaken courses in Mathematics equivalent to at least 30 ECTS credits.

The assessments of the applicants are based on their qualifications and their ability to benefit from the doctoral-level education they will receive. The applicant should have a strong quantitative background, for example in statistics, mathematics, computer science, or a related field, very good programming skills, a demonstrated interest in statistical modelling, and a strong motivation to develop statistical methodology for societally relevant questions. A particularly strong merit is demonstrated theoretical and applied knowledge in statistical machine learning, including its implementation.

How to apply
The application should include:

  • A letter of application with a motivation describing your research interests and how they are relevant for this position.
  • A Curriculum Vitae.
  • Form “New PhD” which you can find here: www.hh.umu.se/emp/newPhD.docx
  • Copies of undergraduate and graduate theses.
  • Copies of relevant degree certificates and other documentation you wish to include in support of your application.
  • The names, with contact details and e-mail addresses, of at least two reference persons.

The application is to be submitted on the University recruitment system no later than November, 4, 2026.

Information
In the event that a residence permit is required for your stay in Sweden, the university reserves the right to revoke your admission, if you are not granted a residence permit, or if you cannot present a valid residence permit before the study start date. The latest date for starting studies is September 1, 2027.

For further information please contact PhD Gabriel Wallin, gabriel.wallin@umu.se , or Professor Marie Eriksson (Director of doctoral studies), marie.eriksson@umu.se. 

More about USBE 
As an internationally respected, nationally influential, and regionally rooted part of Umeå University, Umeå School of Business, Economics, and Statistics contributes to societal development through education and research of a high international standard.

In collaboration with our surrounding society, we provide education and research that contributes to individuals' understanding, ability and responsibility in relation to societal challenges and the importance of sustainable development. We are AACSB-accredited and sustainability certified according to the environmental management standard ISO14001.

The Department of Business Administration, the Department of Economics, the Department of Statistics and The USBE office form USBE, with about 150 employees. About 4000 students follow our programs every year and we offer education from the undergraduate to the doctoral program level in all our main disciplines – Business Administration, Economics and Statistics.

The Department of Statistics has about 30 members of staff. We conduct research in the field of statistical sciences, both method development and empirical research, in collaboration with other sciences.

Read more about USBE here: www.umu.se/en/usbe/

Welcome with your application!

The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Information Processing’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026.
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description 

The project will develop ultrafast optical logic and memory concepts using spatiotemporal metamaterials. The doctoral candidate will design metamaterial structures coupled to quantum emitters for ultrafast information processing and investigate how structured ultrashort light pulses can control optical and magnetic properties on femtosecond timescales.

The research will focus on developing sub-10 fs protocols for all-optical logic operations, data processing, and spatiotemporal magnetic memories. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, quantum emitters, ultrafast optics, and light–matter interaction, with the aim of creating new routes for information processing beyond conventional electronic approaches.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 3-month industrial secondment at NKT Photonics in Denmark, focusing on vectorial ultrashort pulses, and a 6-month research secondment at Imperial College London in the United Kingdom, focusing on nanofabrication and characterization.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Professor Riccardo Sapienza at Imperial College London and from an industrial mentor at NKT Photonics. The position provides the opportunity to work in a stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a prestigious European training network.

Competence requirements

To be admitted for studies at third-cycle level, applicants are required to have completed a second-cycle level degree or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits. The recruitment procedure will follow the Higher Education Ordinance (Högskoleförordningen). Applicants should have a Master’s degree, or equivalent, in physics, applied physics, optics/photonics, nanoscience, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. Fluency in English is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, metamaterials, magnetism, or related experimental or theoretical methods is meritorious.

Willingness to work in an inter-cultural, international, and diverse group, and the ability to work independently or as part of a team, are fundamental.

The applicant must meet the MSCA eligibility and mobility requirements: the candidate must not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment and must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment.

Terms of employment

The employment is expected to result in a doctoral degree, and the main assignment for the doctoral student is to take part in research education, including participation in the described research project and relevant courses. Teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20%, may be included. 

The salary follows the established salary level for doctoral students at Umeå University. The position is funded for 36 months through the MSCA Doctoral Network SPARK, with a salary corresponding to at least the MSCA level (approximately 33 100 SEK gross per month), with the possibility of additional MSCA allowances for mobility and accompanying family members. Funding for the remainder of the employment period is provided from other sources. Employment conditions and additional benefits for employees according to applicable regulations.

The employment is limited to four years at full-time or up to five years if teaching and other departmental work is performed. The employment starts in February 2027 or according to agreement.

The application 

The application should contain:

  1. A cover letter with summary of research interests and motivation (max. 1 page)
  2. Curriculum Vitae.
  3. Certified copies of relevant degree certificate(s) translated to English or Swedish.
  4. Transcripts with grades, with English or Swedish translation. Note that for international applicants the grading system should be explained in brief.
  5. Copies of student theses and publications (if any).
  6. Names and contact information of at least one reference person.

You apply via our e-recruitment system Varbi. The deadline for applications is November 30, 2026. Log in and submit your application via the button at the bottom of the page. All application documents must be uploaded in PDF format and should be written in English (preferred) or Swedish.

More information

For further information, contact the Principal Investigator of the project, Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri, nicolo.maccaferri@umu.se.

The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Hybrid Light–Matter States’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026. 
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description

The project will create spatiotemporal polaritons through ultrafast light–matter interactions in engineered metamaterial systems. The doctoral candidate will explore wide-bandgap semiconductors and high-quality excitonic or molecular emitters coupled to time-modulated gratings, with the goal of realizing hybrid light–matter states whose properties can be controlled on femtosecond timescales.

The research will combine ultrafast pump–push–probe experiments with sub-10 fs resolution, finite-element simulations, and quantum models extending the Tavis–Cummings Hamiltonian. The aim is to demonstrate coherent control of spatiotemporal polaritons and to design spatiotemporal metamaterial platforms supporting new forms of hybrid light–matter dynamics. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum optics.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 6-month research secondment at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid in Spain, where theoretical skills will be developed, and a 3-month industrial secondment at Ultrafast Innovations GmbH in Germany.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Associate Professor Paloma Arroyo Huidobro at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid and from an industrial mentor at Ultrafast Innovations GmbH. The position provides the opportunity to work in a stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a prestigious European training network.

Competence requirements

To fulfil the general entry requirements, the applicant must have qualifications equivalent to a completed degree at advanced level (second-cycle), or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits including at least 60 ECTS credits at advanced level. To fulfil the specific entry requirements to be admitted to doctoral studies in experimental physics, the applicant is required to have completed courses within the field of physics comprising at least 120 credits. 

Applicants should have a Master’s degree, or equivalent, in physics, applied physics, optics/photonics, materials science, nanoscience, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. 

English fluency, both written and spoken, is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, exciton–polaritons, light–matter interaction, numerical simulations, or quantum modelling is meritorious.

Willingness to work in an inter-cultural, international, and diverse group, and the ability to work independently or as part of a team, are fundamental.

The applicant must meet the MSCA eligibility and mobility requirements: the candidate must not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment and must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment.

Terms of employment

The employment is expected to result in a doctoral degree, and the main assignment for the doctoral student is to take part in research education, including participation in the described research project and relevant courses. Teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20%, may be included. 

The salary follows the established salary level for doctoral students at Umeå University. The position is funded for 36 months through the MSCA Doctoral Network SPARK, with a salary corresponding to at least the MSCA level (approximately 33 100 SEK gross per month), with the possibility of additional MSCA allowances for mobility and accompanying family members. Funding for the remainder of the employment period is provided from other sources. Employment conditions and additional benefits for employees according to applicable regulations. 

The employment is limited to four years at full-time or up to five years if teaching and other departmental work is performed. The employment starts in February 2027 or according to agreement.

The application 

The application should contain:

  1. A cover letter with a summary of research interests and motivation (max. 1 page)
  2. Curriculum Vitae.
  3. Certified copies of relevant degree certificate(s) translated to English or Swedish.
  4. Transcripts with grades, with English or Swedish translation. Note that for international applicants the grading system should be explained in brief.
  5. Copies of student theses and publications (if any).
  6. Names and contact information of at least one reference person.

You apply via our e-recruitment system Varbi.
The deadline for applications is November 30, 2026. 

Log in and submit your application via the button at the bottom of the page. All application documents must be uploaded in PDF format and should be written in English (preferred) or Swedish.

More information

For further information, contact the Principal Investigator of the project, Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri, nicolo.maccaferri@umu.se.

We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.title: Doctoral researcher in Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets (MSCA Doctoral Network)
jobs.description_html:
We are recruiting one doctoral researcher (3 years) to the AEGIS network


AEGIS — Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets — is a European research and training network. It is funded by the EU through a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network, runs from 2026 to 2030, and trains 15 Doctoral Candidates (PhD students). The DN targets developing software-defined technologies that turn edge data centers from passive electrical loads into active, carbon-efficient and grid-interactive resources. The project has three layers:

  • A programmable infrastructure layer gives safe, runtime-verified control of a site’s power electronics, cooling, and AI hardware.
  • An intelligence layer reads real-time grid signals and turns a request such as “reduce power by 20%” into the detailed actions that hardware and facilities must take, without breaking service.
  • A fleet orchestration layer coordinates many sites, even when they have different owners, using trusted and privacy-preserving methods, so the whole fleet can act as one Virtual Power Plant.

Read more about the project and other participants here: https://aegis-dn.eu/

 

Your role:

You will be working on “End-to-End Energy Modeling for Distributed AI Services”. To make carbon-aware decisions, both orchestrators and developers need to see the real energy cost of an AI workload. In this project you build analytical models and systems that make energy and carbon metrics visible. You will create compositional energy models that span the radio network, the transport network, and the datacenter hardware, and expose them through a fast query interface so any tool can ask, “what does this AI service cost in energy?”


You will be responsible for:

  • Developing compositional energy models for disaggregated radio (RAN) components, transport networks, and datacenter hardware.
  • Building a low-latency query API that returns the end-to-end energy cost of an AI service.

What you will deliver:

  • Validated models with less than 10% prediction error on the Aalto and Ericsson testbeds.
  • A query API that returns end-to-end energy-cost estimates in under 100 milliseconds.
  • A doctoral dissertation that you will defend.

Secondments:

You will spend two research visits with partners in the network:

  • Ericsson (Finland) — 3 months from around May 2028 (industry), with Tomas Mecklin: test the energy models on Ericsson’s infrastructure testbeds.
  • TU Wien (Vienna, Austria) — 3 months from around May 2029 (academic), with Ivona Brandić: combine the digital-twin models with the end-to-end energy models.

The position requires:

  • Master's degree in computer science, communications engineering, telecommunications, or a related field (with a CGPA of at least 4/5)
  • Experience (e.g. coursework, projects, etc.) in AI and machine learning, including understanding of various DNN architectures, training models, and applying them for different tasks
  • Understanding of computer and telecom networks (for example RAN)
  • Experience with empirical measurements (Prior work on energy or power measurement is strongly preferred)
  • Data analysis and analytical modeling — identifying the features that drive system behaviour and building compositional or analytical models from measured data (an interest or aptitude here is enough; we don’t expect prior demonstrated experience)
  • Good programming skills – you are required to provide a sample of your code during the recruitment process
  • Fluency in written and spoken English. See https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering#8-required-language-proficiency for information on how you can demonstrate proficiency in English. This is required when officially applying for doctoral studies at the School of Electrical Engineering in Aalto University (within 6 months after starting in the job). Please note that you do not need official proof when applying for this job.

If you are chosen for this position, you will apply for the study right in doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering. Thus, please see the student information and admission criteria at https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering.


MSCA eligibility

You must meet the following requirements:

  • No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment, you must not yet hold a PhD.
  • Mobility rule. You must not have lived or done your main activity (work or studies) in Finland for more than 12 months in the 36 months just before you are recruited, unless as part of a compulsory national service or a procedure for obtaining EU temporary protection or refugee status under the Geneva Convention. Short stays such as holidays do not count.
  • All nationalities welcome. The positions are open to applicants of any nationality.

What we offer:

You will become a part of the Cloud and Network Computing group, headed by assistant professor Gopika Premsankar. You will be advised by Riku Jäntti, full professor in Communications Engineering. Both groups are based in the Department of Information and Communications Engineering in the School of Electrical Engineering.


The position starts in March 2027 or as mutually agreed. The start date cannot be later than June 2027. The employment contract will be made for three years.


Application documents

To apply, please share the following application materials (as PDFs) with us through our recruitment site ("Apply now!” at the bottom of the page):

  • A CV
  • A short letter of motivation, at most 1 page, which describes your interest and motivation (please try to include details that are not part of your CV and emphasize how you address the position-specific requirements listed above)
  • Sample code, preferably on a code repository (Provide a URL and describe in one paragraph your role in developing the software)
  • Names and email addresses of two reference providers. They will be contacted directly at a later stage in the application process.
  • Transcript of grades for your Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees

Please note that our recruitment system allows maximum of 5 attachments, so please combine e.g. the copies of transcripts in one PDF, if necessary.


Application process

The application deadline is December 15, 2026 23.59pm (EET). We will go through the applications in batches, and we may invite suitable candidates to interview already during the application period. The call will be closed early, if the position is filled before the application deadline.


Please note: Aalto University’s employees should apply for the position via our internal HR system Workday (Internal Jobs) by using their existing Workday user account (not via the external webpage for open positions).


More information

For more information about the position, please contact Professor Gopika Premsankar (gopika.premsankar@aalto.fi).  For questions about the application process, please contact HR Advisor Johanna Haapalainen at hr-elec@aalto.fi.


Why Finland and why this group

Aalto University provides a vibrant and collaborative environment. We work in a hybrid way, and the primary workplace is Otaniemi, Espoo. The Otaniemi campus is a thriving and connected community of 100 nationalities, 16,000 students and 5,200 employees. Life at the campus is vibrant and filled with amazing architecture, calming nature, and a variety of cafes, restaurants, services and good transport connections.


Finland is a great place for living – it is a safe, politically stable and well-organized Nordic society. Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. The School of Chemical Engineering is one of the six schools of Aalto University. It combines natural sciences and engineering in a unique way.

 

We are now looking for a

 

DOCTORAL RESEARCHER IN CHEMICAL ENGINEERING


for a funded position in an industrial collaboration project together with Neste Oyj, related to development of dynamic trickle bed reactor models. The project duration is four years, during which you are expected to finalize your PhD degree.

 

Your role and goals

Trickle bed reactors are in a central position in many refinery operations, both in traditional oil refining as well as treatment of novel bio-based feedstocks. Trickle bed operations have been studied from many angles, including fluid flow models, chemical kinetics, and mass transfer. Despite these, there is still a need for dynamic models of trickle bed reactors with both industrial and scientific importance. Your task would be to develop such models based on literature, in collaboration with an industrial partner. You should:


  • Collect and critically analyze relevant literature
  • Build and analyze models for predicting dynamic trickle bed reactor operations, including material and energy balances, reaction kinetics, mass and heat transfer, phase equilibria, fluid flow, and process control and operation
  • Collaborate with other members of the research group and external partners to achieve project goals
  • Present research findings at conferences and publish results in peer-reviewed journals

 

Your network and team

You will be working in the Chemical Engineering research group lead by professor Ville Alopaeus. Chemical Engineering research group is part of Department of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering in the School of Chemical Engineering at Aalto University. Currently the research group consists of around 15 researchers in various roles related to research and teaching.

 

Your experience and ambitions

We are looking for motivated and research-oriented candidates with curious engineering mindset, good communication and collaboration skills and good understanding about mechanistic process modeling principles, phase equilibria, reaction engineering, heat and mass transfer, and fluid dynamics. A Master’s degree in Chemical Engineering, or related field is required.


Applicants must fulfill the eligibility and admission criteria for Aalto Doctoral Programme in Chemical Engineering. Doctoral studies at Aalto University take approximately four years. You can find more information about Aalto’s doctoral program and its requirements here: https://www.aalto.fi/en/programmes/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-chemical-engineering

 

What we offer

After a successful evaluation by the end of the first 2 year contract, the contract will be extended. Extension contract is typically based on the progress evaluation, revised project plan and available funding.


The starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is about 3140 €/month (gross). The contract includes Aalto University occupational healthcare benefits.

Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 13 000 students, 400 professors and close to 4 500 other faculty and staff working on our dynamic campus in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.

 

The School of Engineering drives science and innovation in industrial and built environment technologies. We are committed to educating a new generation of experts who combine technical excellence with a deep understanding of sustainable development in shaping societies. Our research focuses on sustainable built environment, mechanics and materials, multidisciplinary energy technology, and design and implementation of technical systems. The strength of our school lies in close collaboration with stakeholders across research and education. About 45 doctoral candidates and 350 master’s students graduate from the school every year. The school is home to 700 staff members, including 70 professors. To learn more, please visit eng.aalto.fi.

 

 

Real Estate Research Group at Aalto University School of Engineering, Department of Built Environment invites applications for

 

Doctoral Researcher in Real Estate Economics

 

We are seeking an excellent doctoral researcher to join the Real Estate Research Group. The position is rooted in strategic asset management and sustainable transition, primary from the perspective of real estate owner, investor and service provider.

 

In this position, the doctoral researcher will develop profitable transition pathways to extend the technical, functional, and financial lifespans of residential buildings and portfolios. The work includes analysing building-level technical transition costs and developing new business, financing, and implementation models, such as servitisation, crowdfunding, assets digitalization and other instruments.

 

The doctoral researcher will work on a project called UP-STOCK (Formulating Just Transition Paths for the Housing Stock). UP-STOCK is a co-research initiative financed by Kone Oyj, Avain Yhtiöt Oy, Helsingin kaupungin asunnot Oy, Haahtela Oy, OP Kiinteistösijoitus Oy, kaukora Oy, Business Finland, and Aalto university.

 

The project offers collaboration opportunities with key industry stakeholders, and the research community with our international partner universities. The Real Estate Research Group has around twenty researchers (doctoral researchers and postdocs) from all fields of Real Estate, including Economic Law, Land Management, Sustainable Real Estate Business, Real Estate Economics and Valuation, and Real Estate Management.

 

Your role and goals

  • Conduct doctoral research in strategic asset management and sustainable transition; publishing and communicating findings (e.g., reports, articles, conference presentations); and completing 30 ECTS of doctoral coursework
  • Close collaboration and co-development with the UP-STOCK project partners and stakeholders
  • Teaching and/or assisting in Real Estate courses (10% of work time)
  • Participating in applying research funding

 

Your experience and ambitions

  • Master’s degree in a relevant field such as real estate economics, construction economics, business administration and management, building technology, quantity surveying or property management with excellent study success.
  • Excellent collaboration skills for working with company and university partners; willingness to visit and work on the campus of the university partner as needed.
  • Excellent writing and presentation skills in English. Skills in Finnish are seen as an asset.

Aalto University is a community of bold thinkers where science and art meet technology and business. We are committed to identifying and solving grand societal challenges and building an innovative future. Aalto has six schools with 14 000 students and a staff of 5000, of which more than 400 are professors. Our main campus is located in Espoo, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.


The Department of Computer Science is an internationally-oriented community and home to world-class research in modern computer science, combining research on foundations and innovative applications. With over 40 professors and more than 450 employees from 50 countries, it is the largest department at Aalto University and the leading computer science research unit in northern Europe. Computer science research at Aalto University ranks high in several international surveys (7th in Europe and 1st in the Nordics (NTU 2023); and 88th worldwide in Times Higher Education subject ranking 2025).


We are now looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Trustworthy Machine Learning

 

Your role and goals

Trustworthy & Adversarial Computing Lab (https://taclab.aalto.fi) led by Sebastian Szyller is looking for a doctoral researcher (PhD student) to pursue a degree in trustworthy machine learning.


As a doctoral researcher your goal is to conduct research in the fast-paced field of trustworthy machine learning. You are expected to:

1) Carry out state-of-the-art research.

2) Prepare and publish manuscripts at leading conferences and journals.

3) Present your work at academic and industry events.

4) Collaborate with other researchers (locally and internationally).


Focus

The position is focused on provenance and integrity of machine learning models and pipelines. You will tackle topics related to:

1) Verifiable, provable and auditable machine learning (e.g. adversarial robustness, privacy, fairness).

2) AI/MLBOM and related topics.

3) Proof carrying in ML.


In addition to research work, the hired is expected to participate in teaching following the standard practices at the department.


Your experience and ambitions

The position requires excellent programming skills in Python with demonstrable familiarity with PyTorch, experience in working on shared codebases, excellent applied math skills (especially probability theory, matrix algebra, calculus). Beyond technical experience, candidates are expected to have strong teamwork and collaboration skills, as well as competency in critical and independent thinking.


You’re a good fit if:

1) you have experience in machine learning and would like to explore the security/privacy angle, or

2) you have a security/privacy background and would like to apply it to machine learning, or

3) you have experience in explainable/interpretable/fair machine learning, and/or software supply chains.

Outstanding applicants have prior experience in trustworthy machine learning, and/or publication record in machine learning or security/privacy, software supply chains.


What we offer

We offer a fully funded position (2 + 2 model) under the supervision of Sebastian Szyller. Trustworthy & Adversarial Computing Lab is a newly established group. The lab has an extensive network consisting of companies and academic institutions in Europe and across the world.
