jobs.title: PhD Project in Real-Time Visual Computing and AI
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Computer Science invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in Real-Time Visual Computing and AI (REVCAI).

REVCAI investigates how advances in visual computing and artificial intelligence can be translated into systems that are not only accurate, but also fast, efficient, scalable, responsive, and practical to deploy. Modern AI systems have made remarkable progress in understanding and generating visual information, but their computational requirements, latency, limited adaptability, and dependence on large-scale computing infrastructure remain major obstacles to their use in interactive and real-world settings.

The project will develop new algorithms and computational methods at the intersection of computer graphics, computer vision, machine learning, geometry, and high-performance computing. Particular emphasis will be placed on representations and algorithms that make sophisticated visual intelligence possible under practical computational constraints.

The expected start date is March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

The project

The PhD project will investigate fundamental problems in real-time and resource-efficient visual computing and AI. The precise research direction will be developed together with the successful candidate and may build on their particular strengths and interests.

Potential research directions include real-time 3D reconstruction and representation, neural and point-based representations, efficient rendering and visualisation, high-performance computer vision, efficient machine learning, dynamic and multimodal scene understanding, geometric and physical reasoning, and visual perception for interactive or embodied systems.

A central theme of the project is that computational efficiency is not merely an implementation detail. Latency, memory consumption, scalability, and computational cost can fundamentally determine whether an algorithm can be used in an interactive system, on resource-constrained hardware, or as part of a larger perception-and-action loop. The project will therefore investigate algorithmic and representational choices that improve computational performance while retaining — or improving — accuracy, robustness, and generalisation.

The project may address questions such as:

  • How can complex visual and multimodal information be represented and processed at interactive or real-time rates?
  • How can modern visual AI methods be made substantially more computationally efficient and scalable?
  • Which representations best combine appearance, geometry, semantics, dynamics, and physical information?
  • How can visual representations be designed not only for reconstruction or prediction, but also for interaction and decision-making?
  • How should visual computing systems be evaluated when latency, memory, computational resources, robustness, and adaptability matter alongside conventional accuracy measures?

Depending on the research direction, the work may range from low-level GPU and systems optimisation to the design of new representations, learning algorithms, or complete real-time visual computing systems. Applications may include robotics and autonomous systems, interactive 3D applications, augmented and virtual reality, scientific and biomedical imaging, and other domains in which visual information must be processed efficiently and reliably.

The successful candidate will be expected to develop novel methods, implement and experimentally evaluate them, and compare them against relevant state-of-the-art approaches. We are particularly interested in research that combines strong algorithmic ideas with convincing practical demonstrations and careful empirical evaluation.

 

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates within the fields of Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or related areas.

Applicants should have strong technical and analytical skills and an interest in developing high-performance algorithms for visual computing and artificial intelligence. Experience in one or more of the following areas is advantageous:

  • computer graphics or computer vision,
  • machine learning,
  • 3D reconstruction or representation,
  • GPU programming or high-performance computing,

  • geometry processing,

Strong programming skills are important. Experience with Python and/or C++ and modern machine-learning or GPU-computing frameworks is particularly relevant.

We do not expect candidates to already be experts in all of these areas. We particularly value curiosity, strong problem-solving ability, mathematical and algorithmic thinking, and an interest in understanding how methods work rather than treating existing models as black boxes.

 

What do we offer?

The project is supervised by Assistant Professor Bernhard Kerbl at the Department of Computer Science, University of Copenhagen.

The candidate will join the IMAGE section at the University of Copenhagen, an active research environment working across computer graphics, computer vision, image analysis, geometry, computational modelling, and artificial intelligence.

The project will provide substantial freedom to develop an independent research profile within the broader REVCAI agenda. The candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with researchers at the University of Copenhagen and with national and international research partners, and to contribute both to scientific publications and to open-source research software.

IMAGE offers a friendly, collaborative, and informal research environment with close interaction between faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and PhD students. We value curiosity, technical depth, openness, and teamwork, and aim to provide a supportive environment in which PhD students can develop into independent researchers.

jobs.description_html:
PhD Project in Cultural Reasoning with Language Models

The AI Section at the Department of Computer Science invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational modelling and evaluation of cultural interpretation with language models. The position is part of the research project “CuRe: Cultural Reasoning for Responsible Language Model Development” (DFF project 5334-00088B), funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark.

The expected start date is February 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

The project

Language models can produce fluent interpretations of texts while obscuring the cultural assumptions, uncertainty and alternative readings underlying their answers. CuRe investigates how language models understand and reason about culture, ambiguity and interpretation, and how these capabilities can be evaluated and improved to support responsible language model development. Literary texts provide a demanding testbed: their interpretation depends on historical and cultural knowledge, close attention to textual evidence and the ability to accommodate several plausible readings.

The PhD candidate will develop computational methods and evaluation resources for culturally grounded interpretation. Working closely with researchers in natural language processing and literary studies, the candidate is expected to:

  • construct datasets and benchmarks linking literary passages, relevant cultural and historical context, textual evidence and expert or reader interpretations;
  • analyse what cultural knowledge and interpretive strategies language models use, where their interpretations fail and how confidently they present uncertain conclusions;
  • develop methods for grounding interpretations in evidence and for representing uncertainty, ambiguity and multiple plausible interpretations;
  • evaluate the resulting methods through automatic experiments and studies with literary scholars and other readers; and
  • publish the results in leading venues in natural language processing, artificial intelligence and computational humanities.

The exact research questions will be refined together with the successful candidate. Relevant methodological directions include language model evaluation and probing, retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation, explicit representations of interpretive evidence and uncertainty, data annotation, human-centred evaluation and multilingual or cross-cultural analysis. The empirical work will primarily use modern Scandinavian literary texts, while aiming to develop methods and findings that generalise beyond literature. The project includes a planned research stay at McGill University.

 

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates with a strong computational background and an interest in how language, culture and interpretation can be studied rigorously. Applicants may have a background in natural language processing, computational linguistics, computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, data science, digital humanities or a closely related field. Formal training in literary studies is not required, but the successful candidate must be motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries and to engage seriously with humanities research questions.

 

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

The PhD fellow will join the CoAStaL research group and the AI Section at the Department of Computer Science. The research environment brings together faculty, postdoctoral researchers and PhD students working on multilingual and cross-cultural NLP, multimodality, language model training and evaluation, responsible AI and computational humanities. The section collaborates broadly with leading research groups in Denmark and abroad.

CuRe is an interdisciplinary collaboration with the Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics at the University of Copenhagen. The project builds on established joint work in computational literary studies and provides access to large literary corpora, domain expertise and relevant annotation resources. The PhD fellow will therefore be part of both a technically strong NLP environment and a close collaboration with literary scholars.

The group is part of the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern GPU computing resources, shared data and annotation infrastructure and access to relevant text corpora.

jobs.description_html:
Applications are invited for a PhD scholarship at the Department of Psychology.

The starting date is March 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Introduction
The PhD-student will be part of a project entitled Exploring the bases of individual differences in face recognition funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (IRFD). The project is headed by Professor Randi Starrfelt and is a collaboration with Professor in Psychology and Epidemiology, Karen-Inge Karstoft and Professor in Cognitive Neuropsychiatry, Birgitte Fagerlund from Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

The overall project investigates variability in face recognition across a large, representative sample of the Danish population, with the aim of relating this to variability in other measures of cognition through questionnaires and data from Danish public registries. The focus of the PhD-project will be on relating variability in face recognition to other measures and indicators of cognitive abilities. Applicants are asked to situate and develop their research plan within the framework of the overall project, and the original project proposal should be requested from Professor Randi Starrfelt, randi.starrfelt@psy.ku.dk prior to submitting the application.

Candidates with various background may be considered for the position, examples of relevant backgrounds are MA/MSc degrees in experimental, cognitive, or developmental psychology, neuropsychology, cognitive (neuro)science, medicine (psychiatry), or public health. Strong skills in data handling and analysis is an advantage, as is an interest in the research questions posed in the overall project. Experience with research using data from Danish public registries will be an advantage but is not a requirement. The PhD student will be working in close collaboration with psychologists from different disciplines including psychological epidemiology and cognitive neuropsychology/neuropsychiatry. The position will be placed at Copenhagen Neuropsychology Lab, part of the Section for Cognition and Neuropsychology. It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and partake in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.

The PhD programme provides PhD students with strong research training which opens a window of opportunity to a variety of careers within the private and public sectors. The programme includes the preparation of a PhD thesis, active participation in research networks, PhD courses, teaching, and other forms of knowledge dissemination. This funded PhD-position is to be undertaken as a three-year full-time study within the framework of the 5+3 study programme. 

Duties and responsibilities
Information about the PhD study programme is available on the website of Copenhagen Graduate School of Social Sciences PhD at the Faculty of Social Sciences and on the PhD website of the department.

Qualification requirements
Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to master’s level related to the subject area of the project, e.g. MSc in psychology, public health, medicine, or cognitive neuroscience. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we will obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency.

Scholarship in the 5+3 programme
The 5+3 PhD study programme 
PhD students are paid a salary in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The PhD student has a work obligation of up to 840 hours over the 3-year period of time without additional pay. The work obligation can include teaching, for instance.

Please note assessment of applicants’ qualifications and eligibility for employment and enrolment will only take place after the application deadline.

How to apply
Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. Your application must be written in English, and include the following attachments (with descriptive titles) in either PDF or Word format:

  • Cover letter (max. 1 page detailing your motivation and background for applying with the specific PhD project)
  • CV
  • Project description of max 3 pages / 6000 characters excluding references presenting and discussing the challenges and advantages of using selected variables from the Danish Public registries as indexes for cognitive ability and cognitive disorders (cf. Work Package 2 and 3 in project proposal for IRFD that should be requested from randi.starrfelt@psy.ku.dk. The description should also include a suggestion for how to select relevant variables and ideas for which analyses might be helpful in analysing their relationship to the face recognition data collected in the project.
  • Diploma and transcripts of records (BSc and MSc) Please note: If your degree diploma is not available by the application deadline, please include your latest transcript of grades.
  • Other information for consideration, e.g., list of publications, documentation of English language qualifications (if any). Please do not include commitments from supervisors, recommendations etc.

Further details on the documents that should accompany your application are available on this website: Admission requirements and application procedures.

Assessment Criteria
The following criteria are used when shortlisting candidates for assessment: 

1. Research qualifications as reflected in the cover letter, CV and project proposal. 

2. MSc from a relevant field, e.g. psychology, public health, medicine, or cognitive (neuro)science.

3. Interest in cognition and variability in cognitive ability.

4. Performance (grades obtained) in graduate and post-graduate studies. 

Salary and Terms of Employment
Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range starts at approximately DKK 31.844,98 (EUR 4.260,48) + an 18.07 % pension contribution.

The Recruitment Process 
After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and then selects applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will then set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

Enrolment
It is a prerequisite for employment that successful applicants enrol at the PhD School of the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

International Applicant?
The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.

An Equal Opportunity Workplace
The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc.To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.

Structure of the PhD programme

How to obtain a PhD scholarship.

jobs.description_html:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
 

The position

This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

 

Project description

The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

 

Description of the scientific environment

The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

 

Who are we looking for?

  • Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field.
  • Good written and oral English skills are a requirement.
  • Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged
  • Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities

The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.

jobs.title: PhD position in Geoscience Education Research
jobs.description_html:
Novo Nordisk Foundation Centre for University Science Education (NNF-USE).

The Department of Science Education invites applications for a three-year PhD position in geoscience education research, commencing on April 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position is part of the research work package “Disciplinary Writing Practices in the AI Era: Enhancing Learning in the Geosciences” at NNF-USE, led by Professor Kristine Harper. The PhD will be part of the research group on University Science Education, which hosts several other scholars working on higher education discipline-based educational research (DBER). NNF-USE, led by Professor Jenny Dauer, also partners with scholars from two other Danish universities (University of Aarhus, University of Southern Denmark) as well as those from abroad.
 

Project Description

Writing is key to disciplinary learning, development and knowledge production. The role of writing in disciplines, however, remains understudied and underutilized in university science education. Particularly in Geoscience Education Research (GER), disciplinary writing often serves merely as an assessment tool, rather than a vehicle for learning. As emerging GenAI technologies fundamentally disrupt writing practices, there is an urgent need to understand the role of writing in disciplinary learning and examine how extant and emerging GenAI technologies interact with disciplinary teaching practices, writing norms, and student learning. This work package examines the role of disciplinary writing in teaching and learning within geology. It explores how writing serves as a learning tool for both acquiring scientific knowledge and developing disciplinary ways of thinking and being in the world as a geologist – examining how students’ writing practices change and how perceptions of authorship, expertise, and disciplinary norms are evolving in the AI era. The aim is to generate knowledge about how writing can be better integrated in teaching and learning at different levels of university geology education and practice, harnessing the potentials of AI tools without undermining core educational goals.

We seek a candidate for an exciting research project focused on scientific writing’s connection to learning in all levels of university geoscience education. The project aims to explore how university students and faculty members currently experience disciplinary writing in relation to their studies and teaching, respectively, how that is changing or might change as large-language models become more sophisticated over time, and what those changes mean or could mean for professional disciplinary development. The project could be designed to provide insights into how faculty members currently do or do not use writing as a teaching and learning tools in their instruction, how it might be better incorporated into teaching, and the outcomes for both teachers’ perceptions of the effectiveness of including disciplinary writing in their teaching and student outcomes.

There will be considerable room to shape and adapt this PhD project to the academic background and interests of the PhD candidate. The project can include a range of methodologies, including, but not limited to, literature reviews, surveys, classroom observations, interviews with faculty and student focus groups, teaching experiments and testing of implementation strategies in the classroom. The PhD project should be relevant to university geoscience education in a Danish context. The final project design will be determined in consultation with the supervisors after the appointment.

 

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate with a strong background in a geoscience (e.g., geology, meteorology, oceanography, physical geography) and interest in geoscience education and its roles in undergraduate and graduate instruction.

In particular, we are looking for the following competencies and experience.

It is required that applicants:

  • Hold a master’s degree by 1 April 2027 (see specifications below) in an appropriate geoscience discipline (see above) or in geoscience education, with a bachelor’s degree in an appropriate geoscience discipline.
  • Are comfortable working in research groups and are interested in collaborative work.
  • Are very interested in pursuing geoscience education research.
  • Have excellent written and oral English skills.

It is advantageous if applicants:

  • Have expertise in geology, since that will be the focus for the undergraduate education part of the project.
  • Have experience and/or training in qualitative research methods.
  • Have Danish language skills or are willing to adapt to an environment where Danish is often used.

 

About the Department of Science Education

The Department of Science Education aims to open up science and mathematics for all through research that enhances education, communication, and public engagement. The Department brings together expertise from the sciences, social sciences, and humanities to lead internationally in science and mathematics education, digital education, history and philosophy of science, and science communication.

The Department currently employs approx. 100 persons – many of whom are international. We offer a vibrant interdisciplinary research environment and an attractive and friendly work environment for all employees, and we are determined to support PhD students, postdocs, and assistant professors in building of a foundation for their future career within and outside academia. It is a hallmark of our research to unite strong fundamental and applied research, with high impact in society.

A large part of the Department’s teaching activities concerns the mandatory university pedagogical training and competence development for teaching faculty at the Faculties of Science and Health.

You may read the Department’s strategy towards 2030 and you may read about the USE Center here: https://use.ku.dk/. You may read more about the department in general here: https://www.ind.ku.dk/english/

Copenhagen is one of the 10 most livable cities in the world with a rich culture within music, theater and associations (https://www.visitcopenhagen.com). Life for families is made easier by a publicly supported daycare and health care system, dual career opportunities, maternity/parental leave and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark at https://workindenmark.dk/. Useful information is also available at the International Staff Mobility (ISM) office at the University of Copenhagen (https://ism.ku.dk/). ISM offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

 

The PhD programme 

Qualifications needed
To be eligible for the PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g., in a geoscience or in geoscience education. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 

Terms of employment
Employment as a PhD fellow is full time and for a maximum 3 years. 

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant. 

The terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. 

Responsibilities and tasks

  • Carry through an independent research project under supervision at the host institution
  • Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE
  • Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad
  • Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities (corresponding to approx. 1/2 FTE)
  • Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals
  • Write and defend a PhD thesis based on your project

 

Your supervisor will be:

Professor Kristine Cecile Harper, Department of Science Education, University of Copenhagen, kch@ind.ku.dk, +45 3533 0710.

 

Application and Assessment Procedure

Applications should include a PhD project proposal with clear and relevant research questions that link to the proposed research design and methodology. In the evaluation of the application, emphasis is placed on the relevance of the research question to the research project within which it will be rooted as well as the originality of the project and the suggested research design and methodology. Further criteria are:

  • The project´s ability to relate the proposal to existing geoscience education research
  • The project’s plan to make the project relevant to geoscience education research and for knowledge transfer through education, dissemination, or development activities.
  • The PhD candidate’s reflections on ethical aspects specifically related to the proposed project.

 

Your application including all attachments must submitted electronically by clicking Apply for position below.

Applications must be made in English.

Please include: 

  1. Letter of application, including your motivation for applying for the specific PhD project.
  2. Proposal for a PhD project related to the research area described above. The proposal may not exceed six-pages in length. 
  3. Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position
  4. Original diplomas for completed Bachelors and Masters education and transcripts of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.
  5. Publication list (if possible).

 

Application deadline: November 29, 2026 23:59 GMT +1

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline and not to consider applications that do not meet the above-mentioned requirements.

 

The further process
After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessment committee. You will be notified whether you qualify to proceed beyond the assessment stage.

The assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessment committee will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in January 2027.

 

Questions
For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor, Kristine Cecile Harper, kch@ind.ku.dk.

General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

jobs.description_html:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), invites applications for a fully funded 3-year PhD-position from 1 May 2027 or after agreement.  

The position and the project
The successful candidate will work on the project Treatments for Complex PTSD (RECONNECT-trial), a randomized controlled trial conducted in the Mental Health Services. The project has a strong focus on patient involvement and investigating mechanisms of change within the three intervention arms (Prolonged Exposure, Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing and Enhanced Emotional and Interpersonal Skills Training). The project is conducted in collaboration between researchers in psychology and psychiatry.

Duties and responsibilities
The PhD student will be central in the research project, being involved in and responsible for large parts of the data collection. Most importantly, the PhD-student will be responsible for conceptualizing and conducting a subset of studies. As such, data management and data analyses, as well as manuscript preparation and communication of research results to the scientific community as well as to relevant stakeholders will be central.

The PhD-student will be responsible for the assessment of the participants with the International Trauma Interview in Danish, overseeing recruitment progress, and conducting quantitative and qualitative research based on survey and interview data. Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis is a must. The candidate must have strong clinical skills and preferably with trauma populations. The candidate must be able to work independently under supervision. Collaborative skills and team spirit are in high regard. For the right candidate, there will be ample possibilities to influence the project and develop new project ideas within the project frame.

Supervision and research group

jobs.title: PhD fellowship(s) in Human-computer Interaction
jobs.description_html:
The Section on Human-Centred Computing invites applicants for one or two PhD fellowships in Human-Computer Interaction. The fellowships are part of the Villum Investigator project TRACTION: Theoretical Research in Human-computer Interaction, awarded to Kasper Hornbæk. The goal of the fellowships is to understand and advance the use of theory in all its forms in the evaluation and design of interactive systems. The start date is April 1 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

The project

The field of Human-Computer Interaction seeks to make computer systems in all forms useful and usable for end users. For the past 40 years, this has been done by creating methods for involving users in the design and evaluation of systems. However, we have all experienced computer systems that are frustrating, help solve the wrong tasks, or cause additional work. The field also struggles to make emerging technologies, such as AI, extended reality, and social media, benefit end users rather than deskill or distract them. The idea of this project is that the field lacks theories that can help us understand and predict when and why computer systems are useful and usable.

In the TRACTION center, we will focus on developing and applying theory about Human-Computer Interaction. We will depart from empirical studies of the difficulties of using existing theories. At the same time, we will develop theories about key problems in the field, such as what makes computer systems valuable to end users and how computers and humans influence each other in interaction. Finally, we will explore systematic approaches to using theory for understanding and predicting phenomena in interactive computing. The intended impact of the center is to shift Human-Computer Interaction from a craft of using methods for evaluation and design to a science of theories, cumulation, and generalization across technologies, users, and contexts of use.

 

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates within the field of Human-computer Interaction with an interest in theory. This could be about a high-level theory like self-determination theory, activity theory, and theory of planned behavior, or they could be about more specific models or frameworks. The ideal candidate will be able to document knowledge on (a) working with particular theories, (b) empirically exploring the use of theory in Human-computer Interaction, (c) using LLMs, NLP, or similar technologies to study or develop theory, or (c) developing systems in AI, XR, or social media by using theory.

In addition, the ideal candidate will be able to document research capabilities (e.g., a thesis, publication, or project portfolio), have strong recommendations from supervisors and mentors, and possess a high level of intellectual humility. The candidate may have a background in computer science, psychology, design research, or any other discipline related to human-computer interaction.

 

Our group and research - and what do we offer?

The section on Human-centered Computing at University of Copenhagen is about 15 faculty focusing on different aspects on Human-computer Interaction; the section has an additional 20+ postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and research assistants. We hold joint research meetings and have a thriving social environment. The group is a part of Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen.

The TRACTION project is a six-year endeavor funded by the Villum Foundation that started in 2025; we are currently 2 postdocs, 2 PhD students, and a center administrator. This call is part of a second wave of hiring up to four junior researchers at the PhD and postdoctoral levels. The idea is to create a thriving center with regular meetings, frequent summer schools and workshops, and many visiting researchers.

The principal supervisor for the project will be Professor Kasper Hornbæk, he can be contacted at kash@diku.dk.

 

The PhD programme

Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

********************************************************************************

Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

Qualifications needed for the regular programme
To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Computer Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

Terms of employment in the regular programme
Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculy of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

Terms of the integrated programme
To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Computer Science.

Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.
A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

  • Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme

 (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme)

  • Carry through an independent research project under supervision
  • Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE
  • Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

***************************************************************************

 

Application and Assessment Procedure

 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking Apply for position below.

Please include:

  2. An outline of your interest in theory, earlier work with theory, and your ideas of working with theory based on the text in this call (max. two pages).

Original diplomas for Bachelor of Science or Master of Science and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.
  5. Publication list.
  6. Up to three reference letters or contact information for people who have agreed to provide a reference letter.

Application deadline:

The deadline for applications is 1th of December 2026 23:59 GMT +2. We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

 

The further process
After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified, whether you will be passed for assessment.

The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

 

Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in late January 2027.

 

Questions
For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in applied nuclear physics
jobs.description_html:
The Nuclear Structure Group at the Division of Particle and Nuclear Physics at Lund University is seeking a skilled and highly motivated PhD student to work on upcycling state-of-the-art detectors used in nuclear structure studies for environmental monitoring and emergency preparedness. The Division of Particle and Nuclear Physics, which has approximately 50 employees, conducts a broad range of research in both theoretical and experimental particle and heavy-ion physics, as well as experimental nuclear physics. The Nuclear Structure Group is active in several international collaborations exploiting large-scale accelerator facilities across the globe. With the present position, however, we thrive to intensify local collaborations with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.
As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.
More about being a doctoral student at the Science Faculty.  

Project Description

The project "From Lundium to L.U.N.D.I.U.M." (Swedish Radiation Safety Authority) will see the upcycling of various state-of-the-art components of the Lundium decay station for studies of Super Heavy Elements into L.U.N.D.I.U.M.: the Lund University Next-generation Device for Identification of Unknown radioactive sources and environmental Monitoring. L.U.N.D.I.U.M. will have unprecedented alpha-beta-gamma resolving capabilities stemming from its high granularity of detector components and contemporary multi-coincidence data acquisition systems.

The research environment constitutes an interdisciplinary community of knowledge and practice focused on data analysis and simulations of complex datasets to be used for radiation safety and emergency preparedness within the disciplines of physics, work environment, medical radiation physics, and environmental monitoring.

We are now recruiting one PhD student to be integrated into the research group and lead this development from conceptualization and optimization via Monte Carlo Geant4 simulations to realization of the device.

The PhD student will collaborate during specific phases of their doctoral education, with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group for sample collection and preparation.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. 

The PhD project will address the need for expanding the Swedish network of environmental monitor and emergency preparedness with the development and usage of a new-generation device for nuclear forensics. The tasks include:

  • Optimize via Monte Carlo simulations the geometry and elements of the new device upcycling the existing state-of-the-art detector components for measurement of various types of environmental filter and electroplated samples.
  • Conduct and coordinate the mechanical construction of the device and develop its data acquisition system and data analysis framework.
  • Validation of the measurements using simulated contamination samples provided by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) for yearly proficiency tests.
  • In close collaboration with the Biospheric and Anthropogenic Radioactivity group, develop methods to analyse radioactive aerosols from environmental samples.

At various stages of the project, close collaboration is envisaged with researchers at the University of Jyväskylä, Finland, in charge of a comparable measurement station.

The research projects will be reported in the form of articles submitted for publication in scientific journals, reports to the funding organisation, and conference contributions.

The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (up to a maximum of 20% of working time).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Specific admission requirements

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle programme in Physics, if they:

  • has at least 45 second cycle credits in physics or engineering physics or an associated field, or
  • has a second cycle (master) degree in physics or engineering physics or an associated field.

The specific entry requirement may also have been obtained through other equivalent education, which is assessed in each individual case. Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme.

 Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • completion of courses amounting to at least 60 credits that are directly relevant to the PhD education
  • a strong ability to work independently and the ability to formulate and address scientific problems
  • good written and oral communication skills
  • good ability to collaborate
  • very good proficiency in English, both spoken and written
  • an interest in interdisciplinary work

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications:

  • excellent laboratory skills concerning contemporary radiation detectors
  • proficiency with multi-parameter data acquisition systems
  • proficiency in modern object oriented programming
  • knowledge of environmental radioactivity or radioecology knowledge of radionuclide production in nuclear power plants and spallation sources
  • previous experience to ionizing radiation detection
  • previous experience with Monte Carlo radiation transport codes

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. It is advisable to enter information on what your unit specifically can offer as a workplace.

More information about working at Lund University on lu.se. 

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting 1 January 2027 at the earliest. Third cycle studies consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More information about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages.

Other

Selection for admission to doctoral studies is based on the assessed ability to successfully complete the doctoral education. The assessment of this ability is primarily based on study results at the first- and second-cycle (Bachelor’s and Master’s) levels.

The following criteria will be considered:

  • Knowledge and skills relevant to the doctoral project and the field of study, as described under Work duties. These may be demonstrated through submitted documentation.
  • Assessed ability to work independently and to formulate and address scientific problems. This assessment may, for example, be based on the degree project and a discussion thereof during a potential interview.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in writing and orally.
  • Other experience relevant to doctoral studies, such as professional experience.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, initiative, independence, and personal suitability, as well as to how the applicant’s experience and competence are assessed to demonstrate the ability required to complete the doctoral education.

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project.
  • Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.)

We welcome your application!

jobs.title: PHD student in Epigenetics and Chromatin Dynamics
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Laboratory of Epigenetics and Chromatin Dynamics at the Department of Experimental Medical Science (Faculty of Medicine), is currently conducting research investigating the epigenetic regulation of repetitive and transposable genetic elements – so-called 'genomic dark matter' – in human brain development and disease. The group consists of 8 research-active members and is led by Dr Christopher Douse. We are fascinated by how these underexplored regions of the human genome contribute functionally to human neurobiology and neurological disease. Our work integrates state-of-the-art wet and dry lab methods. More information can be found here . As a workplace, we safeguard a good work environment with respect and consideration in our relationships with each other. We commit to the following core lab values: Equity – all lab members have value and contribute, there are no stupid questions; People-centric - our work is collaborative and we communicate openly with eachother, the community and the outside world; Integrity – we do not take shortcuts and emphasize reproducibilty and rigor in our data. Curiosity - we are humble about what we don't know, actively seek feedback and are open to ideas; Diversity – we will do better research if we have diversity of background and scientific expertise.

Project description

We are particularly focused currently on three types of element that are repetitive in different ways, but unified by an importance to human brain function and disease: clustered protocadherin repeat genes, viral-like sequences called retrotransposons, and CGG microsatellite tandem repeats. In all cases there are significant knowledge gaps surrounding the epigenetic control and influence of the elements. What are the factors that bind and regulate these REs in neural lineages? How do they functionally impact the epigenome and local transcriptional dynamics, and disease traits? To answer these questions we will combine chromatin biochemistry and cutting-edge functional epigenomics with advanced neural cellular models and tailored bioinformatic analyses. In doing so we will discover new, basic human neurobiology and much-needed insights on the mechanisms underpinning RE-associated neurological disorders.

This PhD project will combine chromatin biochemistry with functional (epi)genomics in stem cell models of the human brain. Importantly, this PhD project will require a balance of wet and dry-lab approaches.

In particular the doctoral student will use the following methods:

  • Stem cell culture (iPSCs, 2- and 3D neural progenitors)
  • RNA-seq, CUT&RUN/Tag, Oxford Nanopore sequencing (cDNA, DiMeLo-seq) and associated bioinformatic analyses
  • Co-immunoprecipitation and/or proximity labelling proteomics

Tasks and responsibilities

The main task for a doctoral student is to devote yourself to your doctoral studies, therefore you will be both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. In addition to your full-time research studies, you may be involved in the supervision of bachelor or master students.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. Read more on the University website about being a Lund University employee Work at Lund University

Qualifications

 

Requirements for admission are:

  • a second-cycle degree, completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 higher education credits are at second-cycle level, or substantially equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad
  • the ability to benefit from doctoral studies

Requirements for the position are:

  • experience in functional (epi)genomics and/or chromatin biochemistry
  • experience with stem cell culture and differentiation models
  • a demonstrable interest in the repetitive genome, either in humans or model organisms, through previous experience or as described in your cover letter or during an interview
  • excellent knowledge of molecular biology and molecular genetics
  • excellent spoken and written English
  • good analytical skills and an independent, problem-solving approach
  • an open and collaborative approach to research, in line with the lab values described above

The following qualifications are considered an advantage:

  • being highly organised and self-motivated
  • experience with long-read sequencing approaches
  • experience with protein biochemistry
  • experience working collaboratively on ambitious research projects
  • being receptive to constructive feedback and demonstrating a willingness to develop and learn throughout the doctoral studies

Further information

Limit of tenure, four years according to HF 5 kap 7§. Start date 1th of December 2026, or as agreed.

How to apply

The application should include a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a CV, degree certificates or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.) Candidates will be considered on an ongoing basis during the application period.

About the Faculty of Medicine
