jobs.description_html:
Placering

Som doktorand blir du en del av forskargruppen Aktivt och hälsosamt åldrande vid Institutionen för hälsovetenskaper. Forskargruppen är knuten till det tvärvetenskapliga Centre for Ageing and Supportive Environments (CASE), där seniora och juniora forskare från fyra av universitetets fakulteter samarbetar.

Hos oss får du en stimulerande och inkluderande arbetsmiljö där samarbete, kunskapsutbyte och utveckling står i centrum. Du får stöd av engagerade kollegor och handledare samt möjlighet att växa i en tvärvetenskaplig och internationell forskningsmiljö. Läs mer om att arbeta på Lunds universitet här.

Beskrivning

Forskarutbildningen leder till en doktorsexamen i medicinsk vetenskap med inriktning hälsovetenskap. I doktorandprojektet bidrar du till ökad kunskap om vad tillgängliga och användbara publika miljöer innebär för personer med olika kognitiva funktionsnedsättningar. Du undersöker också hur kunskapen kan omsättas i nya sätt att utforma publika anläggningar och digital information som stärker människors delaktighet i samhället.

Studierna genomförs inom det fyraåriga projektet ”PRO-COG: Tillgängliga och användbara publika anläggningar som främjar delaktighet i samhället för personer med kognitiva funktionsnedsättningar”. Projektet finansieras av Forskningsrådet för miljö, areella näringar och samhällsbyggande (FORMAS) och bedrivs i en tvärvetenskaplig forskningsmiljö. Du kommer främst att arbeta med kvalitativa metoder för datainsamling och analys. Dina handledare representerar hälsovetenskap och arbetsterapi.

Arbetsuppgifter

Som doktorand ägnar du dig främst åt din egen forskarutbildning. Enligt 5 kap. 2 § högskoleförordningen (HF) kan även utbildning, forskning och administration ingå, dock högst 20 procent av en heltidsanställning innan doktorsexamen har avlagts.

Med stöd av dina handledare kommer du att:

  • medverka i planeringen av projektet,
  • samla in, analysera och sammanställa data,
  • rapportera resultat i vetenskapliga artiklar på engelska,
  • sammanfatta doktorandprojektet i en engelskspråkig ramberättelse och presentera det i en doktorsavhandling,
  • genomföra obligatoriska kurser på forskarnivå och aktivt delta i seminarier och andra relevanta aktiviteter,
  • fördjupa dig i litteratur inom forskningsområdet, samt
  • kommunicera och omsätta forskningsresultat för målgrupper inom och utanför forskarsamhället.

Resor inom Sverige och internationellt förekommer. En forskningsvistelse vid ett annat universitet i Sverige eller utomlands kan också bli aktuell.

Du förväntas också bidra till relevanta aktiviteter och uppdrag inom forskargruppen, institutionen och CASE. Även andra arbetsuppgifter kan förekomma.

Behörighet

För att vara behörig till utbildningen på forskarnivå ska du uppfylla något av följande:

  • avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå, eller
  • fullgjort minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
  • på annat sätt, inom eller utanför Sverige, förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

Forskarutbildningsnämnden kan medge undantag från kravet på grundläggande behörighet om det finns särskilda skäl.

Särskild behörighet

För särskild behörighet krävs minst 60 högskolepoäng inom medicinsk vetenskap och tillräckliga kunskaper inom forskarutbildningens ämnesområde.

Om du har en utomnordisk grundexamen, och ditt hemspråk inte är engelska, behöver du även styrka kunskaper i engelska motsvarande treårig gymnasieutbildning genom ett godkänt prov.

Krav

  • God datorvana.
  • Goda kunskaper i tal och skrift i svenska eller ett annat skandinaviskt språk.
  • Goda kunskaper i engelska.

Meriterande

  • Erfarenhet av att möta och samverka med personer med kognitiva funktionsnedsättningar.

Personliga egenskaper

Vi lägger stor vikt vid personlig lämplighet. För att trivas och lyckas i rollen behöver du kunna arbeta självständigt och noggrant samt samarbeta väl med andra.

Bedömningsgrund

Bestämmelser om anställning som doktorand finns i förordning SFS 1998:80. Endast den som är antagen till utbildning på forskarnivå kan anställas som doktorand. Vid urvalet bedömer vi framför allt din förmåga att tillgodogöra dig forskarutbildningen.

Villkor

Anställningen är på heltid med planerat tillträde den 11 januari 2027 eller enligt överenskommelse.

Anställningen är tidsbegränsad till fyra år enligt 5 kap. 7 § högskoleförordningen.

Kontakt
Har du frågor om anställningen är du välkommen att kontakta huvudhandledare och biträdande forskare Björn Slaug på telefon 046 222 18 38 eller via e-post: bjorn.slaug@med.lu.se.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Industrial Design with focus on strategic design
jobs.description_html:
Beskrivning av verksamheten

Anställningen är placerad vid Avdelningen för industridesign vid Institutionen för designvetenskaper, LTH, Lunds universitet. Institutionen för designvetenskaper är en tvärvetenskaplig miljö som integrerar design, teknik och människa i såväl forskning som utbildning.

Som doktorand kommer du att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig forskningsmiljö och arbeta tillsammans med doktorander, seniora forskare och undervisande personal inom industridesign samt inom den bredare verksamheten vid Institutionen för designvetenskaper.

Att vara doktorand

Som doktorand är du både antagen som student och anställd vid Lunds universitet.
Som forskarstuderande tränas du i ett vetenskapligt förhållningssätt. Det kan kort beskrivas som att du får övning i att tänka kritiskt och analytiskt, att du får lösa problem självständigt med hjälp av rätt metodval och du får en forskningsetisk medvetenhet. Dessutom ges möjlighet för dig som doktorand att arbeta med projekt, att utveckla dina ledaregenskaper och din pedagogiska förmåga. Under hela din studietid guidas du av handledare. Forskarstudierna avslutas med en avhandling och doktorsexamen.
Mer om att vara doktorand vid LTH på lth.se.

Ämnes- och projektbeskrivning

Forskningen inom industridesign undersöker hur design formar och förhåller sig till teknologiska, miljömässiga och samhälleliga förändringsprocesser. Forskningen syftar till att utveckla och kritiskt granska designkunskap, metoder och praktiker för att öka förståelsen för hur design kan bidra till meningsfull och ansvarsfull samhällsomställning.

Forskningsverksamheten kombinerar vetenskapliga och konstnärliga angreppssätt och bedrivs ofta i samverkan med akademiska, industriella och offentliga aktörer samt med civilsamhällets organisationer och andra samhällsaktörer. Forskningsmiljön omfattar bland annat hållbar design, framväxande teknologier och artificiell intelligens (AI), designstrategi, designledning och innovation, designpraktik och designmetoder samt kritiska och deltagande perspektiv på design och designutbildning.

Denna doktorandtjänst har särskilt fokus på strategisk design. Forskningen kommer att undersöka hur design kan verka som en strategisk resurs i organisationer och i samhället samt bidra till innovation, omställning och värdeskapande. Forskningsfrågorna kan exempelvis beröra hur designkompetens utvecklas och integreras i organisationer, hur design och designmetoder kan möjliggöra organisatorisk förändring, design i komplexa system och sammanhang, systemisk design samt användar- och medborgarengagemang i strategiska designprocesser. Forskningen kan även omfatta framtidsorienterade angreppssätt och hur design kan användas för att hantera komplexa och osäkra samhälleliga, teknologiska och miljömässiga förutsättningar.

Inom ramen för detta övergripande forskningsområde kommer doktoranden, i samråd med handledarna, att utveckla och precisera den specifika forskningsinriktningen och projektets utformning. Projektet förväntas kombinera teoretiska studier med empirisk forskning och kan, när så är relevant, innefatta experimentella, deltagande eller praktikbaserade designansatser.

Arbetsuppgifter

Du kommer framförallt att ägna dig åt din forskarutbildning, vilket innefattar såväl deltagande i forskningsprojekt som forskarutbildningskurser, seminarier och konferenser.

Du kommer att utveckla och genomföra ett självständigt forskningsprojekt inom ramen för forskarutbildningen. Arbetet innefattar att formulera forskningsfrågor, identifiera och vidareutveckla relevanta teoretiska perspektiv, planera och genomföra empiriska studier, analysera forskningsmaterial samt kommunicera forskningsresultat genom vetenskapliga publikationer och konferensbidrag. Arbetet omfattar även författande av en doktorsavhandling.

Du förväntas vidare delta aktivt i forskningsmiljön vid Avdelningen för industridesign och Institutionen för designvetenskaper samt samverka med relevanta akademiska och externa forskningspartners.

I arbetsuppgifterna ingår det även medverkan i undervisning och annat institutionsarbete (dock max 20 % av arbetstiden).

Anställningen förutsätter regelbunden närvaro vid Lunds universitet i Lund för att kunna genomföra arbetsuppgifterna och delta fullt ut i forskningsmiljön.

Kvalifikationer

För att kunna antas och anställas som doktorand behöver du uppfylla kraven nedan.

Behörighetskrav

Grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå uppfyller du som har:

  • avlagd examen på avancerad nivå eller
  • fullgjorda kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå eller
  • på något annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

Särskild behörighet för Industridesign uppfyller du som har:

  • minst 30 högskolepoäng med relevans för ämnesområdet, varav minst 15 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
  • ett självständigt arbete om minst 20 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå med relevans för ämnesområdet, eller
  • examen inom konstnärligt område, civilingenjörsexamen, masterexamen eller magisterexamen med relevans för ämnesområdet.

Övriga krav

För att tillgodogöra sig den aktuella forskarutbildningen krävs även:  

  • Dokumenterad kunskap och kompetens med relevans för industridesign och det aktuella forskningsområdet.
  • God förmåga att självständigt formulera och bearbeta vetenskapliga problemställningar.
  • God analytisk förmåga samt förmåga att kritiskt förhålla sig till såväl teoretiska perspektiv som empiriskt material.
  • mycket goda kunskaper i engelska, i tal och skrift.

Meriterande

För den aktuella forskarutbildningen är följande meriterande:  

  • erfarenhet av att genomföra empirisk, praktikbaserad eller deltagande forskning,
  • erfarenhet av tvärvetenskapligt eller multidisciplinärt arbete,e
  • erfarenhet av att leda eller koordinera komplexa projekt som involverar flera aktörer eller perspektiv,
  • erfarenhet av att använda designmetoder och designpraktiker som en del av forsknings- eller utvecklingsarbete,
  • erfarenhet av samarbete med akademiska, industriella, offentliga eller andra samhälleliga aktörer,
  • erfarenhet av att kommunicera forskning eller kvalificerat designarbete till olika målgrupper.

Hänsyn kommer även att tas till den sökandes förmåga att ta initiativ, arbeta självständigt, samarbeta med andra samt utveckla och genomföra ett långsiktigt forskningsprojekt.

Vi erbjuder

Lunds universitet är en statlig myndighet vilket innebär att du får särskilda förmåner, generös semester och en förmånlig tjänstepension.

Mer om att jobba på Lunds universitet på lu.se. 

Om anställningen

Anställningen är en visstidsanställning på heltid, med start 2027-01-01 eller enligt överenskommelse. Forskarutbildningen är fyra år vid heltidsstudier. Vid undervisning och annat institutionsarbete förlängs anställningen i motsvarande grad. Bestämmelser gällande anställning som doktorand finns i Högskoleförordningen (1993:100), 5 kap 1-7 §§.

Mer om anställningsvillkor för doktorander på Lunds universitets medarbetarwebb. 

Övrigt

Denna doktorandanställning finansieras av Ingvar Kamprad Design Foundation (IKDF).

Så här söker du

Ansökan ska skrivas på engelska och till din ansökan ska du bifoga:

  • CV.
  • Ett personligt brev där du beskriver varför du vill genomföra forskarutbildning inom industridesign, ditt intresse för den aktuella anställningen samt hur dina akademiska, professionella och/eller personliga erfarenheter har format dina forskningsintressen och förberett dig för forskarstudier.
  • Kopior av examensbevis och studieutdrag som styrker att du uppfyller de allmänna och särskilda behörighetskraven.
  • En forskningsbeskrivning (maximalt 1 500 ord) där du redogör för de forskningsfrågor, problemställningar eller fenomen inom strategisk design som du är intresserad av att utforska, varför du bedömer dem som betydelsefulla samt hur du skulle kunna närma dig och undersöka dem. Syftet med forskningsbeskrivningen är att visa dina forskningsintressen och din förmåga att formulera en möjlig inriktning för doktorandprojektet. Beskrivningen behöver inte utgöra en färdig forskningsplan.
  • Portfolio eller urval av arbetsprover som visar relevant design-, forsknings- eller yrkesrelaterad verksamhet. Arbetsproverna kan exempelvis omfatta designprojekt, forskningsprojekt, publikationer eller andra skriftliga arbeten, samarbetsprojekt, samhällsengagerade projekt eller annat arbete av relevans för anställningen. För arbeten som genomförts i samarbete med andra ska den egna rollen och det egna bidraget tydligt framgå.
  • Kontaktuppgifter till tre referenspersoner.
  • Eventuella övriga handlingar som du önskar åberopa.

Välkommen med din ansökan!

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Risk and Safety of Heterogeneous Swarm Systems
jobs.department: Lund University, Faculty of Engineering, Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences strives to be a leading center for aeronautics research, development, and education. The department operates a certified commercial flight school (ATO) and an authorized drone school (ADS) under the name of Lund University School of Aviation, Sweden's only state-run civilian flight school. The department’s research facilities are based at Campus Ljungbyhed, providing a unique setting that integrates research, development, and education with access to airport infrastructure, including a runway system and controlled airspace. We seek to understand, innovate, and advance aviation through collaborative efforts, making it more accessible, sustainable, and safe in the digital age. The research emphasizes three primary areas: sustainable aviation, unmanned aviation, and aviation safety, with safety being a central theme across all initiatives.

This doctoral student position is at the Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences and will work at the intersection between unmanned aviation and aviation safety, as part of the Center for Heterogeneous Adaptive Swarm Systems (CHASS) funded by Stiftelsen för Strategisk Forskning*  (SSF). CHASS includes three dual-use relevant large industrial partners (Saab, Sectra Communications and BAE Systems Hägglunds) and societal participation from the Swedish Defence Research Institute (FOI), the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency (MCF) and the Swedish Civil Aviation Administration (LFV).

The duty station is Ljungbyhed.

*More about SSF

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se

Subject and project description

The research area is Risk and Safety of heterogeneous swarm systems.

The multi-disciplinary center for heterogeneous adaptive swarm systems, CHASS, is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI, autonomous systems, robotics, and swarm intelligence to develop novel solutions for autonomous heterogeneous swarm systems for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a leader in intelligent, adaptive, and trustworthy swarm systems by pioneering autonomous heterogeneous collectives of space, aerial, ground, surface, and underwater platforms that can operate as a unified intelligent entity with minimal human intervention. The research program focuses on six key themes: Drone Design, Adaptation, & Production; Perception, Sensing, & Communication; Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation; Coordination, Self-Governance, & Self-Improvement; Human Swarm Interaction; and Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects.

CHASS is led by Linköping University and besides Lund University also includes Örebro University, each with CHASS-affiliated doctoral students, as well as a large number of industry and government stakeholders, providing a stimulating research environment. CHASS will drive world-class research in autonomous swarm systems through a strong, stimulating, and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. CHASS will also serve as a national hub for autonomous swarm systems, promoting education, knowledge sharing, innovation, and policy development.

The doctoral student position in this announcement will work within the theme of Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. It develops and evaluates risk assessment and safety management methodologies (for the phases before, during, and after operations) for heterogeneous swarms, including frameworks for risk assessment, adaptive capacity and control, and accountability and responsibility. The position will include interaction with other doctoral students and researchers within this theme, as well as the Human Swarm Interaction theme and the other technological development themes.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The work duties include:

  • You will work in a multi-disciplinary research project focused on socio-technical aspects of control, risk, and safety of heterogeneous swarms resilience.
  • You will likely combine qualitative (e.g. interviews) and quantitative (e.g. modelling, statistics) methods.
  • You will travel in Sweden and abroad to interact with fellow researchers to collaborate and present research findings at scientific conferences.
  • As parts of the research may be conducted in collaboration with defence-related organisations, a security screening will be carried out if applicable.
  • The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Risk and Safety (TEVBRF11) if the applicant has:

  • at least 90 credits in subjects of relevance to the field, including at least 60 second cycle credits, or
  • a BSc in Fire Protection Engineering amounting to 210 credits.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • good knowledge in risk, system safety, design, and governance of socio-technical systems in complex settings,
  • good ability to take initiative and solve research challenges with drive, creativity, and persistence,
  • good ability to work in a structured way in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary environment,
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems,
  • good written and oral communication skills,
  • good ability to cooperate with other researchers and practitioners,
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as meriting qualifications:

  • knowledge of aeronautical engineering, human-computer interaction, human factors engineering, cognitive science, human control of AI, unmanned aviation, critical infrastructure resilience, interaction design, industrial design engineering, and related disciplines,
  • skills and experience in modelling and simulation,
  • skills and experience in relevant software and programming environments, such as Matlab, Python, C++, UAS communication protocols (MAVLink), ROS2, git.
  • skills and experience in statistical analysis and quantitative research methods,
  • skills and experience relating to relevant qualitative research methods, such as interviews,
  • driving licence B,
  • practical experience of operations in manned or unmanned aviation.

Consideration will also be given to how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting on 1 January 2027 or as agreed. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages

Other

The recruitment process will include interviews and your reflections on work samples. Interviews will be conducted either online or in person at Lund university.

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project.
  • Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.)

We welcome your application.

About the Faculty of Engineering

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Technology and Society on regulatory learning and supervisory competence
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE, which is a MSCA doctoral pan-European network that studies how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. The network will train fifteen fellows to examine this learning process from different angles. They will look at how authorities detect early signals, design and test interventions, evaluate what works, and share findings across organisations. 

REGULAIRE stands for Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies, and the consortium is led by Technical University Munich. The consortium includes technical universities, business schools, social and legal scientists, and public sector actors.

This call is of a doctoral position at LTH, Lund University. The research group environment at LTH in Lund, led by Stefan Larsson, focuses on social science-oriented but multidisciplinary issues linked to AI, with affiliated researchers at both junior and senior levels. The research group has a working space at LTH and is part of the Department of Technology and Society. Read more about the research group on the Research Portal of Lund University.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. 

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

The doctoral subject Technology and Society encompasses multi- and interdisciplinary studies on the role, interaction, regulation and significance of technology within society. Research includes both qualitative and quantitative studies and is often characterized by a diversity of methods and theories.

Regulatory flexibility helps law keep pace with fast-moving technologies, but law also needs predictable norms. This doctoral project studies how the two sit together, asking whether flexibilities, delegations, open-textured duties and codes of practice shift authority among legislators, the Commission, standardisers, private actors, and with a special attention to supervisory authorities.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. 

You will map supervisory competence, organisation and tooling in selected jurisdictions, using the AI Act to structure comparison, and combine document analysis, interviews and process tracing to link design choices to predictability for firms and protection for citizens.

The work will from a critical perspective analyse flexibility mechanisms and their governance implications. It could be grounded in supervisory practice, comparative case reports and contribute to an assessment framework for supervisory capability. It will also translate evidence into guidance on aligning flexibility with foresight without eroding legal certainty, if possible. This project offers a focused route into socio-legal research, AI governance and the study of technology-oriented supervision.

The employment will include a three-month intersectoral secondment in another country.

The work duties include:

  • Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team, and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials.
  • Collect, manage and analyse research data using the approved project-specific methods.
  • Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the doctoral programme and the REGULAIRE plan.
  • Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, network reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement, including three residential summer schools and monthly paper development seminars.
  • Undertake the planned three-month intersectoral secondment with a partner institution within REGULAIRE.
  • The duties may also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications 

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: 

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or 
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or 
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Technology and Society if the applicant has: 

  • at least 30 credits awarded in the second cycle relevant to the subject area.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: 

  • An educational background in relevant field, for example law, socio-legal studies, political science, science and technology studies, or related social science and interdisciplinary fields.
  • You take initiatives, are structured and persistent.
    Good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems. 
  • Good written and oral communication skills
  • Good ability to cooperate
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written 

To be eligible for MSCA funding, the selected candidate must also, on the first day of employment: 

  • not hold a doctoral degree; candidates who have successfully defended a doctoral thesis but have not yet formally received the degree are not eligible; 
  • comply with the MSCA mobility rule, meaning you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding that date, excluding compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent in a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: 

  • experience of qualitative methods, such as document analysis, interviews or process tracing.
  • sociolegal knowledge on how society and law interacts.
  • technological knowledge of emerging technologies.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. 

More about working at Lund University on lu.se.

About the employment

jobs.title: PhD student in Political Science
jobs.description_html:
Duties

The PhD program in political science consists of 240 credits (equivalent to four years of full-time studies) and is concluded with the public defense of a printed doctoral thesis. The appointed doctoral student will receive a salary from the University for four years, and the primary obligation is to complete the PhD studies. The position may involve departmental duties, for instance in the form of teaching, of up to 20 percent of full-time working hours, in which case the appointment will be extended accordingly. The doctoral student will have access to a workspace at the Department of Political Science. The terms of employment for doctoral students are regulated in the Swedish Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1–7.

The position is part of the research project “A Divisive Spiral? Elite Communication, Voter Engagement, and Algorithmic Amplification of Affective Polarization”. The project is funded by the Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet) 2027–2030 and led by Professor Hanna Bäck at the Department of Political Science, Lund University. The project focuses on how affective polarization, strong negative feelings toward political opponents, emerges from the interplay between politicians’ communication and voters’ engagement on social media. Large language models are used to analyze polarizing communication in text and audio from Sweden and Finland at scale, and experiments test how forms of communication and algorithms affect voters. Read more about the project here

The doctoral student is expected to contribute to the study of affective polarization among elected representatives and voters, in line with the overall aim of the project. Within these parameters and in dialogue with the other project participants, the doctoral student will conduct independent research and formulate their own research questions, theoretical ideas and methodological approaches. The doctoral student is expected to be present at the department and actively participate in its research and teaching environment, as well as take part in the work of the project.

Qualifications

The requirements for admission to third-cycle courses and study programs (in accordance with (HF ch. 7 § 35) are that the applicant:

  • meets the general and specific entry requirements that the higher education institution may have laid down, and
  • is considered in other respects to have the ability required to benefit from the course or study program (Swedish Code of Statutes 2010:1064).

Applicants meet the general entry requirements for third-cycle courses and study programs if they:

  • have been awarded a second-cycle qualification,
  • have satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

 Specific entry requirements

In addition to the general entry requirements, the applicant must have completed at least 30 second-cycle credits within the main field of political science, or have acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or abroad. The applicant must also have completed an independently written thesis of at least 15 second-cycle credits in political science or in a discipline deemed equivalent in relation to the project. The thesis must have been examined and graded at the time of application.

Assessment criteria

Only applicants who are admitted to third-cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral studentship. Admission is primarily to be based on the applicant’s ability to benefit from the third-cycle program. The applicants will be ranked based on an overall assessment of the quality of their submitted thesis or theses and research plan, grades from previous studies, and their personal suitability. As third-cycle studies in political science are very demanding, the applicant must be highly motivated and able to work independently under time constraints. Good collaboration and communication skills are also required, as is proficiency in both written and spoken English. Documented experience of research related to the project’s themes, and of automated text analysis, is a strong merit. Further merits include experience of programming and of working with large-scale social science data, as well as knowledge of languages relevant to the project’s empirical material. Interviews will be conducted with a short-listed number of applicants during the final stages of the admission process.

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment for four years in accordance with the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1–7. Starting date January 1, 2027, or by agreement.

The main language of the PhD program is English. However, non-Swedish speaking students are expected to acquire basic skills in Swedish during the period of employment. There are opportunities to participate in language courses taught at the University.  The general syllabus and other information about the PhD program in political science is available at https://www.svet.lu.se/en/internal/research-education-external-engagement/doctoral-studies-introduction

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. https://www.staff.lu.se/research-and-education/research-support/doctoral-education/terms-employment-doctoral-students

How to apply

Applications are to be submitted via the Lund University recruitment portal. The evaluation of applicants is based on documents submitted by the application deadline. Only complete applications will be considered. It is not possible to add documentation after the deadline.

The application must include:

  • a cover letter in Swedish or English of max 1 000 words, which contains a brief presentation of yourself and your qualifications, as well as a brief explanation of why you are interested in third-cycle studies at the Department of Political Science at Lund University;
  • a CV in Swedish or English that demonstrates your eligibility for the third-cycle program in political science;
  • degree and grade certificates in Swedish or English;
  • a thesis in Swedish or English corresponding to at least 15 second-cycle credits in political science or a discipline deemed equivalent (where applicable, a Bachelor’s thesis may also be submitted in addition to the second-cycle thesis);
  • a brief research plan in Swedish or English of max 2 000 words, including references;
  • the names and contact information of two references, preferably active in academia (letters of reference are not required at the application stage);
  • any other documentation you wish to submit in support of your application.

 We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Astronomy and Astrophysics
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Planet Formation Group at the Department of Physics (Division of Astrophysics) at Lund University is seeking a PhD student to work on models of planet formation on a galactic scale. Research within the division encompasses galaxy formation, galactic dynamics and evolution, star formation and dynamics, stellar evolution, stellar spectroscopy and astrometry, planet formation and dynamics, as well as exoplanet atmospheres.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se.

  • Allmän studieplan för forskarutbildning

Work duties

We are seeking a PhD student in theoretical astrophysics. The PhD student will study how planets form at different times and in different regions of our galaxy. The PhD student will also calculate how certain planetesimals are ejected from planetary systems to become free-flying interstellar planetesimals. The PhD project will give astronomers new insight into where interstellar comets came from.

Your primary responsibility will be to pursue your doctoral studies, which will mainly consist of conducting research and writing a doctoral thesis. In addition, you will be expected to:

  • Conduct research within the subject area.
  • Publish results in high-quality scientific journals.
  • Present research results at national and international conferences.

In addition, you are expected to participate in doctoral courses, seminars and conferenes. In addition to studies, a maximum of 20% of working time may be spent on teaching and other departmental work

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Specific admission requirements

To be admitted to the third-cycle programme in Astronomy and Astrophysics the student must have earned credits in first and second-cycle programmes in which physics, mathematics and/or corresponding engineering subjects have been substantial elements. In addition to 60 credits in basic physics, there is a requirement for at least 60 credits in subjects of relevance to Astronomy and Astrophysics, e.g., courses in astronomy or other physics subjects, or engineering subjects such as space technology and automatic control. The 120 credits must include at least 60 second-cycle credits. 

Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually. 

In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Astronomy and Astrophysics may be considered for admission.

Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Strong ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle scientific problems.
  • Good written and oral communication skills.
  • Strong collaborative and teamwork skills.
  • Very good proficiency in English, both spoken and written.

Merits

  • Experience in analyzing and working with models of planet formation or galaxy formation
  • Excellent numerical and analytical problem-solving skills, as well as experience with programming languages (e.g. Python and Fortran).
  • Extensive knowledge of galaxy formation and galaxy formation.

Selection criteria

The selection of eligible applicants will be made taking into account the ability to benefit from the training based on the following criteria:

  • Relevant qualifications and expertise (see the requirements and merit criteria listed above).
  • Demonstrated ability to handle complex research problems and to work both collaboratively and independently, as well as to complete tasks on schedule.
  • Consideration will also be given to strong collaborative skills, motivation, and independence, as well as to how the applicant’s experience and qualifications demonstrate the abilities required to successfully complete doctoral studies.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Biomedical Engineering specializing in engineering acoustics
jobs.department: Lund University, Faculty of Engineering, LTH, Dep. of Biomedical Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The position is based at the Department of Biomedical Engineering and is linked to researchers working in marine biology, medical ultrasound, biomechanics, physics, e-science, and the strategic research area eSSENCE in Lund. The research group you will join conducts research in areas including engineering acoustics, medical ultrasound, acoustic measurement technology, non-destructive testing based on acoustic methods, signal processing, and numerical modelling, with applications in, among other fields, biomedical engineering, civil engineering, and biological systems.

The working environment is highly interdisciplinary and is characterized by close collaboration between doctoral students, researchers, and academic staff, often with very different technical and scientific backgrounds and areas of expertise. The group strives to provide an open and inclusive working environment with good access to supervision, knowledge exchange, and broad scientific and interdisciplinary collaborations.

More about the strategic research area eSSENCE - on Lund University's website

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. 

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

We are looking for a candidate who is curious, focused, and highly motivated by scientific questions. You have a creative and open-minded approach and enjoy combining methods and perspectives from different fields, such as physics, acoustics, computational modelling, and biology. You are driven by a desire to understand complex phenomena and to contribute new knowledge that is relevant to technology and society, as well as to our understanding of biological systems.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH - lth.se

Work duties

You will primarily devote your time to your doctoral studies, which include participation in research projects as well as doctoral-level courses, seminars, and conferences.

You will be part of an interdisciplinary research project investigating the physical mechanisms underlying dolphin echolocation. The overall aim of the project is to develop and apply computational models in acoustics and structural mechanics to describe how the short, broadband ultrasonic pulses generated in the dolphin’s head propagate through tissues and other anatomical structures and are thereby shaped into a forward-directed echolocation beam. Particular emphasis will be placed on how variations in acoustic material properties, geometry, and potential reflective or refractive structures influence the direction, frequency-dependent shape, and temporal structure of the beam.

The work is interdisciplinary and lies at the interface of engineering acoustics, computational physics, biomedical engineering, and zoology/bioacoustics. The project also includes developing the technical aspects of the results into practically useful concepts for human-made technologies, for example medical applications in diagnostic ultrasound, underwater acoustic sonar systems, or non-destructive testing of civil engineering structures.
 
The work duties include:

  • research on the acoustic properties of relevant tissues and anatomical structures, for example by measuring sound speeds, densities, and attenuation properties, as well as assisting with anatomical CT imaging of the physiology of stranded harbour porpoises and related specimens
  • development of computer-based three-dimensional finite element models (FEM) of acoustic wave propagation in the sound-generating organs of dolphins and surrounding tissues, with the aim of creating a physically accurate so-called digital twin
  • collection and analysis of acoustic, mechanical, and anatomical data from toothed whales
  • development and use of computational and analysis code, with or without machine-learning components, in MATLAB and COMSOL or equivalent environments for model setup, post-processing, signal analysis, visualisation, and comparison between simulations and measurement data
  • collaboration with researchers in, among other fields, physics, marine mammal research, and computational sciences, acting as an interdisciplinary knowledge bridge between different scientific disciplines
  • communication of research results at scientific conferences and through the publication of scientific articles.

The duties may also include participation in teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: 

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or 
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or 
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Biomedical Engineering if the applicant has: 

  • at least 45 credits at second-cycle level relevant to the subject area

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: 

  • Knowledge and skills relevant to the doctoral project and the subject area (e.g. engineering or theoretical physics, wave propagation, engineering acoustics, programming, modelling, bioacoustics, computational methods, electronics, applied mathematics, zoology, materials physics, etc.). 
  • Very good analytical skills, including problem-solving and data analysis. 
  • Goal-oriented approach, which may be demonstrated through perseverance and the ability to work methodically, in a structured manner, and with focus.
  • Good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems. 
  • Good collaborative skills (i e manifested as a willingness to share ideas, constructive approach to challenges etc).
  • Very good written and oral communication skills.
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written 

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: 

  • Master’s degree in engineering physics or theoretical physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mathematics, computer engineering, engineering acoustics, or another subject relevant to the research area
  • Knowledge of numerical computational methods and/or FEM-based modelling of physical problems
  • Experience of finite element modelling in acoustics and multiphysics
  • Knowledge of marine mammals, toothed-whale echolocation or other areas of bioacoustics
  • Practical experience of acoustic or measurement systems
  • Practical experience of measurement technology and electronics
  • Programming experience beyond introductory-level courses
  • Experience of working with computing clusters
  • Experience of classical machine-learning or deep-learning-based signal analysis.

jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

Within EU doctoral network FairCFD, this project will combine high-performance computing, experiments and artificial intelligence in non-Newtonian flows, with the aim of improving rheological characterisation and modelling. In particular, we will design a digital twin rheometer to reliably measure complex fluid parameters in time-varying and chaotic flows.

We will use modern AI techniques to exploit spatial patterns in the computational and experimental data and optimize parameter sensitivity. The researcher will join the dynamic Complex Fluids Research group, have access to the supercomputing facilities at KTH, the Swedish e-Science Research Centre (SeRC) and the excellent research environment FLOW.

Supervision: Outi Tammisola and Fredrik Lundell are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.

Project description

Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering

Autonomous systems are increasingly deployed alongside humans to carry out complex coordinated tasks. In these settings, autonomous systems must handle strict spatial and temporal constraints while adapting in real time to supervisory commands, unexpected obstacles, and environmental disturbances. Enabling trustworthy human–robot collaboration calls for new mathematical foundations and computational tools that unify decision-making, planning, and control.

We are seeking an exceptional doctoral student to conduct research at the intersection of game theory and control for multi-agent autonomous systems. The position is part of the Digital Futures project Human-in-the-Loop Autonomy via Hybrid Games. The work will span both mathematical foundations of hybrid games and the design of computationally tractable controllers for deployment on real robotic platforms.

The research will address:

  • Hybrid dynamic games under temporal logic task specifications;
  • Game-theoretic modelling of human–robot interaction;
  • Experimental validation on multi-robot and underwater robotic platforms;

Third-cycle subject: Computer Science

The PhD student will work within GEOMANIP, an ERC Starting Grant project that aims to revolutionize the robotic manipulation of deformable objects by uncovering and exploiting their fundamental geometric nature. The PhD student will contribute to one or more of the following topics: theoretical foundations and geometric formalization, representation learning, robust perception and geometric state estimation,  robot policy learning and control.

Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

FLOW is a strong community of researchers engaged in fundamental and applied research in fluid mechanics within the department of Engineering Mechanics.

We are currently seeking an experimental PhD student in fluid mechanics to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group within FLOW. This position offers an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to contribute to a cutting-edge research program funded by the Swedish Research Council (VR).

The project aims to uncover how complex films, including biological and living films, interact with surrounding fluid flows. Such films are ubiquitous in nature and technological applications, ranging from mucus in the lungs to biofilms on medical devices and ship hulls. When exposed to shear and potentially unsteady flows, these films can deform into complex shapes, exhibit unusual material properties, and evolve over time, thereby creating a dynamic and continuously changing boundary for the flow. At the same time, the films modify the overlying flow, potentially altering frictional resistance as well as the transport and exchange of species.

Despite their importance, the coupled interaction between complex films and fluid flows remains poorly understood. This limits our ability to predict and control these systems and poses major challenges across medical, industrial, and geophysical applications.

In this project, the PhD student will work with and further develop a unique experimental platform for studying complex films under controlled, yet complex, flow conditions. The experimental work will be complemented by continuum modeling of complex materials, data-driven methods, and computational fluid dynamics.

Supervision: Shervin Bagheri is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission

Admission requirements

jobs.title: PhD student in experimental nuclear physics with a focus on nuclear fission and gamma-ray emission
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with experimental nuclear physics, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Division of Applied Nuclear Physics, at Uppsala University conducts research and education in applied nuclear physics. Its activities aim to deepen our understanding of the properties of atomic nuclei and apply this knowledge in areas such as energy and materials research.

The successful candidate will join an internationally active research group investigating nuclear-reaction dynamics and nuclear fission through experiments and modelling. Our research tests theoretical predictions and addresses fundamental questions relevant to nuclear physics and astrophysics. It also produces high-precision nuclear data for applications in nuclear-energy systems, cancer treatment, and radiation-tolerant microelectronics. The group collaborates with leading research facilities across Europe.

This doctoral project forms part of a Nordic collaboration between Uppsala University and the University of Oslo (UiO), within the Norwegian Nuclear Research Centre (NNRC). It brings together expertise in nuclear fission, nuclear structure, gamma-ray spectroscopy, detector development, and nuclear modelling. A substantial part of the experimental work will take place at the Oslo Cyclotron Laboratory (OCL).


Duties

The doctoral project will ultimately investigate how excitation energy and angular momentum are shared between fission fragments and subsequently carried away by gamma-ray emission. You will measure prompt fission gamma-ray spectra, multiplicities, and total energies as functions of excitation energy, and attempt to extract fission-product yields and isomeric yield ratios. These measurements will test our understanding of nuclear fission and provide data to improve predictions of gamma-ray heating and other fission observables relevant to Generation IV reactors operating with fast neutron spectra.

You will prepare and conduct experiments at OCL in close collaboration with researchers and technical specialists at UiO. The experiments will use the uranium-235(d,pf) reaction as a surrogate for neutron-induced fission of uranium-235. Detecting the outgoing proton together with fission fragments and gamma rays will allow the measured observables to be related to the excitation energy of the fissioning nucleus.

A central part of your work will be centered around the OSCAR gamma-ray detector array, charged-particle detectors, and a newly developed fission chamber. You will contribute to detector characterisation, calibration, commissioning, and optimisation of the experimental setup.

You will analyse the experimental data using coincidence techniques, detector-response corrections, background subtraction, and uncertainty analysis. Characteristic gamma-ray transitions will be used to identify selected fission products, while delayed emission will provide complementary information about fragment angular momentum through isomeric yield ratios.

The project also includes computational fission modelling in close collaboration with the nuclear data section at the International atomic energy agency. Using TALYS and fission models such as FREYA and GEF, you will assess how well current calculations describe energy sharing, angular momentum, and fragment de-excitation. Comparisons with the measurements will help identify model limitations and guide further development.

The position involves extended research visits to Oslo and may include detector tests and experiments at other international facilities. You will present your research in peer-reviewed publications, at scientific conferences, and in collaboration meetings.


Requirements

Applicants must meet the general eligibility requirements for doctoral studies through one of the following:

  • Hold a Master’s degree in physics, engineering physics, nuclear engineering, applied physics, or another subject relevant to the project;
  • or Have completed at least 240 higher education credits, including at least 60 credits at Master’s level and an independent project of at least 15 credits;
  • or Have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge through other studies or professional experience.

The position also requires:

  • An interest in physics, experimental work, data analysis, and physical modelling.
  • The ability to work independently and systematically, with attention to data quality.
  • Good collaboration skills.
  • Good oral and written communication skills in English.
  • Willingness and ability to undertake research visits abroad, particularly to Oslo, and participate in experimental campaigns and scientific conferences.


Additional qualifications

Desired qualifications that will be used in the ranking of the candidates:

  • Good knowledge of physics, including nuclear physics and radiation detection.
  • Programming experience, for example in Python or C++, and an interest in developing your scientific-computing skills.
  • Gamma-ray spectroscopy, coincidence measurements, or nuclear-fission experiments. Radiation detectors, detector electronics, or data-acquisition systems.
  • Experimental data analysis using ROOT or comparable tools.
  • Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport and detector response, for example using Geant4.
  • Nuclear-reaction or fission calculations using TALYS, FREYA, GEF, or related codes.
  • Statistical analysis, uncertainty propagation, or detector-response unfolding.
  • Scientific computing involving large experimental or simulated datasets.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

  • Please attach your transcript of records, a copy of or link to your degree project, and any other supporting documents you wish you rely on in your application.
  • We also welcome applications from candidates who have not yet completed their master’s thesis, however the eligibility requirements must be completed at the time of employment.

PhD student in meteorology- statistics and dynamics of compound climate extremes

Are you interested in working on the statistics and dynamics of compound climate extremes, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a doctoral position at Uppsala University.

The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden´s most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues.

Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development.

Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland.

Our six research divisions:

Geophysics • Air, Water and Landscape Science • Mineralogy, Petrology and Tectonics • Natural Resources and Sustainable Development • Palaeobiology • Wind Energy

For more information see: www.uu.se/earthsciences

The Programme for Air, Water, and Landscape Science encompasses education and research in meteorology, hydrology, environmental analysis, and physical geography. More information on the programme’s science can be found at: LUVAL.

You will work within the frame of the ERC grant ”DYnamical drivers, predictability and trends of compound CLimate EXtremes” (DYCLEX).

Duties

The project focuses on quantitative analyses of mid-latitude compound climate extremes in recent and future climates. You will work on connecting atmospheric dynamics and circulation features to the occurrence of different surface compound extremes, and use this understanding to explore event predictability and long-term trends. Teaching/supervising duties up to 20% are possible on a voluntary basis. You will be based at the Dept. of Earth Sciences in Uppsala, but will be expected to travel both nationally and internationally.

Requirements

You should show a solid knowlegde of programming for data analysis and demonstrate excellent spoken and written communication skills in English. We further require good cooperation skills as the work involves collaborations with different research groups internationally.

Additional qualifications

Knowledge of atmospheric dynamics, a strong background in statistics and past experience of analysing large amounts of climate data and work on physical drivers of climate extremes are a merit. We also value positively experience in the non-academic sector.

jobs.title: PhD student in Recycling of Solid Electrolytes for All-Solid-State Batteries
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Disciplinary Domain of Science and Technology, Faculty of Chemistry, Department of Chemistry - Ångström Laboratory
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's six programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. Department of Chemistry Ångström Laboratory

The Department of Chemistry – Ångström Laboratory has for many years hosted an environment focused on research and development of materials and their applications within the energy storage area: the Ångström Advanced Battery Centre. We develop novel electrode and electrolyte materials, characterize them, evaluate and improve them with respect to battery performance, and study fundamental chemical processes and properties using both experimental and computational techniques. The research is, as such, both fundamental and applied

Duties 
The project  aims to establish a scientific basis for the recycling of solid electrolytes used in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). The project is a collaboration between Uppsala University, KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Université de Lorraine in France, combining expertise in solid-state chemistry, battery materials, hydrometallurgy, purification and crystallization.The project focuses on lithium halide solid electrolytes, an emerging class of materials with high ionic conductivity and promising electrochemical stability. The central goal is to understand how the recycling process and impurities introduced during battery operation and recycling influence the structure, ionic transport and electrochemical performance of resynthesized solid electrolytes. The results will be used to establish precursor quality specifications for closed-loop recycling of solid-state battery materials.

The doctoral student will be based at Uppsala University and will work across the different stages of the recycling process. Key duties include synthesis and structural characterization of lithium-containing halide solid electrolytes, preparation and characterization of solid-state battery cells, ionic transport measurements using impedance spectroscopy, and investigation of the influence of impurities on material and cell performance.

The candidate will also participate in the development and evaluation of recycled precursor materials produced through hydrometallurgical processing. A research stay at Université de Lorraine in France, where the candidate will work on leaching and purification processes, is an integral part of the project. The candidate will also collaborate with researchers at KTH on crystallization and synthesis of purified precursor materials.

The work will involve a combination of synthesis, structural and chemical characterization, electrochemical measurements, data analysis and interpretation. Particular emphasis will be placed on establishing quantitative relationships between precursor composition, impurity content, crystal structure, ionic transport and battery performance.

The duties may also include:

  • Planning and performing air- and moisture-sensitive synthesis of inorganic solid electrolytes
  • Structural and chemical characterization using techniques such as powder X-ray diffraction, SEM-EDS and XPS
  • Ionic transport characterization using temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy
  • Assembly and electrochemical testing of solid-state battery cells
  • Analysis and interpretation of experimental data
  • Research visits to collaborating institutions in Sweden and France
  • Supervision of degree projects
  • Data analysis and dissemination of research results through scientific publications and conference presentations
  • Teaching at first and second cycle level
  • Administration linked to the tasks above

Requirements 
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must

  • been awarded a second-cycle degree in Chemistry, Physics, Materials Science, or equivalent/another relevant field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • acquired essentially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

The candidate must have:

  • very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • good organizational and time-management skills.
  • good collaborative skills and the ability to work independently.
  • a strong interest in materials chemistry, solid-state chemistry, energy storage or related fields.
  • experience with experimental laboratory work in chemistry, materials science or a related field.
  • experience with data analysis and scientific writing..

Experience in hydrometallurgy, leaching, solvent extraction or crystallization is considered advantageous but is not required. The project provides the opportunity to develop expertise in these areas through collaboration with KTH and Université de Lorraine.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant’s experience and skills complement and strengthen ongoing research within the department, and how they stand to contribute to its future development of research on solid-state batteries and circular battery materials.

Additional qualifications 

Experience with battery assembly and electrochemical testing, inorganic synthesis, powder diffraction, or solid-state ionic transport is desirable. Previous experience with air- and moisture-sensitive materials is particularly relevant to the project.

PhD student in Geophysics: Enhancing exploration drilling efficiency through integrated analyses rock formation and drilling data

Are you interested in working with sustainable and responsible exploration drilling of critical raw materials, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden's most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues.

Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development.

Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland.

Our six research divisions:

  • Geophysics • Air, Water and Landscape Science • Mineralogy, Petrology and Tectonics
  • Natural Resources and Sustainable Development • Palaeobiology • Wind Energy

For more information see: www.uu.se/earthsciences

Geophysics is about "looking into" and understanding the Earth’s structure, its history and processes-based on measurements of the Earth’s physical properties. In geophysics we use quantitative physical methods to investigate the Earth and its environment. In addition, physical property measurements, rock mechanical field testing, scientific drilling and numerical modelling are employed to investigate the subsurface structures and processes. The Geophysics program currently runs several national and international projects and has a wealth of world-class infrastructures. It also leads the Smart Exploration Research Center (SERC) (www.smartexploration.se). SERC is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, with members from four Swedish universities, three mining companies, four technology companies, and one development company. The PhD project will be conducted in close collaboration with Epiroc, Nordic Iron and Lund University.

In this PhD project, you will be enrolled as a PhD student at Uppsala University in close collaboration with Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro. You will mainly be placed at Uppsala University, Uppsala. During shorter periods, you will also be placed at Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro and participate if field work.

Access to certain technology or data associated with industry partners within the project may be subject to applicable export control legislation and will be managed in accordance with current regulations.

Duties

The PhD candidate will conduct research within SERC, focusing on sustainable and responsible exploration of critical raw materials. The overarching aim of the PhD project is to develop a framework for integrating rock formation and drilling data to improve exploration drilling efficiency, thereby contribute to more sustainable and responsible exploration drilling.

The project combines geoscience and drilling technology, with a focus on diamond core drilling in crystalline rock. The PhD candidate will develop advanced theoretical, technical and practical expertise in the technical and operational challenges of the drilling process, as well as geoscientific methods for subsurface characterization.

The work involves data acquisition in connection with exploration drilling, borehole logging, in-situ testing, drill core analyses, and laboratory testing. Separate and integrated analyses of these datasets will be used to investigate potential relationships between rock formation properties, drilling data, and exploration drilling efficiency. 

The doctoral student  will work in close collaboration with academic and industry research groups contributing to stronger collaboration and knowledge exchange between these communities. The PhD candidate is expected to combine theoretical and practical work, work both independently and collaboratively, spend parts of the project period with industry partners, and participate in field and laboratory work.

Requirements

To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in geophysics, geology, rock mechanics, drilling technology, physics, earth sciences or a similar field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

We are seeking a candidate with strong interests in exploration drilling in crystalline rocks and methods for subsurface characterisation, both in-situ and in the laboratory. Good oral and written proficiency in English is required.

Additional qualifications

Experience in various types of data acquisition and analysis, such as measurement while drilling (MWD), logging while drilling (LWD), borehole logging, rock stress measurements, drill core logging, and rock mechanic laboratory testing, is considered a merit. Experience in integrating and analysing different types of drilling data, rock formation data, or a combination of these is also considered a merit. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively is considered a merit. Proficiency in spoken and written Swedish is a merit, because communication in Swedish may be required during fieldwork and collaboration with industry partners. A driving license is a merit, as it may be required for fieldwork.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines. A PhD position is full-time for four years. Teaching or administrative duties at the department corresponding to a maximum of 20 per cent may occur by agreement. The employment is extended to a corresponding extent.

jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry - Ångström conducts research and education in the chemistry field. The department has more than 270 employees and has a turnover of 300 million SEK. At the department's six programs, we conduct very successful research of a high international standard. We have a large number of externally funded research projects, often with international cooperation and we see continued good growth in our subject area. The department has education assignments in engineering programs and master's programs. More information is available on our website. www.uu.se/en/department/chemistry-angstrom-laboratory?languageld=1

Duties
The research is related to perovskite solar cells (PSCs), a novel photovoltaic technology that has quickly reached efficiencies as high as that of silicon. PSCs are, however, much easier and cheaper to produce. Unfortunately, their stability is still insufficient. Ion conductivity in the material could be the main reason. In this project the PhD student will investigate the ion conductivity in perovskite thin films and solar cells and determine its effect on performance and stability. Furthermore, strategies to control ion conductivity in perovskites will be developed.

The PhD student will prepare perovskite films and solar cells in different configurations using wet-chemical deposition methods. Along with vapor-deposited films and solar cell devices from our collaborator, these will be investigated, using electrochemical techniques and advanced spectroscopies. This project is done within the consortium SOLVE - Solar Electricity Research Centre, Sweden (https://www.uu.se/en/research/solve).

The main duties of doctoral students are to devote themselves to their research studies, which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20%). The PhD student should design, plan, perform the experimental work, as well as critically analyze and discuss the results, initially with close guidance by the supervisor. As the PhD students develop, they are expected to become more independent in taking the initiative and planning the research. The students are expected to participate actively in workshops and to present their results at scientific conferences as well as in scientific peer-reviewed journals.
