jobs.title: Doctoral student in mathematics education
jobs.department: Karlstad University / Faculty of Health, Science and Technology / Department of Mathematics and Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Are you a practicing teacher or a teacher education graduate with an interest in how teaching can be developed based on research? Would you like to further specialise in your subject while contributing to school development? Then a doctoral studentship within the graduate school BEPPE might be the next step in your professional career.

Karlstad University is now accepting applications for a doctoral studentship at the graduate school BEPPE. The doctoral student will be employed at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science.

The graduate school on subject-specific education models in primary school (BEPPE)

The graduate school BEPPE aims to contribute to more systematic knowledge about how several scientifically established, yet mutually distinct, subject-specific education models function across different subjects and school contexts, and how they can be integrated into teacher education and primary education. As a doctoral student, you will conduct research on applied teaching practices in primary school, with a close connection to teacher education and school practice.

The graduate school is jointly organised by Karlstad University and the University of Gothenburg and currently has a total of nine doctoral students.

We welcome applications from teacher educators, schoolteachers, and from those who are otherwise interested in conducting research on teaching and learning within the advertised areas of specialisation. Applicants can be at an early stage of their careers – the key point is an interest in teaching, learning and school development in interaction with research. BEPPE offers a dynamic environment with opportunities to establish international networks, participate in conferences and engage in exchange programmes abroad. More information about the graduate school and its research (in Swedish): BEPPE.

Subject environments

The graduate school is a part of Karlstad University’s research environment focusing on subject-specific education. The research environment includes ROSE (Research on Subject-specific Education) and three research centres: CSL (Centre for Language and Literature Education), CSD (Centre for Social Science Didactics ) and SMEER (Science, Mathematics and Engineering Education Research). The subject-specific education perspective involves a particular interest in teaching and learning within specific subjects or subject areas. As a doctoral student in mathematics education, you will be affiliated with SMEER.

Duties

As a doctoral student, you will primarily dedicate time to your own studies. The doctoral programme comprises 240 credits for a Degree of Doctor and 120 credits for a Degree of Licentiate. The doctoral appointment is a paid position that offers a combination of studies and work, and a great opportunity for a potential career in academia. Doctoral students are expected to work independently and be prepared to contribute to the activities and development of the discipline and the department. You are given the opportunity to deepen your interests in collaboration with others. Teaching and administrative duties may also be included upon agreement but will not constitute more than 20% of full-time. Work as a doctoral student allows for great freedom and flexibility in terms of how you organise your tasks. This requires commitment, drive, and the ability to structure your work to successfully complete the doctoral thesis.

To contribute to a positive work environment and further both the department's activities and your own development as a researcher, we expect you to be a present and active part of the day-to-day operations and workplace community, whether working remotely or on site.

Entry requirements and admission

To be eligible for a doctoral studentship, applicants must meet the general and specific entry requirements (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 7, Sect. 35).

To meet the general entry requirements, applicants must have been awarded a second-cycle qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 7, Sect. 39).

To meet the specific entry requirements for third-cycle education in mathematics with a specialisation in mathematics education, the applicant must hold a Degree of Master (60 or 120 credits) that includes courses in mathematics and mathematics education corresponding to at least 90 credits, including a degree project (independent project) of at least 15 credits with relevance to third-cycle education, alternatively have a Bachelor or Master of Education, or equivalent qualifications according to previous programme requirements, with a specialisation in mathematics.

An applicant can also meet the specific entry requirements by in some other way having acquired equivalent prerequisite knowledge, in Sweden or abroad. Applicants who have not completed 90 credits in mathematics but have acquired equivalent prior knowledge in another way may be subject to an equivalence assessment.

To be eligible for doctoral studies, applicants must also be considered to have the ability required to benefit from the programme (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 7, Sect. 35). Admission is based on individual assessment.

Assessment criteria

The assessment of eligible applicants is based on the criteria listed below.

Special weight will be given to:

  • Results from previous studies
  • The quality of independent written work of a scholarly and investigatory nature included in the previous studies, particularly at master’s level and within mathematics education
  • Completed teacher education or other pedagogical education of similar scope, as well as experience as a teacher
  • At least 2 years of professional experience as a teacher, including mathematics education

Considerable weight will be given to:

  • Research plan and its relevance to the focus areas of the graduate school
  • The extent to which the applicant is able to be a physically present and active member of the research environment of the subject
  • Personal qualities such as the ability to work independently, demonstrate strong collaboration skills, a structured approach and effective oral communication

Weight will be given to:

  • Proficiency in Swedish and English (the doctoral studies will be conducted in a Swedish context, and data may include spoken and written content in Swedish)

Terms

Upon admission to doctoral studies, the person will be offered the appointment of doctoral student (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 5, Sect. 3). The position comprises four years of full-time studies consisting of research only. If teaching or other departmental duties become relevant, the appointment will be extended by a corresponding period, up to a maximum of five years full-time. The position is fixed-term, one year initially, followed by possible extensions of a maximum of two years at a time (Higher Education Ordinance, Chap. 5). Start date as agreed by both parties.

The salary for the doctoral studentship corresponds to the standard level of salary for doctoral students and progresses in accordance with a local collective agreement.

Application

Submit the application via the University’s web-based recruitment tool, Varbi. Applicants are responsible for submitting a complete application in accordance with the advertisement, for providing translations of any documents written in a language other than Swedish, Norwegian, Danish or English, and for ensuring that the documentation allows for objective and qualitative assessments. A complete application should be submitted by the application deadline. An incomplete application may jeopardise a fair assessment of qualifications. The application should include:

  • A cover letter where the applicant details the reasons behind their interest in the position
  • Brief research plan: The plan should include problem statement, purpose, theory and method, and will serve as a basis for assessing suitability for doctoral studies (1,000-2,500 words). However, it does not necessarily have to be linked to the future research project.
  • An account of language skills
  • A list of qualifications (CV)
  • Degree certificate with a complete transcript of the courses included, or a certified list of completed courses with grades and dates
  • Copy of master’s thesis (60 or 120 credits) or similar
  • Where applicable, copies of publications or certificates for other qualifications
  • Any letters of recommendation
  • Two references, such as a teacher, supervisor, or former or current manager

Attach all the documents and publications you wish to be considered to the electronic application (do not just provide links). Name each uploaded document to clearly indicate its content.

Documents that cannot be submitted electronically should be sent to the following address:

Karlstads universitet
HR-avdelningen
HR-administratör
651 88 KARLSTAD
SWEDEN

Application deadline: November 1, 2026

State the reference number: REK2026/230

Applicants with qualifications from abroad

If you have qualifications from a university outside Sweden or if they have not been recognised by a Swedish authority before, it is important that you attach degree certificates and official transcripts to facilitate the recognition of foreign qualifications.
Provide a contact for the degree-awarding institution (phone number or email) who can verify your qualifications.

We look forward to your application!

Karlstad University has chosen advertising channels for this recruitment and firmly declines any contact with advertising or recruitment agencies.

jobs.title: Doctoral Student in Psychology
jobs.department: Department of Psychology and Social work
jobs.description_html:
Job description
The research project is at the intersection of social psychology and sociolinguistics, examining how accents function as social signals. The focus is on social perception, attitudes, emotions, and behaviours related to foreign accents.

The research addresses questions of stereotypes, discrimination, and social inclusion from a Swedish and international perspective, with a consistent gender perspective throughout. The project is interdisciplinary and connects to work and organisational psychology, political science, gender studies, and research on integration and belonging.

Methodologically, the project is primarily based on experimental studies and psychometric approaches, with the possibility of applying neuroscientific methods as well.

The position is within the Department of Psychology, which is characterised by a close and personal environment with strong collegial support. The doctoral student will be part of an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented research environment and will work in close collaboration with supervisors, with considerable emphasis on developing independence in planning, implementation, and scientific communication. In the later stages of the dissertation, the doctoral student may have the possibility to design their own sub-study within the project's overarching themes.

The position involves doctoral studies, comprising research (80%) and teaching and administrative work (20%). The primary duties consist of conducting supervised research leading to a doctoral dissertation. The position also includes completing 60 higher education credits in doctoral courses, as well as participating in seminars and other activities within the subject area and the department. 

 

Entry requirements
General entry requirements include a second-cycle level qualification, or fulfilment of courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits must be at second-cycle level, or the equivalent knowledge gained in some other way in Sweden or abroad. Specific entry requirements include at least 90 credits in the subject of psychology or the equivalent knowledge gained in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

 

Other Requirements
Strong English skills, both spoken and written, are required. Good knowledge of Swedish or another Scandinavian language (Norwegian or Danish) is an asset.

The applicant must be driven and independent, analytical, initiative-taking, collaborative, development-oriented, and persistent.

Higher education at the advanced level in psychology, as well as prior experience in the project's research area, are assets for the position. Experience in developing or validating psychometric tools, working with EEG/ERP or other neuroscientific methods, and knowledge of tools such as R, MATLAB, or Python are also considered assets. A scientific publication or manuscript in progress may be considered an asset, particularly if it relates to the project's research area.

 

Assessment criteria
Selection among eligible applicants is made on the basis of an overall assessment of the applicant's ability to successfully complete a doctoral education. The assessment will place particular emphasis on the scientific quality of independent degree projects, the project plan submitted with the application, the applicant's personal qualities, and the applicant’s understanding of and interest in the project's research area.

 

Employment process
Processing of the appointment will comply with the provisions in Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (Högskoleförordningen, SFS 1993:100) and will be carried out in accordance with Mid Sweden University’s Employment Procedures.

 

Terms of employment 
The doctoral position corresponds to five years of employment and is expected to lead to a doctoral degree. In addition to doctoral studies, which comprise 80% of the full-time position, teaching and administrative work will make up the remaining 20%, making it equivalent to a full-time post. If the pace of study in doctoral education changes, the employment period will be adjusted accordingly.

Initial doctoral student positions are valid for a maximum of one year, after which the position may be renewed by no longer than two years at a time. Provisions regarding doctoral studentship employment can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1-7. 

Start date: 2027-01-15 or as agreed

Place of employment: Östersund

Salary: In accordance with Mid Sweden University’s salary scale for doctoral student.

 

Information
For more information, contact the Head of department, Ulrika Danielsson, ulrika.danielsson@miun.se or 010-142 84 90, or the Project leader, Marie-France Champoux-Larsson, marila@miun.se or 010-142 85 38.

 

Application
Application documents must be submitted in Swedish or English.

A cover letter, CV, proof of completed degrees, undergraduate and advanced level theses, a project plan, and any scientific publication/manuscript in progress should be attached to the application.

The project plan (approx. 2 – 3 single-spaced pages excluding references) should present a possible research project within the scope of the position’s research area and must include a background to the research area, one or more research questions, a description of methods and research design, and a brief discussion of the project's relevance to the position. The project plan does not need to correspond to the final dissertation project, but is intended to give the applicant the opportunity to demonstrate their ability for scientific reasoning, research design, and critical thinking.

Qualifications cited in the application must be substantiated.

Please submit your application through our recruitment system no later than 2026-11-22.

jobs.title: PhD position: High-Throughput Development of Chemical Conversion Treatment for Light Metals
jobs.description_html: Cutting-edge Research for a Changing World PhD position: High-Throughput Development of Chemical Conversion Treatment for Light Metals JobID: 1077 Location: Geesthacht Application deadline: 03 November, 2026 Aluminium and magnesium alloys are key to lighter vehicles, aircraft, drones and consumer goods but only if they are safe and durable, reliably protected against corrosion. Chemical conversion coatings are one of the most effective and commercially successful ways to do this. They protect the metal and help paint adhere to it. Yet finding better, environmentally friendly formulations is still largely a matter of trial and error. The number of possible formulations is virtually infinite, so we do not test them one by one. At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data, we run a robotic high-throughput testing platform combined with machine learning for AI-assisted discoveries. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a PhD student in the quickly developing field of high-throughput and robotic experimentation in materials science. The position is part-time (19,5 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg). We value diversity and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply. Your tasks Develop and validate experimental methods for the accelerated screening of chemical conversion treatment formulations Translate these methods into automated high-throughput workflows on our existing robotic testing platform Work side by side with our computational scientists to build large, machine-readable datasets for AI-assisted discovery Uncover the mechanisms behind effective adhesion promotion and corrosion protection, and turn them into design rules for next-generation coatings Publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports, and contribute to open, FAIR datasets Your profile A completed master's degree in chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, computational materials science or a related field Solid experimental skills in chemical laboratories and confidence in quantitative data analysis using appropriate software Experience with corrosion protection, including chemical conversion coatings for light alloys (Mg, Al or Zn) Experience with electronic lab notebooks, FAIR data, databases or machine learning Curiosity about automation and AI, and motivation to work at the interface of experiment and computation Very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learning Content-related enquiries regarding this position can be directed to Sviatlana.Lamaka@hereon.de. Our offer A research topic with real industrial relevance, at the frontier of lab automation and Al-driven materials discovery A doctorate awarded by Hamburg University of Technology, TUHH, our partner university Access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure Access to a large international research and industrial network Funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays An exciting job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations International Welcome Office with guest accommodation 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day Social benefits according to the collective agreement of the public service and remuneration up to EG 13 (according to EntgO Bund) Very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible work A green campus on the Elbe River, well-connected with Hamburg (public transport), subsidy for the Deutschlandticket if certain conditions are met (job ticket), charging facilities for electric vehicles PhD Buddy Program Family-friendly company policy with childcare facilities, e.g. nursery/kindergarten close to the company Operational Health Management, e.g. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Corporate Benefits A varied offer in the canteen on campus Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon The Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon conducts cutting-edge international research for a changing world: Around 1,000 employees contribute to the tackling of climate change, the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range. Institute of Surface Science The Institute of Surface Science specializes in the development of corrosion protection concepts and functional coatings that meet the requirements of future applications from the fields of structural lightweight construction, energy research and medical technology. The experimental development is closely accompanied by modelling approaches and artificial intelligence methods. Interested? Then we are looking forward to receiving your comprehensive application documents (cover letter, CV, transcripts, certificates, etc.) indicating the reference number 1077 until 03 November, 2026. Apply now Severely disabled persons and those equaling severely disabled persons who are equally suitable for the position will be considered preferentially within the framework of legal requirements. Max-Planck-Straße 1 21502 Geesthacht www.hereon.de

jobs.title: PhD position in inverse modelling of greenhouse gases and radioactivity in the atmosphere (4 years)
jobs.description_html:
Job description:

The University of Vienna is a community of almost 11,000 individuals, including approximately 7,700 academic staff members, who passionately pursue answers to the profound questions that shape our future. They represent individuals driven by curiosity and a relentless pursuit of excellence. With us, they find the space to try things out and unfold their potential. Are you inspired by their passion and determination? We are currently seeking a

PhD position in inverse modelling of greenhouse gases and radioactivity in the atmosphere (4 years)

53 Faculty of Earth Sciences, Geography and Astronomy
Startdate: 01.12.2026 | Working hours: 30 | Collective bargaining agreement: §48 VwGr. B1 Grundstufe (praedoc)

Reference no.: 6309

Explore and teach at the University of Vienna, where more than 7,700 academics thrive on curiosity in continuous exploration and help us better understand our world. Does this sound like you? Then join our accomplished team!

Your personal sphere of influence:

The research group “Atmospheric Transport Processes,” led by Prof. Andreas Stohl, is part of the Department of Meteorology and Geophysics. The group develops the Lagrangian transport model FLEXPART and studies all aspects of transport in the atmosphere, ranging from greenhouse gases to pollutants, water vapour and heat, and uses inverse modelling techniques to determine sources of greenhouse gases, radionuclides, or air pollutants.


To learn more about our team, we invite you to visit our website: https://flexteam.univie.ac.at/. To learn more about FLEXPART, visit https://www.flexpart.eu/.

In the framework of the research association VINAR (Vienna Network for Atmospheric Research) with the Austrian weather service, Geosphere Austria, we have a PhD position available in our group. 

We seek a highly motivated PhD student, who will carry out Lagrangian transport model simulations with FLEXPART, and apply inverse methods to determine the emissions of greenhouse gases and/or radionuclides into the atmosphere. The PhD student will be involved in ongoing and future research projects conducted jointly by the University of Vienna and Geosphere Austria, as well as with other collaboration partners.

Your future tasks:

While the focus of the PhD study will be discussed with the successful candidate, possible tasks will be:

  • Quantify greenhouse gas emissions (e.g., of methane or carbon dioxide) based on flux, concentration or remote sensing measurements of these gases;
  • Quantify emissions of radionuclides (e.g., Cs-137) released from historic nuclear weapons tests and accidents in nuclear power plants based on available atmospheric concentration as well as deposition data;
  • Further develop the Lagrangian transport model FLEXPART as required for these applications;
  • Further develop the inverse modelling techniques used for constraining emissions into the atmosphere;
  • Publish your scientific results in peer-reviewed journals;
  • Teach classes within our bachelor or master programs in Meteorology (independently / within the scope of the provisions of the collective bargaining agreement);
  • Strengthen the collaborative culture of our team and the Department;
  • Become an active member of the Vienna International School of Earth and Space Sciences (VISESS / doctoral school).

This is part of your personality:

  • Completed master or diploma in the atmospheric sciences (e.g., meteorology, climatology), or a related field;
  • Strong programming skills;
  • Data analysis and interpretation experience;
  • A good team spirit and willingness to collaborate;
  • Very good command of the English language.

These skills would be an advantage:

  • Experience with Lagrangian transport models;
  • Expert knowledge of programming, preferably in Python and/or Fortran;
  • Experience with space-industry based emissions and their impact on the atmosphere.

What we offer:

VISESS doctoral school: You will enroll in the Vienna International School of Earth and Space Sciences, which offers specific education and training events.

Work-life balance: You have flexible working hours and the option to partly work from home upon agreement.

Inspiring and supportive working atmosphere: You will be part of an international team in a healthy and fair working environment with excellent research infrastructure. You will not perform your work in isolation but collaborate with a strong research team.

Good public transport connections: Your workplace is easily accessible by public transport.

Internal further training & Coaching: Opportunity to deepen your skills on an ongoing basis. There are over 600 courses to choose from – free of charge.

Fair salary plus health care and social benefits: The basic salary of EUR 3.776,10 (on a full-time Basis) increases if we can credit professional experience and allows for a comfortable life in a vibrant city with affordable housing prices and quick access to the outdoors.

Get off to a great start in your new job: the Welcome Compass helps you settle into your new role at the University of Vienna and life in Vienna.

Equal opportunities for all: We welcome every additional/new personality to the team!

The University of Vienna aims to become carbon neutral by 2030: We fully support low-carbon options for travelling. 

The position as university assistant (predoctoral) is available from 01 December 2026. The latest starting date is 15 December 2026. The review of applications will begin on 1 November, 2026. The search will continue until the decision is made but we aim for a decision as soon as possible after that.

The employment duration is 4 years. Initially limited to 1.5 years, the employment relationship is automatically extended to 4 years if the employer does not terminate it within the first 12 months by submitting a non-extension declaration. 

It is that easy to apply:

  • With a short letter stating your interest in the position;
  • With your CV including a list of publications;
  • With contact details of two persons who could provide a recommendation upon request;
  • Via our job portal / Apply now -  button.

If you have any questions, please contact:

Andreas Stohl  

andreas.stohl@univie.ac.at

We look forward to new personalities in our team! 
The University of Vienna has an anti-discriminatory employment policy and attaches great importance to equal opportunities, the advancement of women and diversity. We place particular emphasis on enhancing women’s representation among the academic and general university staff, particularly in leadership roles, and therefore expressly encourage qualified women to apply. Given equal qualifications, preference will be given to female candidates.

jobs.title: Doctoral Students for the DIW Graduate Center PhD Program in Economics
jobs.institution: DIW Berlin - Deutsches Institut für Wirtschaftsforschung e.V.
jobs.description_html:
The DIW Graduate Center (GC) at the German Institute for Economic Research welcomes applications from highly qualified students from around the world to enroll in its structured doctoral program in Economics.

The goal of the DIW Graduate Center is to provide outstanding doctoral students with a research environment and a training structure that will allow their talents to fully develop. The program equips them with a deep understanding of economic and social processes while offering them the opportunity to apply their knowledge at the largest economic research institute in Germany.

We are looking for Doctoral Students for the DIW Graduate Center PhD Program in Economics The DIW Graduate Center offers a five-year program of in-depth training in Economics leading to a PhD from one of Berlin’s universities. Students will complete a rigorous coursework curriculum and receive on-the-job training in DIW Berlin’s research departments. Students' research may be theoretical or applied in nature. Most work at the GC, however, has a strong empirical component. The program also encourages funded internships at prestigious institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and government ministries, as well as research stays at renowned universities around the world.

The DIW Graduate Center offers five years of funding with a standard stipend of 1,650 euros per month in the first year and a work contract in subsequent years. After completing the first year, doctoral students will join one of the research departments at the institute.

Requirements: Applicants to our PhD program must hold a master’s degree or diploma in Economics. Applications may also be submitted while the degree is still in progress, provided it is completed before the program starts. Degrees from other related fields (such as statistics, quantitative social sciences, mathematics or engineering) may also fulfill requirements for the program if the applicant has a sufficient background in Economics.

Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English language proficiency unless they hold a degree from a university in an English-speaking country or can document at least one year of studies in an English-speaking degree program. A high score on the TOEFL or IELTS test is considered sufficient evidence of English proficiency. Knowledge of German is not required for a successful application, but students are encouraged to learn German and improve their language skills over the course of the program

Application and Information: We value diversity and therefore welcome all applications—regardless of gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic and social background.

Please apply only online through our application portal by January 15, 2027, quoting the reference number GC-1-26-Stip-e and include the following application documents:

  • Motivation letter (max. 2 pages) explaining your reasons for applying and briefly outlining your major research interests;
  • Detailed curriculum vitae (without photograph);
  • Two academic letters of recommendation, to be submitted directly by senior academics (e.g., professors, postdoctoral researchers) via our application site;
  • Copies of academic transcripts and other certificates;
  • Completed application form (can be found on our application site);
  • IELTS or TOEFL scores, if applicable;
  • GRE General Test – Test Taker Score Report (PDF), if applicable. Please also attach your GRE Test if you have already submitted it to the Institutional Account.
You can access the application portal via our GC website under application site.

Please note that only applications submitted through the application portal will be considered and that the application is to be completed in English.

Do you have any questions about this call for applications or the online application? You may find your question already answered on our GC website, particularly in the FAQ section of the application site — please take a look before contacting us.

If you still have questions after reviewing our GC website, please contact gradcenter@diw.de for content-related inquiries and recruiting@diw.de for technical questions regarding the online application.

Founded in 1925, DIW Berlin (the German Institute for Economic Research) is one of the leading economic research institutes in Germany. The Institute analyzes the economic and social aspects of topical issues, formulating and disseminating policy advice based on its research findings. DIW Berlin is part of both the national and international scientific communities, provides research infrastructure to academics all over the world, and promotes the next generation of scientists. A member of the Leibniz Association, DIW Berlin is independent and primarily publicly funded.

jobs.description_html: German Centre for Astrophysics Shape the future of science and the region with us! Shape the future of science and the region with us! The German Center for Astrophysics (DZA) is being established as a new large-scale research center in Lusatia, Germany. Its mission is to strengthen astrophysics in Germany, foster scientific excellence, and make a lasting contribution to the structural transformation of the region. As an internationally oriented research institution with a strong focus on innovation, the DZA will create new opportunities for scientific leadership while shaping the future of one of Germany's most dynamic research landscapes. Its goal is to enable solutions to urgent societal challenges, including communication, artificial intelligence, climate protection, and health, through modern electronic and photonic technologies. jobs.title: PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys
jobs.description_html: Cutting-edge Research for a Changing World PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys Reference code: 1057 - 2026/WD 1 Commencement date: as soon as possible Work location: Geesthacht Application deadline: November 12th, 2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. jobs.description_html:
At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating tofundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.

The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for two Research Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m) with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)
The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order istransformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules andinstitutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes theseprocesses as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating,reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutionalarrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how suchconstellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce,transform, or erode.

Job description The successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.

Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:
  • an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or
  • a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within aparticular field, such as security, economy, or technology
Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.

The doctoral researchers will:
  • develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;
  • conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;
  • contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;
  • participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;
  • present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;
  • contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.
Your profile
  • An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis
  • A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies
  • A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)
  • A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets
  • The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environm
We offer

  • A varied, responsible and team-orientated job
  • Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)
  • Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases
  • A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces
  • A job ticket for public transport
  • Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centres

The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.

Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearlyrelates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendation.

The documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early Decemberin person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expensescannot be covered.

jobs.title: Doctoral Researcher (m/f/d)

jobs.description_html: The newly founded Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science studies contemporary challenges to political, social, and economic life. The institute places special emphasis on the political dimension, thereby spanning the spectrum from political sociology through conflict and peace research to political economy. Rigor and imagination guide the institute’s analytical and empirical approach, which draws inspiration from cross-disciplinary developments. The institute aims to produce new, evidence-based insights for pressing challenges to policy and contemporary society. At the Institute, the Department of Political Institutions and Conflict is inviting applications for the position of Doctoral Researcher (m/f/d) (full-time for three years with a starting date of January 1, 2027). The newly established department “Political Institutions and Conflict” (led by Ursula Daxecker) studies the relationship between political institutions and conflict, broadly construed. Conflict is inherent in politics but can be managed peacefully or break out in the open and turn violent. Research in the department explores whether and how political, economic, and social institutions create or reduce the potential for conflict, how structural changes have changed institutions’ ability to manage conflict, and how these shifts affect political outcomes downstream. Through this research, the department aims to produce novel insights for important challenges in contemporary society, including the rise of extreme strategies and violence, threats to electoral integrity, and democratic erosion. The PhD candidate will be affiliated with the “Doctoral Network Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe (DIViNE)” project, funded by the HORIZON MSCA action. The candidate will be supervised by Dr. Ursula Daxecker. DIViNE brings together leading European research environments — UvA (Amsterdam), UESSEX (Essex), UMIL (Milan), UC3M (Carlos III de Madrid) and UU (Uppsala) — and partner organizations – including the new Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science — to combine complementary strengths in quantitative conflict research, behavioral and experimental methods, historical and archival inquiry, institutional and normative theory, and applied policy engagement. Responsibilities (what you will do): Democracies are commonly seen as able to channel contestation through institutionalized processes and nonviolent action. Yet, democratic politics frequently experience a broad range of political violence — from riots and organized electoral intimidation to extremist mobilization and criminal violence — and violence can test and, at times, erode democratic norms and institutions. Moreover, democracies themselves may respond to perceived threats with measures (e.g., militarized policing, emergency legislation, selective repression) that threaten to undermine core features of liberal democracy such as the rule of law, civil liberties and institutional impartiality. The DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe) consolidates comparative, historical, theoretical and methodological strands to build a coherent new research program on political violence in democracies. The position is part of WP3 on Dynamics of Support for Violent Movements and Responses, which focuses on the micro-foundations of public support for, and tolerance of, political violence, including how violent organizations cultivate legitimacy. The PhD project aims to explain variation in violent strategies across time and space, distinguishing between violent rhetorical and behavioral strategies. The project is also interested in understanding the relationship between rhetoric and behavior, and how both strategies shape outcomes downstream. Empirically, the project examines political violence in the Global North, aiming to conduct subnational, constituency-level analyses of violent strategies in Global North cases. The methodological approach makes uses of innovations to study sensitive topics and difficult-to-reach populations, such as shadowing, fieldwork, special survey techniques, and use of multimodal data. The project will generate policy-relevant knowledge on patterns of radicalization, public tolerance for violence, and the vulnerabilities of established democracies. The doctoral trajectory includes a secondment at the University of Amsterdam and Clingendael in the Netherlands, which will provide the PhD candidate with additional training and exposure to policy engagement and strategic communication on extremist threats. Specifically, you will: produce a doctoral thesis that will be defended at the University of Amsterdam’s Faculty of Social Sciences, with the goal of obtaining the degree of PhD. conduct PhD research on the dynamics of support for violent movements and responses, including quantitative analysis of data, surveys and survey experiments, and fieldwork interviews. co-author publications with other project members; carry out fieldwork and interviews in research locations; assist with administrative responsibilities related to the project, such as the organization of workshops, conferences, or other project events. take active part in DIViNE training network activities including network training modules, PhD colloquia, research workshops, secondments, and training workshops; be affiliated with and take active part in the research environment at the department and institute. Regular physical presence at the Institute is therefore required and researchers need to reside within commuting distance of Göttingen. We will assist with finding adequate housing and with applying for visas and residence permits. Requirements: You have the following credentials: Essential: a Master’s degree or equivalent in political science or closely related discipline. The degree must have been obtained by the start of your employment; an excellent command of social science research methods, including quantitative methodology such as panel regression, analysis of large administrative data, survey data, large language models and AI, causal inference design, and statistical programming in Stata/R/etc.; excellent oral and written communication skills in English; independent thinking and critical analytical skills; the ability to work independently and in a team. Desirable: experience with qualitative methods and mixed-methods approaches; interest and willingness to conduct fieldwork; expertise in research on political violence. What We Offer: The position is full-time and for a period of three years (with the option of up to two extensions of six months each). Salary is based on the German collective agreement for civil servants (TVöD Bund), pay group EG 13, 75%/​grade 1 – 2. The Max Planck Society is mainly funded by German Federal and State Governments (see www.mpg.de). Max Planck Institutes provide outstanding facilities, academic resources and intellectual environments for the support of independent research. Max Planck Institutes are not tied to universities. There are no teaching obligations for staff, but teaching and other forms of co-operation with universities are possible. The Max Planck Society wishes to increase the participation of women across the sciences. Applications from women are therefore particularly welcome. Following its commitment to equal opportunities employment policies, the Max Planck Society especially encourages applications from persons with a disability. Persons of any nationality can apply. Applications must be submitted online no later than Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Applications must consist of: a CV a two-page cover letter that outlines your preparation and motivation to pursue this degree a two-page proposal outlining a PhD project that fits the above parameters unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts the contact details of two academic references a writing sample of max. 10 pages (this can be an excerpt from longer written material). The deadline for applications is November 11, 2026. Additional materials such as recommendation letters will be requested only for shortlisted candidates. The selection committee expects interviews to take place in Göttingen in the week of November 23. We ask you to ensure availability this week. Queries should be directed to silvia.stoermer@ips.mpg.de. The Institute has been newly reestablished in 2026. Apply now! Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science Hermann-Föge-Weg 11 37073 Göttingen For information on the institute, please consult ips.mpg.de.

jobs.title: Research Associate / PhD Candidate (m/f/d) iMOL
jobs.institution: Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main
jobs.description_html: The Johann Wolfgang Goethe University Frankfurt am Main is one of the largest universities in Germany with around 41,000 students and with about 7,000 employees. Founded in 1914 by Frankfurt citizens and since 2008 once again proud of its foundation status Goethe University possesses a high degree of autonomy, modernity and professional diversity. As a comprehensive university, the Goethe University offers a total of 16 departments on five campuses and 159 degree programs along with an outstanding research reputation. Furthermore, the Goethe University is part of the Group of Rhine-Main-Universities (RMU). As part of the DFG Research Training Group iMOL (GRK 2566) at Goethe University Frankfurt, we are looking for creative and highly motivated candidates. iMOL connects advanced imaging with molecular life sciences. The doctoral program trains outstanding young researchers in cutting-edge microscopy and AI-driven image analysis, enabling them to investigate the principles of life across different spatial and temporal scales. A position is available starting on 01.03.2027 as Research Associate (m/f/d) PhD Candidate E 13 TV-G-U initially, the position is limited to a fixed term of three years. The salary grade is based on the job characteristics of the collective agreement applicable to Goethe University (TV-G-U). This position is also available on a part-time basis. Your responsibilities Preparation of medical and biological samples Preparation and application of next-generation microscopy techniques Computer-assisted acquisition and analysis of multidimensional imaging data Visualization of biological and medical samples Presentation and publication of research findings Your profile You hold a completed university degree (Master’s, Diploma, or State Examination) in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biophysics, Physics, Molecular Biology, Medicine, Computer Science or a related field and have a strong interest in microscopy. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Working with cells and organisms Light and electron microscopy Image processing, computer-assisted image analysis, and data evaluation We are looking for technical aptitude, an independent and careful approach to work, and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary collaboration. Good English language skills are an advantage due to our international research environment. Goethe University is committed to equal opportunity, family friendliness, and diversity. To strengthen the diversity of perspectives and lived experiences within the university, applications from individuals with a migration background and from members of other groups that have so far been underrepresented are particularly welcome. Applicants with a severe disability, or those legally equivalent, will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal suitability. If women are underrepresented in a faculty or administrative unit, they will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal qualifications. Interested? We look forward to receiving your application! Please submit your application documents (cover letter, detailed CV, academic transcripts, and a description of your research interests and motivation) as a single PDF file by November 30, 2026, via email to: Prof. Dr. Achilleas Frangakis, office.frangakis@biophysik.org For further information, please visit: https://imol.uni-frankfurt.de/apply/ Please note that the application documents will not be returned. Costs incurred during the application process will not be reimbursed by Goethe University. www.uni-frankfurt.de

jobs.title: PhD positions at the International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials
jobs.institution: Max-Planck-Institut für Chemische Physik fester Stoffe
jobs.description_html: The International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials is a joint PhD program between the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids in Dresden, Germany, Technische Universität Dresden and the University of St Andrews, Scotland. By working together, we create a highly attractive overall package of PhD‑level research on solid-state chemistry and condensed matter physics, building on world‐class research activities in quantum materials at the three institutions. PhD positions at the International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials Our program will provide successful candidates with a stimulating environment, in which they will have the opportunity to interact and work with world-leading scientists from the three sites and use our excellent infrastructure and facilities. Our research is generously funded and successful candidates will receive competitive payment based on the primary location of their research project. We seek to recruit multiple PhD students in 2027 for a range of inter‐institutional research projects in the broadly defined field of quantum materials. Research work will be combined with graduate courses and general skills training. Both experimental and theoretical projects are offered and a complete list of all projects is available on our website. Excellent candidates from any country are encouraged to apply. Applicants are expected to have an outstanding bachelor's or master's degree in a field of study that is well-aligned with our research activities. The IMPRS-CPQM places great importance on fostering a pleasant working atmosphere and encouraging friendly cooperation. We are committed to increasing the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. We have also set ourselves the goal of employing more people with severe disabilities. Your application Closing date for applications is November 30, 2026. Accepted candidates are expected to start their projects no later than September 2027. Apply now For more information, including application guidelines, please visit our website: https://imprs-cpqm.mpg.de

jobs.title: PhD Student Positions (f/m/x) Electron-Light Interaction in Silicon Photonic Nanostructures
jobs.description_html: At the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, we bridge the gap between basic research and technological advancement. Here, researchers from the fields of physics, chemistry, biology, and medicine collaborate across disciplines, supported by high-performance service facilities and a modern research infrastructure. As the largest institute of the Max Planck Society, with around 1,000 employees from more than 66 nations, we offer an inspiring, international working environment with exceptional scientific breadth. The Department of Ultrafast Dynamics (Prof. Dr. Claus Ropers) is inviting applications for two PhD Student Positions (f/m/x) – Electron-Light Interaction in Silicon Photonic Nanostructures – Study the interaction of free electrons with silicon nanostructures, including the investigation of quantum effects. Conduct scientific work at the emerging intersection of electron microscopy and quantum photonics. Primary emphasis is on ambitious experimental work using electron microscopes and silicon photonic structures. The MPI-NAT invites applications for two fully funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Candidate positions, within the Horizon Europe Doctoral Network QUEST – Quantum Electrodynamics with Silicon Nanotechnology (QuEST). QUEST brings together leading European universities, research institutes and innovative companies to advance quantum technologies through silicon nanotechnology. Within this network, you will be one of 15 doctoral candidates working on complementary research projects spanning semiconductor materials, nanofabrication, quantum photonics, quantum electrodynamics, advanced characterization and theoretical modelling. The two PhD candidates will conduct research in the above-mentioned scientific field, while focusing on different areas of specialization. Project 1 focuses on enhancing electron-light interactions in tailored nanostructures using flexible geometries and variable beam energies. Meanwhile, project 2 will explore hybrid devices that couple local quantum states to electron beams. One application applies to both projects simultaneously. If you have a preference, please indicate in your application which project interests you most. Candidates will be matched to a project based on qualifications, skills and their stated preference. Position details The selected PhD candidates will participate in the EU-funded HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN project QUEST, combining network-wide training activities with excellent research opportunities at MPI-NAT. You will be expected to work on your project in close collaboration with fellow PhD students in QUEST and with the other members of the Department of Ultrafast Dynamics. Together, you will explore, experimentally and theoretically, novel custom photonic devices tailored for efficient interactions with electron beams and solid-state quantum systems. In particular, this includes assisting the design and optical coupling of photonic structures, performing extended experiments in an electron microscope and complementing the results with numerical simulations. You are expected to communicate your results in the form of scientific publications and presentations at international conferences. As part of the GAUSS PhD program at the University of Göttingen, you will complete several PhD courses and participate in teaching as a teaching assistant. You will also attend regular meetings with other PhD students and partners in the doctoral network, including two training schools and two workshops. The duration of the stay in Göttingen (Germany) and the two secondments vary by project as follows: Project 1 is set to last a total of 36 months, which includes two 2-month secondments each to Copenhagen (Denmark) and Göttingen (Germany). Project 2 includes a 32-month stay in Göttingen and two 2-month secondments each to Copenhagen (Denmark) and Dresden (Germany), so that this project is also scheduled to last a total of 36 months. For the respective secondments, you are expected to relocate to the project partners. Your profile The ideal candidates for the positions are highly motivated and talented researcher holding a Master’s degree (MSc or equivalent) in physics, chemistry, or engineering, with an excellent academic record and preferably demonstrated scientific achievements. We are interested in working with candidates who are team-minded, reliable, self-driven and have demonstrated excellence in electron microscopy, nano-optics, integrated photonics or quantum optics during their Master's thesis (or equivalent). Other qualities of the successful candidates: Is academically curious and thinks deeply and creatively Takes responsibility for the progress and quality of the project Communicates well in both written and spoken English Is empathetic and enjoys working with others from diverse backgrounds The positions are subject to the mobility and eligibility rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie actions. In particular, the candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Germany for more than twelve months during the three years immediately prior to the recruitment date, unless as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention. At the date of recruitment, the candidates must be a Doctoral Candidate, i.e. in the first five years (full-time equivalent research experience) of their research career and must not have been awarded a doctoral degree. What we offer The successful candidates will receive a salary in accordance with the MSCA regulations for Doctoral Researchers. The salary includes a living allowance, a mobility allowance, and a family allowance (if applicable). The PhD funding is for 36 months. The two PhD positions are full-time with a 39-hour workweek and will start on 01/01/2027 or according to mutual agreement. We are committed to being a cosmopolitan institute that offers a diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities. We also aim to increase the number of employees with disabilities. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. For further questions, please inquire at the email address down below. Application Please submit your application by 1st November 2026, preferably via email as a single PDF file including a CV, motivation letter, copy of the Master’s degree (or proof of expected completion), Master's thesis (if available), contact information for at least two references and all academic transcripts to: ausschreibung26-26@mpinat.mpg.de Apply now Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences Department of Ultrafast Dynamics Prof. Dr. Claus Ropers and Dr. Armin Feist Am Faßberg 11 37077 Göttingen Germany www.mpinat.mpg.de/ropers Information pursuant to Article 13 DSGVO on the collection and processing of personal data during the application process can be found on our website below the respective job advertisement.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Cloud-Native and AI-Native 6G Networks
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about shaping next-generation mobile networks? If so, please continue reading!

Join us!
Software-defined and programmable networking is a key enabling technology for cloud-native and AI-native 6G networks, supporting greater scalability, flexibility, automation, and efficient resource utilization. Cross-layer and cross-domain programmability, across the control and data planes and from RAN to core, is expected to be a defining characteristic of 6G systems, which are currently being developed and standardized. In this context, data plane programming capabilities in next-generation mobile networks can bring significant benefits with regards to network slicing and multi-tenancy, dynamic traffic engineering, offloading network functions to hardware accelerators, etc.

Specifically, this PhD project, conducted in collaboration with Ericsson, the leading mobile communications equipment manufacturer, will investigate data-plane programmability in next-generation mobile networks, with a particular focus on cloud-native and AI-native Radio Access Networks (RAN). The candidate will investigate research challenges including, but not limited to, the specification and implementation of common abstraction layers for heterogeneous programmable data planes, mechanisms for data-plane multitenancy and modularization, and programmable radio resource management, with an emphasis on intelligent and adaptive control.

The research is conducted within the scope of the Future Network Services (FNS): the 6G flagship project for the Netherlands where 60 leading ICT businesses, mobile operators, semiconductor manufacturers and research institutions, have united to spearhead the development of specific aspects of 6G: Software antennas, AI-driven networking, and groundbreaking 6G applications.

You will be embedded in the MNS group. The group focuses its research on the fundamental architectural problems that arise from the interconnection of systems and of data flows. We look at the emerging architectures that can support the operations of the future Internet. More information can be found at: https://mns-research.nl/

Within Ericsson Hungary, your work will be anchored to the team in Ericsson's Research Area Networks, which drives innovations towards 6G and the future network platform. Our local competence and expertise are in Radio Network (RAN) and Packet Core architectures and protocols, programmable networks, and network automation. More information is available at https://www.ericsson.com/en/about-us/company-facts/ericsson-worldwide/hungary/research-ericsson-hungary

This is what you will do
Tasks and responsibilities:
  • focus on the development and evaluation of and end-to-end programmable data plane, supporting multitenancy and modularity, through the definition and implementation of a generic hardware abstraction layer, supporting heterogeneous systems e.g., GPUs, TPUs, FPGAs, SOCs.
  • Investigate optimization aspects of network control and data plane functionality.
  • develop appropriate proof of concept(s) to benchmark the performance or validate the applicability of proposed approaches;
  • access a unique state-of-the-art testbed to also put theory to practice and be at the forefront of the Dutch 6G national ecosystem;
  • become active in the research community and collaborate with other institutes and/or companies that are part of the project;
  • publish and present work regularly at international conferences, workshops, and journals;
  • contribute to teaching activities, including lab sessions, and assist in the supervision of Bachelor’s and Master’s students.

What we ask of you
Your experience and profile:
  • Master's degree or equivalent program (completed or near completion: see below) in a relevant discipline, such as computer science, electrical and computer engineering, security and network engineering etc.;
  • excellent programming skills (python, C/C++);
  • experience with cloud-native platforms, particularly Kubernetes, is an advantage.
  • experience in programmable networking technologies and DSLs such as eBPF and P4 is a plus;
  • knowledge in mobile network architectures and protocols is a plus;
  • the willingness to be part of an international research team;
  • fluency in oral and written English and good presentation skills;
  • commitment to maintaining an inclusive, collaborative, diverse, supportive work environment.

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,059 to € 3,881 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile Promovendus is applicable.. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

Curious about our extensive secondary benefits package? You can read more about it here.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

The mission of the Informatics Institute (IvI) is to perform curiosity-driven and use-inspired fundamental research in Computer Science. The main research themes are Artificial Intelligence, Computational Science and Systems and Network Engineering. Our research involves complex information systems at large, with a focus on collaborative, data driven, computational and intelligent systems, all with a strong interactive component.

The MultiScale Networked Systems (MNS) group) is part of the Informatics Institute at the University of Amsterdam. The group focusses its research on multiscale systems e.g. cloud systems or clusters that define themselves by their dynamic size and scale, and on the network connecting them. The MNS group explores the emerging architectures that can support emerging applications across the future internet.

Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the button. We accept applications until and including 15 November 2026

Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file):
  • a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience;
  • a letter of motivation;
  • a list of publications;
  • the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation.

A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure.
(for details: national knowledge security guidelines)

Only complete applications received within the response period via the link below will be considered.

jobs.title: Promovendus Governance, Vertrouwen en Data-gedreven Duurzaamheidstransities (0,8 - 1,0 fte)
jobs.description_html:
Hoe verandert besluitvorming wanneer data en digitale technologie een steeds grotere rol spelen in de verduurzaming van de landbouw? En wat is er nodig om nieuwe kennis en technologie daadwerkelijk bij ondernemers, overheden en andere maatschappelijke partijen te laten landen?

Dit ga je doen
Binnen het NWO-project SOLIDTREE zoekt het Instituut Bestuurskunde van de Universiteit Leiden een promovendus die onderzoek doet naar de bestuurlijke en maatschappelijke dimensies van een data-gedreven duurzaamheidstransitie in de laanbomenteelt.

De Nederlandse laanbomenteelt staat voor een complexe opgave. De sector moet verduurzamen en tegelijkertijd economisch levensvatbaar blijven. Binnen SOLIDTREE ontwikkelen onderzoekers en maatschappelijke partners nieuwe manieren om het bodemleven beter zichtbaar te maken en mee te nemen in beslissingen over bodembeheer. Daarbij wordt onder meer gewerkt aan een data-gedreven beslissingsondersteunend systeem.

Maar technologische innovatie leidt niet vanzelf tot verandering. Nieuwe vormen van kennis en besluitvorming roepen ook bestuurlijke vragen op. Wie vertrouwt welke data? Hoe verhouden wetenschappelijke kennis, professionele ervaring en lokale kennis zich tot elkaar? Welke institutionele en regulatoire barrières beïnvloeden de toepassing van nieuwe technologie? En hoe kunnen publieke en private partijen gezamenlijk bijdragen aan duurzamere praktijken?

Wat ga je onderzoeken?
Als promovendus ontwikkel je binnen de bredere doelstellingen van SOLIDTREE een eigen bestuurskundig onderzoeksproject. Mogelijke thema’s zijn onder andere:
  • vertrouwen en legitimiteit rond data-gedreven besluitvorming;
  • de manier waarop telers, overheden en andere actoren omgaan met verschillende vormen van kennis en expertise;
  • governance en institutionele barrières rond duurzame innovatie;
  • samenwerking tussen publieke, private en maatschappelijke organisaties;
  • de rol van digitalisering en data in duurzaamheidstransities;
  • de voorwaarden waaronder technologische innovaties daadwerkelijk worden opgenomen in beleid en praktijk.

Je combineert wetenschappelijk onderzoek met intensief contact met de praktijk. Je voert bijvoorbeeld interviews en casestudies uit, observeert samenwerking binnen het consortium en organiseert workshops of andere interactieve onderzoeksactiviteiten met betrokken partijen.
Samen met onderzoekers uit andere disciplines werk je aan een beter begrip van de ecologische, technologische én bestuurlijke voorwaarden voor duurzaam bodembeheer.

Een interdisciplinair onderzoeksproject
SOLIDTREE brengt onderzoekers uit verschillende disciplines samen met telers, bedrijven, overheden en andere maatschappelijke organisaties. Daardoor krijg je toegang tot een uitzonderlijk rijk onderzoeksveld en kun je ontwikkelingen gedurende meerdere jaren van dichtbij volgen.
Je bent onderdeel van het Instituut Bestuurskunde van de Universiteit Leiden en werkt vanuit Den Haag. Tegelijkertijd maak je deel uit van het bredere SOLIDTREE-consortium en werk je regelmatig samen met onderzoekers en praktijkpartners buiten de universiteit.
Het project biedt daarmee een interessante omgeving voor kandidaten die academisch onderzoek willen combineren met maatschappelijke relevantie.

Hier ga je werken
Het doel van de Faculteit Governance en Global Affairs (FGGA)? Bijdragen aan de samenleving. Dit doet de faculteit met hoogwaardig interdisciplinair onderwijs en (nieuwe) wetenschappelijke kennis. Of het nu gaat om terrorisme, veiligheid, artificial intelligence of een bestuurlijke oplossing voor de stikstofcrisis, bij FGGA komen hedendaagse vraagstukken uitgebreid aan bod.

In hartje Den Haag, waar belangrijke beslissingen worden genomen, komen studenten en professionals samen om kennis en vaardigheden op te doen. Er wordt veel samengewerkt met universitaire en maatschappelijke partners, wat ervoor zorgt dat studenten de universiteit verlaten met een glimlach en alvast met één been in de toekomst, klaar om een substantiële bijdrage te leveren aan de maatschappij.

FGGA is één van de zeven faculteiten van de Universiteit Leiden. Deze jonge, ondernemende, vernieuwende en innovatieve organisatie heeft drie wetenschappelijke instituten, twee centers, ruim 3700 studenten en 425 medewerkers. Voor meer informatie over de faculteit klik hier.

Het Instituut Bestuurskunde in Den Haag is een van de grootste en oudste instellingen voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek en onderwijs in de bestuurskunde in Nederland. Het instituut combineert een sterke internationale academische reputatie met een centrale positionering bij de internationale, nationale, regionale en lokale overheidsinstellingen, inclusief die in Den Haag. Het Instituut Bestuurskunde ontvangt consequent hoge beoordelingen in peer reviews voor zowel zijn onderwijs- als onderzoeksprogramma’s. Zie voor meer informatie Instituut Bestuurskunde - Universiteit Leiden

Dit breng je mee
We zoeken vooral een nieuwsgierige en analytisch sterke onderzoeker met belangstelling voor governance en maatschappelijke verandering.
Je hebt:
  • een afgeronde masteropleiding in bijvoorbeeld Bestuurskunde, Politicologie, Sociologie, Science and Technology Studies (STS), Sustainability/Transition Studies, Milieuwetenschappen, Innovation Studies of een verwante discipline;
  • aantoonbare belangstelling voor thema’s als governance, duurzaamheid, digitalisering, innovatie of publiek-private samenwerking;
  • belangstelling voor empirisch onderzoek en voor het werken met verschillende soorten organisaties en respondenten;
  • ervaring met, of de bereidheid je verder te ontwikkelen in, kwalitatieve en/of kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden;
  • uitstekende communicatieve en schrijfvaardigheden;
  • een goede beheersing van het Engels.

Omdat een belangrijk deel van het veldwerk plaatsvindt in Nederland en je met Nederlandse telers, beleidsmakers en andere praktijkpartners zult spreken, is voldoende beheersing van het Nederlands om interviews en gesprekken te kunnen voeren sterk gewenst.

We verwachten niet dat je al expert bent op het gebied van laanbomenteelt of bodemecologie. Belangrijker is dat je geïnteresseerd bent in de bestuurlijke vraagstukken die ontstaan wanneer wetenschap, technologie, beleid en praktijk samenkomen.
Herken je jezelf volledig in dit profiel, óf voldoe je niet aan alle eisen, maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren!

Dit bieden we je
Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om gedurende vier jaar een zelfstandig promotieonderzoek uit te voeren binnen een groot, interdisciplinair NWO-project.

We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarbij bieden we:
  • begeleiding door onderzoekers met expertise op het gebied van governance, innovatie en duurzaamheid;
  • toegang tot een breed netwerk van academische en maatschappelijke partners;
