jobs.title: PhD Position on Biophysical Origins of RNA Toxicity in Huntington’s Disease
jobs.description_html:
In Huntington’s Disease (HD), expansion of CAG repeats in the huntingtin (HTT) gene leads to a toxic gain-of-function that ultimately results in fatal neurodegeneration. HD research has long focused on the toxic effects of the HTT-encoded polyglutamine protein that aggregates in neurons. However, recent discoveries reveal that the HTT mRNA itself forms condensates and aggregates, contributing to neuronal toxicity. In this project, your work will help define the origins of RNA toxicity in HD - a critical step toward developing therapies.

Your job
As a PhD candidate in this project, you will design, execute, and analyze single-molecule experiments using optical tweezers and confocal fluorescence imaging, building on previous work (O’Brien et al., Nat Comm 2024). Together with our collaborators, you will produce materials for these experiments and develop novel approaches for protein and RNA labeling. Working at the interface of biophysics and biochemistry, you will establish new paradigms that explain why some repeat RNAs are toxic while others are not.

Your responsibilities include:
  • Independently conducting experimental work and performing data analysis;
  • Presenting your progress in regular team meetings;
  • Publishing your findings in peer-reviewed journals;
  • Participating in scientific conferences;
  • Supporting teaching and mentoring undergraduate and master's students.

Under the mentorship of Prof. Christian Kaiser, you will have the freedom to explore your own ideas within the project goals. You will work closely with junior investigators in the group as well as with our local and international collaborators, and engage with the broader research community at the Bijvoet Centre and the Faculty of Science. Visit the Kaiser Lab and the Bijvoet Centre websites for more information.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Access, Actors and Accountability: The Role of Researchers in AI Governance
jobs.description_html:
What is the role of researchers in the governance of AI systems and digital platforms? What legal exceptions and safeguards do researchers need to be able to play that role? And how can we organise productive interactions between researcher, policy makers, regulators, civil society and companies? Research and expertise have critical role in making sure that AI and digital technologies are safe, respectful of fundamental rights and beneficial to society, but we have yet to develop the legal and organisational frameworks to enable their work, while protecting their safety and academic freedom. If you want to help doing so, this position might be for you.

Join Us!
Access, Actors and Accountability: The Role of Researchers in AI Governance
Governing AI systems and digital platforms, identifying systemic risks and developing adequate policy responses is complex and requires research and expertise. In the new European Digital Framework, researchers are central stakeholder ins AI and platform governance, and regulations like the DSA and the AI Act, define prominent roles for them to produce evidence, audit big tech companies and public bodies, monitor the way AI technology impacts society and help to ensure transparency and accountability. At the same time, this role comes with new challenges for academic freedom, navigating dependencies on regulators and large technology companies, being meaningfully involved and heard, and sometimes even having to navigate issues around safety against personal attacks and threats to their safety. At the same time, the ability of independent researchers to study platforms and AI systems often depends on research exemptions and access rights, and so does the evidence base available to regulators.

This is what you will do
This doctoral project examines the legal position of researchers under the DSA and AI Act, and the research exemptions, safeguards and policy processes needed to allow independent researchers to generate evidence for regulatory learning and anticipatory governance without eroding legality or academic freedom. This research combines doctrinal, normative and comparative research with interviews (with academics, policy makers, civil society and other societal stakeholders) and participatory research to co-design how research exemptions and researcher-regulator feedback loops can be designed and operationalised. The work will build an evaluative analysis of exemption scope and adequacy, a typology of enablers and obstacles to researcher–policy engagement, and concrete proposals how to enable policy research while protecting academic freedom.

You will work on a legal PhD thesis at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Amsterdam Law School, University of Amsterdam, as part of the REGULAIRE project. The PhD will provide the opportunity to contribute to the activities of the DSA Observatory, the AI, Media & Democracy Lab and the Amsterdam Law School Sectorplan initiative Democratic Digital Transformation (2026-2031) and offers a focused route into information law, platform and AI regulation.

About REGULAIRE
REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Across the network, regulatory learning means treating regulation as a learning architecture that generates, tests and refines knowledge about what works, rather than as one-off rulemaking. Each researcher joins an international cohort, receives supervision across institutions and takes part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The network is coordinated by Prof. Urs Gasser at the Technical University of Munich (TUM).

More specifically, you are expected to:
  • Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team, and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials.
  • Collect, manage and analyse research data using the approved project-specific methods.
  • Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the doctoral programme and the REGULAIRE plan.
  • Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, network reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement, including three residential summer schools and monthly paper development seminars.
  • Undertake the planned three-month intersectoral secondment with EDMO – The European Digital Media Observatory (EDMO), Florence, Italy.
  • Contribute to the research and activities of the AI, Media & Democracy Lab and the DSA Observatory.
  • Contribute to research integrity, equality and diversity, open science and FAIR data practices.

What we ask of you
  • A Master's degree (or an equivalent qualification giving access to doctoral studies) in law, political science, media and communication studies, or related legal, social science and interdisciplinary fields, completed by the start date.
  • A demonstrable interest in studying the relationship of law to digital technologies and services;
  • Skills or a demonstrable interest in qualitative research, such as interviews and participatory design.
  • Excellent command of written and spoken English.
  • Willingness to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities.
  • Fulfilment of the MSCA eligibility conditions listed below.
  • A creative mind and strong critical and analytical skills;
  • Collegial attitude and capacity to work not only independently but also in teams;
  • Ability and willingness to organize workshops, lectures, and similar events (demonstrable experience with these activities a plus).

If the vacancy appeals to you, but you are doubting whether you might be THE person we are looking for, please do apply? We encourage all qualified applicants, including minorities, women, people with disabilities, and members of other groups underrepresented in academia. We wish to create a research group that consists of persons who each contribute in their unique way to the team. Complementarity and not homogeneity is what we are looking for.

Supervision, training and mobility
Your supervision team will consist of Supervision team: Prof. Natali Helberger (University of Amsterdam), Prof. Joris van Hoboken (University of Amsterdam), an external supervisor from the REGULAIRE project network, and a sectoral mentor at the anticipated secondment host.

The secondment enables the candidate to observe how a research-based civil society organisation engages in policy research, challenges involved and possible best practices. The candidate will be part of a supervisory team consisting of the primary supervisor at the host institution, an academic co-supervisor at a partner institution in another country, and a sectoral mentor at the secondment host. Candidates meet the primary supervisor at least monthly and the full team at least four times per year; progress and training are recorded in a personal Career Development Plan. Network-wide training includes three residential summer schools (regulatory learning and foresight at TUM; methods and analytics at BI Norwegian Business School; academic writing and impact at the University of St. Gallen), monthly paper development seminars, and annual network reviews aligned with major community events. Candidates obtain a minimum of twenty ECTS through local and network-wide training, of which at least ten from network-wide provision.

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 12 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is January 1st 2027. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3.204 to € 4.051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile 'PhD student' is applicable. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. The UvA offers excellent possibilities for further professional development and education.

What else do we offer
  • a position where own initiative and input are highly valued;
  • an enthusiastic and dynamic team that is open to new colleagues;
  • an inspiring academic and international working environment in the heart of Amsterdam.

You will work in this team
The University of Amsterdam is the largest university in the Netherlands, with the broadest spectrum of degree programmes. It is an intellectual hub with 39,000 students, 6,000 employees and 3,000 doctoral students who are all committed to a culture of inquiring minds.

With over 5,000 students and more than 500 staff members, the Amsterdam Law School is one of the larger law faculties in the Netherlands. We educate lawyers who know how to apply the law effectively with the aim of making a real contribution to solving social problems. The Amsterdam Law School stands for progressive and trail-blazing education and research, for stronger legal institutions, solutions to social problems and a better and juster society.

The Institute for Information Law (IViR), officially established in 1989, is one of the largest research centers in the field of information law in Europe, and one of the largest of its kind in the world.

The Institute engages in cutting-edge research into fundamental and topical aspects of information law, and provides a forum for critical debate about the social, cultural and political aspects of regulating information markets.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Systemic Actors and the Enforcement of Digital Rules
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in the functioning of law in relation to big tech? Do you want to research how law and enforcement of digital rules can engage systemic actors in the digital economy? And would you like to become part of a European network of researchers studying how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, digital platforms, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Then the Phd project ‘Systemic Actors and the Enforcement of Digital Rules’ may be right for you.

Join Us!
How can regulation and enforcement take account of systemic actors in the digital economy
Enforcing digital rules against very large platforms large tech companies is a moving target. This PhD project will look at the existence of systemic actors in the digital economy and their implications for enforcement dynamics. The digital economy is characterized by the emergence of actors that have a significantly broader systemic impact on the way in which compliance with digital rules is organized and enforced than just their own operations. Examples from the literature include smartphone ecosystems, and infrastructural cloud services. This project will study the extent to which the systemic influence of these actors is recognized in and how the enforcement of digital rules can optimally approach these actors, considering broader impacts on compliance and enforcement.

This is what you will do
The doctoral project will examine how regulators adapt enforcement strategies in response to systemic actors under the DSA, DMA, AI Act and GDPR, studying how initial enforcement attempts evolve as regulators learn from complex platform ecosystems. You will trace enforcement processes across cases and jurisdictions and interview those involved. The work will build a typology of regulatory learning patterns concerning systemic actors, best-practice enforcement learning cycles and a framework for adaptive enforcement.

You will work on a legal PhD thesis at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Amsterdam Law School, University of Amsterdam, as part of the REGULAIRE project. The PhD will provide the opportunity to contribute to the activities of the DSA Observatory and the Amsterdam Law School Sectorplan initiative Democratic Digital Transformation (2026-2031) and offers a focused route into information law, platform regulation and enforcement research.

About REGULAIRE
REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Across the network, regulatory learning means treating regulation as a learning architecture that generates, tests and refines knowledge about what works, rather than as one-off rulemaking. Each researcher joins an international cohort, receives supervision across institutions and takes part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The network is coordinated by Prof. Urs Gasser at the Technical University of Munich (TUM).

More specifically, you are expected to:
  • Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team, and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials.
  • Collect, manage and analyse research data using the approved project-specific methods.
  • Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the doctoral programme and the REGULAIRE plan.
  • Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, network reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement, including three residential summer schools and monthly paper development seminars.
  • Undertake the planned three-month intersectoral secondment;.
  • Contribute to the research and activities of the DSA Observatory;
  • Contribute to research integrity, equality and diversity, open science and FAIR data practices.

What we ask of you
  • A Master's degree (or an equivalent qualification giving access to doctoral studies) in law, political science, media and communication studies, or related legal, social science and interdisciplinary fields, completed by the start date.
  • A demonstrable interest in studying the relationship of law to digital technologies and services;
  • Skills or a demonstrable interest in qualitative regulatory process tracing and interviews.
  • Excellent command of written and spoken English.
  • Willingness to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities.
  • Fulfilment of the MSCA eligibility conditions listed below.
  • A creative mind and strong critical and analytical skills;
  • Collegial attitude and capacity to work not only independently but also in teams;
  • Ability and willingness to organize workshops, lectures, and similar events (demonstrable experience with these activities a plus).

If the vacancy appeals to you, but you are doubting whether you might be THE person we are looking for, please do apply? We encourage all qualified applicants, including minorities, women, people with disabilities, and members of other groups underrepresented in academia. We wish to create a research group that consists of persons who each contribute in their unique way to the team. Complementarity and not homogeneity is what we are looking for.

Supervision, training and mobility
Your supervision team will consist of Supervision team: Prof. Joris van Hoboken (University of Amsterdam), Prof. Natali Helberger (University of Amsterdam), an external supervisor from the REGULAIRE project network, and a sectoral mentor at the anticipated secondment host.

The secondment enables the candidate to observe how a leading digital regulator engages with systemic actors, providing insight into adaptive enforcement cycles, learning barriers and evolving supervisory strategies.

The candidate will be part of a supervisory team consisting of the primary supervisor at the host institution, an academic co-supervisor at a partner institution in another country, and a sectoral mentor at the secondment host. Candidates meet the primary supervisor at least monthly and the full team at least four times per year; progress and training are recorded in a personal Career Development Plan. Network-wide training includes three residential summer schools (regulatory learning and foresight at TUM; methods and analytics at BI Norwegian Business School; academic writing and impact at the University of St. Gallen), monthly paper development seminars, and annual network reviews aligned with major community events. Candidates obtain a minimum of twenty ECTS through local and network-wide training, of which at least ten from network-wide provision.

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 12 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is January 1st 2027. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3.204 to € 4.051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile 'PhD student' is applicable. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. The UvA offers excellent possibilities for further professional development and education.

What else do we offer
  • a position where own initiative and input are highly valued;
  • an enthusiastic and dynamic team that is open to new colleagues;
  • an inspiring academic and international working environment in the heart of Amsterdam.

You will work in this team
The University of Amsterdam is the largest university in the Netherlands, with the broadest spectrum of degree programmes. It is an intellectual hub with 39,000 students, 6,000 employees and 3,000 doctoral students who are all committed to a culture of inquiring minds.

With over 5,000 students and more than 500 staff members, the Amsterdam Law School is one of the larger law faculties in the Netherlands. We educate lawyers who know how to apply the law effectively with the aim of making a real contribution to solving social problems. The Amsterdam Law School stands for progressive and trail-blazing education and research, for stronger legal institutions, solutions to social problems and a better and juster society.

The Institute for Information Law (IViR), officially established in 1989, is one of the largest research centers in the field of information law in Europe, and one of the largest of its kind in the world.

The Institute engages in cutting-edge research into fundamental and topical aspects of information law, and provides a forum for critical debate about the social, cultural and political aspects of regulating information markets.

jobs.title: PhD position: Trait-based drivers of global plant distributions
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in spatial ecology, species distributions, and plant functional traits? Do you want to contribute to understanding global patterns of plant diversity, and plant responses to environmental change?

Conserving biodiversity in a rapidly changing world requires understanding why some species occupy vast geographic ranges while others remain restricted to small areas. Traditionally, efforts to answer this question have focused on understanding and predicting the distributions of individual species. However, recent advances in biodiversity and trait datasets have expanded our capacity to incorporate the functional characteristics of species, allowing us to go beyond the species concept and better capture the variation in biota using functional traits across different levels of biological organisation.

This PhD position explores how functional traits influence global patterns of plant biodiversity and plant responses to environmental change. The project focuses on three different levels of organisation, ranging from broad functional forms that capture major ecological plant strategies (e.g. tree, epiphyte, shrub), to finer levels of organisation among species (inter-specific variation) and within species (intra-specific variation). As a PhD candidate, you will make use of large trait databases like TRY and BIEN, and be responsible for setting up a greenhouse experiment similar to that of a provenance trial set-up (i.e. growing seeds collected from across a species’ native geographic range under varying environmental conditions). Specifically, your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Collating plant distributions, functional traits, and environmental data from various sources
  • Setting-up and conducting a greenhouse experiment to assess variation in plant phenotypic plasticity under simulated environmental conditions
  • Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting your research at (inter)national conferences
  • Mentoring BSc/MSc students

You will work here
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation group, which is led by Prof. David Kleijn. You will be supervised by Dr. Coline Boonman and Dr. Amanda Taylor. Prof. David Kleijn is the promotor.

jobs.title: PhD position in modelling the formation and flooding of coastal peat landscapes
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by how water, sediment and vegetation shape coastal landscapes? Would you like to use numerical models to reconstruct the formation and flooding of peat landscapes during the Holocene, to better understand coastal landscape development under future sea-level rise? And are you eager to work in an interdisciplinary research team? Then this PhD position may be for you!

Zeeland is a low-lying coastal province in the south-western part of the Netherlands. During the Holocene, large parts of the region developed into an extensive peat landscape. Following a combination of sea-level rise, natural landscape dynamics and human land use, this landscape was flooded and transformed into the tidal environment it is today.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate the processes behind these major landscape changes. You will translate existing geological records and paleo-tidal reconstructions into morphological and hydrodynamic boundary conditions for new numerical model simulations. In turn, you will validate the simulated coastal landscape development with the available paleo-records.

You will work with numerical models such as Delft3D, to capture interactions between hydrodynamics, sediment transport, morphology, and peat dynamics. The model studies will help to unravel how these bio-physical interactions have, over centuries to millennia, formed the Zeeland peat landscape and caused its subsequent rapid flooding.

This PhD position is part of Re-Flex Zeeland, an interdisciplinary project funded by the Delta Climate Center. The project brings together Wageningen University, Utrecht University, the Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research (NIOZ), and regional partners. Although the project focuses on Zeeland, it addresses internationally relevant questions about the resilience and vulnerability of low-lying deltas under sea-level rise, land subsidence and human intervention.

Within the Re-Flex Zeeland project, you will collaborate closely with another PhD candidate working on geological and vegetation reconstructions, and with a postdoctoral researcher developing three-dimensional visualizations of the past landscapes.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • developing, calibrating and evaluating numerical models that couple hydrodynamics, sediment transport, morphology and vegetation dynamics;
  • translating geological and paleo-tidal reconstructions into model configurations;
  • designing numerical experiments to investigate the formation and flooding of coastal peat landscapes;
  • collaborating with researchers at Wageningen University, Utrecht University, NIOZ and the Delta Climate Center;
  • publishing your findings in scientific journals and presenting them at international conferences;
  • supervising BSc and MSc thesis students, and contributing to field excursions in Zeeland as part of BSc and MSc education;
  • completing a PhD thesis.

You will work here
We are the Hydrology and Environmental Hydraulics Group (HWM), a dynamic and committed team of academics, support staff, postdocs and PhD researchers. Our focus is on hydrology and environmental hydraulics, which we combine to understand and quantify hydrological processes in catchments, aquifers, rivers and deltas. We develop novel sensing techniques, create models and perform field and lab experiments to advance process understanding.

You will be supervised by Roeland van de Vijsel and Ton Hoitink, and will work closely together with other researchers in the Re-Flex Zeeland project.

Your working time will be divided between Wageningen University, and the Delta Climate Center in Vlissingen, a coastal city in Zeeland. The exact balance will be agreed at the start of the appointment. Regular presence at both locations and travel between them will be expected.

jobs.title: PhD position EEG and Neurobiological Markers
jobs.description_html:
Are you a motivated early-career researcher with a strong interest in EEG, neurobiology, and precision medicine? Would you like to investigate how neurobiological markers related to reward, motivation, and impulsivity can contribute to a better understanding of health and disease?

We are looking for an enthusiastic PhD candidate to join an international, multidisciplinary research programme investigating reward, motivation, and impulsivity across major depressive disorder, Alzheimer's disease, and obesity.


Your PhD research will combine three closely connected components: a systematic review of EEG measures, empirical EEG analyses, and hypothesis-driven research investigating relationships between EEG and other neurobiological markers.

The position provides an opportunity to develop expertise in EEG methodology and quantitative analysis while contributing to a broader precision medicine approach that integrates evidence across different populations, research settings, and types of biological and clinical data.

What are you going to do?

Your PhD research will connect systematic evidence synthesis with empirical EEG research and hypothesis-driven investigation of neurobiological markers.

Systematic review of EEG measures

A first component of your research will be a systematic review of EEG measures relevant to reward, motivation, and impulsivity.


You will:

  • Develop and conduct a systematic review of EEG measures relevant to reward, motivation, and impulsivity.
  • Define and document search strategies and eligibility criteria.
  • Screen and select relevant scientific literature.
  • Extract and organise information on EEG measures, study characteristics, populations, outcomes, and relevant neurobiological markers.
  • Synthesise and map the available evidence in a transparent and reproducible manner.
  • Investigate the consistency and potential relevance of different EEG measures across populations and research settings.
  • Identify promising EEG measures as well as important gaps in the existing evidence.
  • Contribute to scientific publications and other outputs arising from the evidence synthesis.


This work will provide an evidence-based foundation for the interpretation and selection of EEG measures used in the empirical research.


EEG analyses

A substantial part of your PhD will involve analysing EEG data generated through cohort and clinical research.


Depending on the available datasets and specific research questions, you will:


  • Contribute to the preparation, preprocessing, and quality control of EEG data.
  • Develop and apply appropriate EEG analysis pipelines.
  • Investigate EEG measures relevant to reward, motivation, and impulsivity.
  • Examine associations between EEG measures and behavioural, clinical, and other relevant variables.
  • Analyse data collected across different populations and research settings.
  • Contribute to the development of reproducible and well-documented analytical workflows.
  • Interpret EEG findings in the context of the broader scientific framework.
  • Communicate findings through scientific publications, presentations, and research meetings.


You will progressively develop methodological independence and contribute to decisions concerning the analysis and interpretation of EEG data under the guidance of the supervisory team.


Hypothesis testing with neurobiological markers

A further aim of the PhD is to investigate hypothesis-driven relationships between EEG measures and other neurobiological markers.


You will:

  • Formulate and test hypotheses concerning relationships between neurobiological markers relevant to reward, motivation, and impulsivity.
  • Investigate associations between EEG measures and other available biological, clinical, behavioural, or phenotypic measures.
  • Examine whether neurobiological markers are associated with transdiagnostic dimensions of reward, motivation, and impulsivity or with relevant clinical outcomes.
  • Apply appropriate statistical methods to test predefined hypotheses.
  • Investigate whether combinations of neurobiological measures provide complementary information.
  • Interpret findings in relation to existing evidence and the broader precision medicine framework.
  • Contribute to understanding the potential of neurobiological markers for characterising clinically relevant profiles across different conditions.


The precise analytical approaches will be developed in collaboration with the supervisory team and will depend on the available datasets and scientific questions.


Integration of evidence and empirical research

An important feature of the PhD is the connection between what is known from the literature and what can be learned from new data.


You will therefore have the opportunity to:


  • Use findings from the systematic review to inform empirical EEG analyses.
  • Compare findings across different populations and research settings.
  • Integrate EEG findings with other neurobiological, behavioural, and clinical measures.
  • Critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of candidate biomarkers.
  • Contribute to the identification of neurobiological measures that may have relevance across diagnostic categories.


This integrated approach will allow you to develop a broad understanding of how EEG and other neurobiological measures can contribute to transdiagnostic and precision medicine research.

jobs.title: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’
jobs.description_html:
Research challenges

As a PhD candidate, you will develop methods for adaptive privacy protection of energy data, combining differential privacy, empirical privacy attacks and privacy–utility optimisation. Your research is part of the  Adaptive Privacy and Legal Compliance work package in the SHARE project. More specifically, your challenges are to:

  • Investigate how temporal patterns, spatial information, rare events and other distinctive features contribute to re-identification and inference risk. You will work with metrics such as uniqueness, entropy, attack success rates and time-series-specific indicators.
  • Implement and study attacks such as membership inference, reconstruction, re-identification and attribute inference to understand where information leakage occurs in both original and synthetic datasets.
  • Investigate methods that allocate stronger protection to sensitive components and lighter perturbation to lower-risk components, thereby preserving as much analytical utility as possible.
  • Formulate privacy protection as an optimisation problem balancing formal privacy guarantees against statistical, temporal and physical utility requirements for energy-system applications.
  • Collaborate closely with researchers at Radboud University, who develop physics-informed generative models for synthetic energy data, and investigate approaches such as differentially private training and post-generation privacy calibration.
  • Work closely with distribution system operator Alliander and other consortium partners to evaluate whether the developed methods provide meaningful protection while retaining the information required for practical energy-system applications.
  • Ultimately contribute to an open-source privacy layer for the SHARE toolbox.

jobs.title: PhD Position Decision-making Under Uncertainty for Emerging Orphan and Breakthrough Medical Devices
jobs.description_html:
What uncertainty in clinical evidence is acceptable for regulatory actors and patients to allow orphan or breakthrough devices on the market, while also ensuring these devices are sufficiently safe?

Job description
Innovative medical devices can offer important benefits to patients, especially when existing diagnostic or treatment options are limited. At the same time, the available clinical evidence may be limited or contain uncertainties when a device is assessed for market access. Regulators and notified bodies therefore need to decide when evidence is sufficient, what uncertainties can be considered acceptable, and under what conditions additional evidence should be collected after a device enters the market.

In this PhD project, which is part of the European COMPASS4MD project, you will study how these decisions are currently made in practice, and how uncertainty could be managed in the future. You will explore how uncertainty in clinical evidence is described and assessed, which factors make uncertainty more or less acceptable, and how unmet medical needs, small patient populations and expected patient benefits influence regulatory decisions. Building on these insights, you will examine how future regulatory approaches could support more responsible decision-making under uncertainty.

The research combines several methods. You will review regulatory documents and publicly available regulatory opinions from accross Europe (and possibly other jurisdictions). You will also interview professionals involved in the assessment of medical devices, such as notified-body assessors, regulators, and Expert Panel members. Based on these findings, you will develop realistic case scenarios that present different types and levels of uncertainty. These scenarios will be discussed with patients, clinicians, manufacturers, regulators, notified bodies, and health technology assessment bodies to explore where their views overlap and where they differ.

The final part of the project focuses on how regulation can deal with uncertainty in a responsible way. A particular area of interest is the use of regulatory sandboxes: controlled environments in which regulators, developers, and other stakeholders can explore regulatory questions and test approaches to evidence generation while a technology is still developing. You will also consider related approaches, including conditional market access and post-market evidence generation. The aim is to develop practical recommendations that support access to promising medical technologies while continuing to protect patients.

This PhD project is part of the European COMPASS4MD consortium and will involve close collaboration with research institutes, regulators, clinical experts, patient representatives, and other partners across Europe. You will contribute to joint project activities, exchange findings with partners from different countries and disciplines, and help organise interviews and stakeholder workshops. The position therefore suits someone who communicates easily, enjoys working with people from different countries and disciplines, and is willing to take an active role in an international consortium. You should be comfortable working independently on your own research while also contributing to shared activities, meetings, workshops, and deliverables with European project partners. Some travel within Europe may be part of the position.

English proficiency is required. Proficiency in Dutch is considered an advantage, but is not a requirement. Experience with medical-device regulation, clinical research, benefit–risk assessment, stakeholder workshops, survey experiments, or anticipatory governance is an advantage. We do not expect candidates to already possess expertise in all these areas; we particularly value the ability and motivation to work across disciplinary boundaries.

Job requirements
  • Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as Health Sciences, (Technical) Medicine, Health Policy or Healthcare Management, Public Policy, Innovation Sciences, Management of Technology or Technology Governance, Biomedical Engineering or a related field. As the project combines the analysis of clinical evidence with empirical research into regulatory decision-making, we particularly welcome candidates who can connect biomedical or clinical questions with policy, governance, and stakeholder perspectives.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
  • Good organisational skills.
  • Research experience and writing skills demonstrated through a thesis, publications, or previous research projects.
  • Excellent command of English is required. Dutch is considered an advantage.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty Technology, Policy & Management
The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Marine Renewables: Energy and Societal Impacts under Climate Change
jobs.description_html:
Join TU Delft to model the future ocean. Work on Digital Ocean Twins and climate scenarios shaping marine energy and coastal resilience across Europe.

Job description
Climate change is transforming our oceans: reshaping wave climates, marine renewable energy potential, and coastal systems. This PhD position offers a unique opportunity to contribute to this challenge by working on resilient future energy systems and their societal impacts under Climate Change (EU-INTERCHANGE, EU-FUSION), led by Dr George Lavidas.

As a PhD candidate, you will join the Marine Renewable Energies Lab at TU Delft and work within an interdisciplinary and international research team. Your work will focus on high-fidelity Energy System Modelling (ESM), and the development of coupled pwathway frameworks for “what-if” scenario analysis derived by Integrated Assessment Models (IAM).

You will develop different pathways based on multiple realisations of CMIP6 and/or CMIP7 datasets, aligned with IPCC scenarios, to assess their future implications on energy systems and societal indicators (such as GDP, etc). Your research will include developing new modules in ESM, IAM and active coupling between them, comprehensive econometric analysis and development of pathways based on what-if scenarios. A key component of your work will be integrating these insights into the European Digital Ocean platform (EDITO).

You will collaborate closely with academic and industry partners across Europe, contributing to joint research activities and project deliverables.

In addition to your research, you will:
  • Contribute to the coordination of project activities and ensure timely delivery of milestones.
  • Publish in leading scientific journals and present at international conferences.
  • Engage with project partners through reporting and collaboration.
  • Support the supervision of MSc students, and assist in teaching.

We are looking for a researcher who can work both independently and collaboratively, with strong organisational and communication skills, and a proactive approach to research and teamwork.

jobs.title: PhD position Data Science
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in using data science to understand how digital measures can capture clinically meaningful aspects of reward, motivation and impulsivity? Do you want to develop and apply innovative digital proxies and combine them with neurobiological markers to advance precision medicine across mental and metabolic health conditions? Then this PhD position in an international pioneering project may be an excellent opportunity for you.

You will work in an interdisciplinary, international research project aiming to advance a transdiagnostic precision-medicine framework centred on Reward, Motivation and Impulsivity. The project brings together expertise in longitudinal research, biomarker discovery, clinical validation, data science, evidence synthesis and stakeholder engagement.


A central ambition is to move beyond disease-specific approaches by identifying biological, behavioural and digital markers that can help characterise clinically meaningful processes across different health conditions.


As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to this ambition by helping establish the evidence base for digital proxies, developing and applying data-driven measures, and investigating their relationships with neurobiological markers.

What are you going to do?

We are looking for an ambitious and analytically minded PhD candidate to investigate digital proxies of Reward, Motivation and Impulsivity (RM&I) and their relationship with neurobiological markers and clinically relevant outcomes.

Your work will be connecting systematic evidence synthesis, data science, longitudinal research and clinical validation. Your research will contribute to understanding whether and how digital measures can provide scalable and meaningful proxies for RM&I-related processes across major depressive disorder (MDD), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and obesity (OB).


Your PhD research will have three closely connected components:

  • Systematic review of digital proxies: You will systematically synthesise existing evidence on digital proxies relevant to RM&I, identifying the types of digital measures that have been investigated, their relationship with behavioural and clinical constructs, and their potential relevance for transdiagnostic research.
  • Development and application of digital proxies: You will use data-science approaches to develop, characterise and/or evaluate RM&I-related digital proxies. You will subsequently apply these digital proxies to analyses conducted within the project's longitudinal and clinical datasets, contributing to the identification of meaningful patterns across individuals and disease trajectories.
  • Hypothesis testing with neurobiological markers: You will investigate relationships between digital proxies and neurobiological markers, testing hypotheses about the biological mechanisms underlying RM&I-related processes. Depending on the available data and the development of the research, this may involve integrating digital, behavioural, clinical and neurobiological measures.

An important aspect of your work will be to examine the clinical and transdiagnostic relevance of digital proxies. You will contribute to determining whether digital measures can complement existing biomarkers and endpoints and help identify measurable features of RM&I that are relevant across different conditions.

You will work closely with researchers involved in longitudinal cohort analyses, clinical studies, biomarker research and evidence synthesis. Your work will therefore sit at the intersection of data science, digital phenotyping, clinical research and neurobiology.

jobs.title: PhD in NWO Project CERRADO
jobs.description_html:
Looking for a PhD position to contribute to environmental justice in Brazil’s Cerrado? Join an interdisciplinary research team exploring how small-scale farmers and traditional communities can foster nature conservation, sustainable production and territorial justice. You will collaborate with researchers, producers, practitioners, and grassroots organizations to co-produce knowledge that supports a resilient Cerrado and sustainable sociobioeconomies in a region facing rapid agribusiness expansion and climate change.

Strengthening Justice and Resilience through Sociobioeconomies in Brazil’s Cerrado
The CERRADO Project—Conservation and Ecological Restoration for Resilient Agriculture and Development Outcomes—examines how agricultural development and biodiversity conservation can be better balanced in Brazil’s Cerrado, particularly in the rapidly transforming MATOPIBA region. It addresses pressures arising from agribusiness expansion, deforestation, land conflicts, and increasingly severe climate impacts, while exploring how sustainable practices developed by Indigenous peoples, traditional communities, and family farmers can contribute to sustainability and agrarian justice in the region.

The PhD research will contribute to the assessment of the sociobiodiversity economy in the MATOPIBA region, including small-scale farming, agroforestry, and sustainable extraction, as well as to in-depth socioeconomic and governance analyses of two cases involving local producers living in private and collective settlements in southern Maranhão. The regional assessment will examine the diversity, extent, challenges and social-economic relevance of sociobiodiversity production systems across MATOPIBA, as well as identify the key social, epistemic and political factors shaping these production systems within landscapes increasingly dominated by large-scale agriculture. The case studies will focus on producers’ social relations and organization, knowledge systems, governance arrangements, economic conditions, political mobilization, and perceptions of agrarian transformations and climate change. They will also examine how these production systems, in turn, contribute to the maintenance of natural systems and local livelihoods.

The PhD research will be carried out in collaboration with local stakeholders and other project members and will be closely aligned with the project’s other two pillars: ecological assessment and advocacy. The ecological assessment includes an integrated socioecological analysis of the contributions of different production systems to biodiversity conservation, water regulation, carbon storage, pollination, pest control, local livelihoods, food security, and climate resilience. The advocacy pillar will focus on translating research findings into policy recommendations and other societal products, thereby strengthening the contribution of the research to sustainable development and agrarian justice in the region.

This is what you will be doing
Developing skills for academic training and participatory research
  • submission of a PhD thesis within the period of appointment;
  • completion and submission of three article manuscripts to peer-reviewed journals within the period of appointment;
  • presenting intermediate research results at workshops and conferences;
  • participation in the ARTES Research School and Faculty of Humanities PhD training programmes;
  • (co-)teaching courses at BA-level in the second and third year of the appointment (maximum 0,2 fte per year, which corresponds to approximately 8 hours per week);
  • participating in meetings of the project research group and developing a shared database;
  • provide support to organization and execution of project-related activities;
  • co-supervise two Master research theses in your PhD research area;
  • participation in national and international academic events;
  • organising knowledge dissemination activities;
  • participating actively in meetings of the project research team and developing a shared database and eventually co-publications.

This is what we ask of you
  • a completed Master's degree in Social Sciences or Environmental Sciences; preferably with focus on socioenvironmental and agrarian change;
  • excellent research skills demonstrated by a Master thesis and/or published articles;
  • demonstrable knowledge in theoretical perspectives relevant to environmental and agrarian justice;
  • solid knowledge of qualitative research methods;
  • research experience with rural communities in Brazil;
  • experience with interdisciplinary research and collaboration with non-academic actors is desirable;
  • excellent spoken Portuguese, and language proficiency in English;
  • availability for extended fieldwork stays in remote areas at time.

Please note that if you already hold a doctorate/PhD or are working towards obtaining a similar degree elsewhere, you will not be admitted to a doctoral programme at the UvA.

This is what else we offer you
  • We offer a temporary employment contract for the period of 48 months. The first contract will be for 16 months, with an extension for the following 32 months, contingent on a positive performance evaluation within the first 12 months. The preferred starting date is 01 February 2027;
  • Based on a full-time appointment (38 hours per week) the gross monthly salary will range from € 3.204 in the first year to € 4.051 (scale P) in the last year. This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD candidate applicable. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable;
  • PhD candidates receive a tuition fee waiver;
  • PhD candidates have free access to courses offered by the Graduate School of Humanities and the Dutch National Research Schools;
  • financial support for the execution of the research project and participation in academic events;
  • an inspiring academic and international work environment in the heart of Amsterdam;
  • excellent possibilities for further professional development and education;
  • an enthusiastic and professional international academic team composed of researchers, practitioners and grassroots organizations from Brazil and The Netherlands;
  • A broad network of local partners to give support throughout the research period.

This is where you will be working
You will benefit not only from the project team’s rich interdisciplinary academic expertise, but also from its engaged methodological approach, strong connections with local actors, and commitment to generating societal impact. CERRADO is a research project grounded in knowledge co-production between academic actors across the social and ecological sciences and non-academic partners. The team brings together expertise in research, practice, and advocacy for sustainable land use in the Cerrado, with a particular focus on sociobiodiversity production systems. It combines regional, thematic, methodological, and disciplinary expertise with a strong research–practice–policy interface and active international exchange between Brazil and the Netherlands. The team is committed to horizontal knowledge building and exchange and has extensive experience in participatory research and advocacy. It is supported by a broad network of sociobiodiversity producers, grassroots organizations, and other local partners, as well as an active presence across the wider MATOPIBA region.

The PhD position is part of ARTES, one of the Research Schools of the Amsterdam Institute for Humanities Research , at the Faculty of Humanities of the University of Amsterdam. ARTES is home to more than 50 scholars and 50 PhD candidates. ARTES research engages with political, intellectual and institutional cultures in their national as well as transnational dimensions. As an interdisciplinary and transnational Research School, ARTES aims to go beyond traditional ‘area’ and ‘regional’ studies approaches, focusing also on the re-making and relations between world and regional orders, borders, and identities, historically and in today’s world. The Faculty of Humanities provides education and conducts research with a strong international profile in a large number of disciplines in de field of language and culture. Located in the heart of Amsterdam, the faculty maintains close ties with many cultural institutes in the capital city. Research and teaching staff focus on interdisciplinary collaboration and are active in several teaching programmes. The University of Amsterdam is the Netherlands' largest university, offering the widest range of academic programmes. At the UvA, 30,000 students, 6,000 staff members and 3,000 PhD candidates study and work in a diverse range of fields, connected by a culture of curiosity.

The PhD candidate will be located at the Centre for Latin American Research and Documentation (CEDLA), which is part of ARTES. CEDLA is the Latin American Studies hub of the Netherlands and contributes to the development of research and education on topics related to societal change in Latin America. The Centre is involved in multiple academic and societal networks with Latin American and other international researchers and institutions. In addition to several funded projects, CEDLA coordinates education programs such as the BA Minor in Global Justice and the MA program Global Justice and Social Transformation. Through a community approach, the staff, postdocs, PhD and MA students, and research fellows stay in close contact through several academic and social events.

Questions?
For questions about the position or department, you can contact us during office hours at:
Fabio de Castro - f.decastro@uva.nl
Senior Lecturer, CEDLA

Application
If you recognise yourself in the profile and are interested in the position, we look forward to receiving your application. Please add the following documents to your application:
  • CV
  • Motivation letter
  • Provide the names and contact details of two academic or professional references
  • One sample of your academic writing, preferably a published piece

In your motivation letter, please explain your interest in the PhD position and research topic, and briefly outline the ideas, questions, or perspectives you would like to explore within the project.

Apply no later than 29 October. The first round of interviews will take place online in the second half of November.

jobs.title: PhD candidate for the project "Modulation of inflammatory Dendritic cell subsets in atherosclerosis"
jobs.description_html:
The Faculty of Science and the Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for a:

PhD candidate for the project “Modulation of inflammatory Dendritic cell subsets in atherosclerosis”
Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease where atherosclerotic plaques develop in the larger arteries. Atherosclerosis is the underlying pathology of cardiovascular disease events such as myocardial infarction or stroke. Currently, treatment focusses on lipid-lowering interventions, which do not target the chronic inflammation that causes plaque instability and major acute cardiovascular events. Therefore, studying the immune cells that contribute to atherosclerotic plaque destabilization may lead to novel therapeutic targets and intervention strategies.

In this project, we aim to investigate how inflammatory myeloid cell populations, with a focus on dendritic cell subsets contribute to the progression of atherosclerosis. Dendritic cells act as directors of the immune response by activating T cells and may thus fuel the ongoing chronic inflammatory response in advanced atherosclerosis. We aim to investigate novel mechanisms and identify new targets for more targeted therapeutic intervention.

What you will do
The aim of your PhD project is to obtain novel knowledge regarding myeloid immune cells in cardiovascular disease, specifically in advanced atherosclerosis.

You will:

1) identify myeloid cell subsets, with a particular focus on dendritic cells, in advanced human atherosclerosis and associate these with patient characteristics

2) investigate the functional changes of different dendritic cell subsets in advanced atherosclerosis

3) identify proatherogenic dendritic cell subsets and validate potential therapeutic targets for intervention.

You will make use of available human atherosclerotic tissue and datasets, design and perform in vitro studies and validate findings in vivo.

What you bring
We are looking for an enthusiastic, bright, well-motivated and ambitious scientist:
  • With a recent Master degree in Bio-Pharmaceutical/Bio-medical sciences, immunology, molecular biology, or a related field,
  • Strong background in immunology and/or cardiovascular research,
  • With experience with in vivo studies (artikel 9, proefdierkunde), spectral flow cytometry, single-cell sequencing (working in R), microscopical techniques and molecular biology is an advantage,
  • English proficiency (verbally and written),
  • Who is an independent and creative team player with good communicative skills.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Science at Leiden University is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future.

The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelors’ and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and over 6,000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

The division of BioTherapeutics operates at the forefront of research in the field of therapeutic modulation of cardiovascular disease. The research aims to identify new immune targets in atherosclerosis and to develop innovative biopharmaceutical concepts to intervene in cardiovascular disease. The use of specific gene-knockout technology, biologics such as vaccines, therapeutic proteins and cellular therapy, provides a unique approach for the development of new therapies for the treatment or prevention of atherosclerosis. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/drug-research/biotherapeutics.

What we offer
We offer a full-time appointment of initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, teaching evaluations, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for another three years. You will be appointed in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities. The salary ranges from € 3.204,- per month in the first year to € 4.051,- gross per month in the fourth year based on a full-time position (pay scale P).
Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3 %), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. For international spouses we have set up a dual career program. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. For more information, see the website: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions.

All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school.

What we value
Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Nieuwe inzichten in het gebruik van remimazolam'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Wil jij bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling van veiligere en meer patiëntgerichte anesthesiologische zorg? En spreekt het je aan om klinische vragen te vertalen naar vernieuwend wetenschappelijk onderzoek? Voor een nieuw onderzoeksproject naar remimazolam zoeken wij een enthousiaste promovendus die klinisch onderzoek wil combineren met farmacologie en anesthesiologie.

Remimazolam is een relatief nieuw, kortwerkend benzodiazepine voor sedatie en algehele anesthesie. Het middel kenmerkt zich door een snelle werking en een snel herstel en lijkt minder negatieve hemodynamische en respiratoire effecten te hebben dan verschillende veelgebruikte anesthetica. Tegelijkertijd zijn er nog belangrijke vragen over hoe remimazolam optimaal kan worden ingezet in de dagelijkse anesthesiologische praktijk.

Binnen dit promotietraject onderzoek je nieuwe toepassingen en mogelijkheden van remimazolam binnen de anesthesiologie en perioperatieve zorg. Het project bestaat voornamelijk uit prospectief klinisch onderzoek en bevindt zich op het snijvlak van anesthesiologie, klinische farmacologie en perioperatieve geneeskunde. Het uiteindelijke doel is om beter te begrijpen hoe remimazolam kan worden ingezet om anesthesiologische zorg veiliger, voorspelbaarder en meer patiëntgericht te maken.

Als promovendus ben je betrokken bij het volledige traject van klinisch-wetenschappelijk onderzoek. Je ontwikkelt onderzoeksprotocollen, bereidt medisch-ethische en andere regulatoire aanvragen voor en draagt zorg voor de praktische uitvoering van de studies. Je includeert patiënten en/of gezonde proefpersonen, verzamelt en analyseert onderzoeksgegevens en vertaalt de resultaten naar wetenschappelijke publicaties.

Taken en verantwoordelijkheden
  • Opzetten en uitvoeren van prospectieve klinische studies naar remimazolam.
  • Schrijven van onderzoeksprotocollen en het voorbereiden van medisch-ethische en regulatoire aanvragen.
  • Includeren en begeleiden van patiënten en/of gezonde proefpersonen.
  • Verzamelen, beheren en analyseren van onderzoeksgegevens.
  • Uitvoeren en interpreteren van statistische analyses, in samenwerking met ervaren onderzoekers en statistici.
  • Presenteren van onderzoeksresultaten op nationale en internationale congressen.
  • Schrijven en publiceren van wetenschappelijke artikelen in internationale peer-reviewed tijdschriften.
  • Actief bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling van nieuwe onderzoeksvragen op het gebied van anesthesiologie, perioperatieve zorg en klinische farmacologie.

De verschillende studies vormen uiteindelijk de basis voor jouw proefschrift.

jobs.title: PhD Replacing Chemicals with Electricity: Engineering Local pH Environments
jobs.description_html:
Can electricity replace acids, bases, and cleaning chemicals used throughout industry today? How do local pH conditions develop near electrodes and membranes in electrochemical systems, and how can they be controlled? In this PhD project, you will investigate these questions by combining modelling and experimental data to develop electrically driven alternatives for industrial cleaning and separation processes.

What will you do?
Many industries rely on acids, bases, detergents, and other chemicals to clean equipment, recover valuable products, and produce high-quality process water. These chemicals increase environmental impact, complicate water re-use and require downstream treatment. In this project, we take a different approach: rather than adding chemicals, we aim to create the required chemical conditions directly using electricity.

A key challenge in replacing these chemicals with electricity is that electrochemical systems create localized pH environments near electrodes and membranes. These local conditions often differ strongly from bulk solution properties, yet they determine chemical speciation, surface interactions, selectivity, cleaning efficiency, and fouling behavior. The aim of this PhD project is to understand, predict, and engineer these local pH environments in electrochemical systems.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how local pH environments develop near electrodes and membranes in complex water matrices. You will integrate theory, modelling, and experiments to determine how local pH conditions develop, how they depend on water composition and material properties, and how they can be engineered for practical applications. The insights obtained in this project can be used to develop electrically driven, chemical-free technologies for industrial cleaning and separations.

You will be part of the Electrically-driven Chemical-free Operations (ECO) consortium, a collaboration between the Institute for Sustainable Process Technology, the University of Twente, TU Delft, the University of Groningen, the University of Copenhagen, Wageningen University & Research, and industrial partners from the food, chemical, paper, and water sectors.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • investigate how electrically induced local pH environments develop in electrochemical systems;
  • develop theoretical and computational models to predict local pH conditions in complex water matrices and investigate the impact of water composition, electrode materials, and membrane materials on pH conditions;
  • design experiments to quantify local pH environments near electrodes and membranes and integrate experimental observations and modelling results to develop design principles for electrically driven processes;
  • use the obtained insights to guide the design of electrochemical cleaning and separation technologies in close collaboration with the industrial partners in the consortium;
  • present research results at consortium meetings, international conferences, and scientific workshops and publish findings in leading peer-reviewed scientific journals.

You will work here
The research is embedded within the Environmental Technology group. You will join the Electrified Interfaces group, a research group studying transport, reactions, and selectivity at charged interfaces in environmental technologies, including electrochemical systems, membrane processes, adsorption and ion-exchange materials. You will be supervised by Dr. Jouke Dykstra and Dr. Hanieh Bazyar from TU Delft.

jobs.title: PhD: Effects of atmospheric nitrogen deposition on plant and insect diversity
jobs.description_html:
Are you a highly motivated and enthusiastic ecologist who wants to uncover how nitrogen deposition affects plant and arthropod biodiversity? Are you excited by the idea of combining large-scale fieldwork across Northwestern Europe with hands-on experiments to answer a question that matters for biodiversity conservation? If so, this PhD-position could be the perfect fit for you!

Human-driven nitrogen (N) deposition is changing ecosystems worldwide. It can cause an oversupply of nitrogen in the soil and soil acidification, and shift the balance of nutrients; not just how many nutrients are available, but also the ratios between them (their ‘stoichiometry’). This changes which plants thrive, and it changes the nutritional quality of the leaves and pollen that herbivorous and pollinating insects consume. However, we still poorly understand how these changes unfold within and among plant species, or how they cascade to affect insect performance and, ultimately, insect community diversity. As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to finding this out. You will combine field studies in Northwestern European forests across a N-deposition gradient spanning the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark and Sweden with greenhouse and controlled feeding experiments on caterpillars and solitary bees.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Design and conduct field studies across Northwestern Europe to assess how large- and small-scale gradients in N deposition affect soil chemistry, plant stoichiometry, and plant and arthropod diversity
  • Perform experiments to find out how nutrient concentrations in plant leaves and pollen affect the performance and food preferences of insect herbivore and pollinator species
  • Analyse complex ecological datasets, linking soil, plant and insect variables
  • Co-supervise MSc students conducting thesis research within the project
  • Publish your results in a PhD thesis, as well as in peer-reviewed papers

You will work here
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation (PEN) group at Wageningen University, which is led by Prof. David Kleijn. Daily supervision will be by Dr. Philippine Vergeer, Dr. Jeroen Scheper, Dr. Fons van der Plas (all PEN) and Dr. Wim Ozinga (Vegetation and Landscape Ecology, Wageningen Environmental Research).
