  • het begeleiden van scriptie- en stagestudenten die binnen het project werkzaam zijn;
  • het leveren van een actieve bijdrage aan het academische netwerk rond het onderzoeksthema;
  • samenwerken met promovendi die vergelijkbaar onderzoek doen in de ouderenzorg.

jobs.title: PhD candidate 'Quest for genetic causes of bleeding tendency'
jobs.description_html:
Job description
Within the Thrombosis and Hemostasis research group of the Laboratory of Hematology, we investigate the mechanisms that maintain the delicate balance of the hemostatic system. Disruption of this balance may result in either bleeding or thrombosis, both of which represent major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Bleeding following trauma remains one of the leading causes of death in individuals under the age of 46 years, while thrombotic diseases are among the most common causes of mortality globally, with incidence increasing with age.

Identifying the cause of a bleeding tendency remains a major challenge in clinical hematology. Despite extensive laboratory and genetic investigations, no underlying hemostatic defect can currently be identified in approximately 50% of these patients. This may be further improved by evaluating clot degradation (fibrinolysis). However, assays assessing fibrinolytic capacity are poorly standardized and are not routinely available in clinical practice.

In this PhD project, you will contribute to advancing our understanding of unexplained bleeding disorders through a combination of genomic analysis, functional characterisation and translational research approaches. The project aims to identify and characterize novel genetic variants and biological mechanisms underlying bleeding phenotypes by integrating whole-genome sequencing with functional studies in individual patients and affected families.

In parallel, the project focuses on improving diagnostic strategies for fibrinolytic disorders by characterizing current diagnostic modalities and by developing, optimizing, and validating novel assays that assess fibrinolytic potential. Together, these approaches will provide novel insights into the pathophysiology of bleeding disorders and ultimately contribute to improved diagnostic evaluation and personalized patient care.

Tasks and responsibilities as PhD researcher:
  • Analysis of genetic data.
  • Functional analysis of identified proteins.
  • Conducting systematic searches in literature databases.
  • Validation of laboratory tests.
  • Writing scientific publications for international journals.
  • Presenting results at (scientific) meetings.
  • Collaborating with promoters, supervisors and internal and external partners.

All these tasks are aimed at obtaining an academic PhD. In addition, PhD students contribute to general activities taking place within the laboratory of hematology and within the research institute.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Decoding Environmental History from Microorganisms for Living Sensors and Memory
jobs.description_html:
Help pave the future for living sensing systems by decoding microorganisms' encoding of environmental history.

Job description
Background:

Living microorganisms could transform how we sense and store information, replacing single-use electronics with inherently biodegradable systems that track environmental conditions over time. Even basic electronic sensing systems today require sensors, microcontrollers, memory, and batteries, and are often disposable. For example, temperature and humidity dataloggers used during food and vaccine transport become e-waste within weeks. Meanwhile, many species of microorganisms, such as the iridescent Flavobacteria, integrate environmental signals and store history structurally, all with minimal energy. Readout may be as simple as taking a photograph. Could these organisms replace conventional electronics and enable fully degradable, battery-less dataloggers? What's missing in realizing this future is our ability to interpret this biological record: we do not yet understand what the visual characteristics of organisms represent quantitatively, or how reliably we can recover that information.

This PhD:

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to play a formative role in understanding how to decode environmental information from living microorganisms, in pursuit of living sensing and memory systems. This effort is truly trans-disciplinary, drawing on biodesign/biotechnology, machine learning, and interaction design. This project builds on groundwork already underway in our group but is meant to be shaped substantially by the candidate's own interests and expertise.

The candidate will cultivate the living organism itself, characterize and model its visible responses to different environmental conditions, and develop and validate computational decoders that recover environmental history from an image of the living organism. Based on the found capabilities, the candidate will also design prototypes that incorporate living sensors, such as fully compostable, smart packaging for temperature and humidity monitoring for food, vaccines, or archival documents.

The PhD candidate will be situated at the intersection of the Knowledge and Intelligent Design group and the Materializing Futures group in Sustainable Design Engineering (SDE), a department within the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering.

Job requirements
We look for candidates who have:
  • A Master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Biodesign, Design Engineering, or a related field
  • Experience in building and deploying machine learning or computer vision models
  • Technical competencies in one or more of the following: bio-digital systems, biodesign, applied machine learning, computer vision, computational biology, and/or physical prototyping
  • Experience or strong interest in biodesign and hands-on interaction with living organisms
  • Experience or interest in conducting research with sound experimental design
  • Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team, communicate effectively, and take initiative
  • Prior publications and experience presenting at international conferences are assets but not requirements

Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty Industrial Design Engineering
Matching the evolution of people with the speed of the revolution of technology. This is the focus of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering (IDE). Delft designers act as a bridge between advances in technology and the needs of people, organisations and society to create products, services and systems with purpose.

IDE is a leader in design research across the application areas of mobility, sustainability and health, as well as its development of design tools and methods. A 350-strong research team and over 2,000 students work together in our inspiring hall, labs and studios.

In close cooperation with industry, the public sector and NGOs we rehearse possible futures in research and education to design for a complex future.
Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , increasing from Promovendus gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information
For more information about this vacancy, please contact Dr. Katherine Song, e-mail: k.w.song@tudelft.nl

Application procedure
Apply via the application button before 15 November 2026. Upload your CV and cover letter. Please do not submit AI-generated (or heavily doctored) content.

For information about the application procedure, please contact Ioanna Charalampous, e-mail: secretariaat-SDE-HR@tudelft.nl

Please note:
  • You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
  • As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security.
  • Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Perioperatieve Waardegedreven Zorg'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Wil jij onderzoeken hoe we de perioperatieve zorg ook in de toekomst toegankelijk, betaalbaar en van hoge kwaliteit kunnen houden? En spreekt het je aan om klinische vraagstukken over schaarste, wachtlijsten en innovatie te vertalen naar vernieuwend wetenschappelijk onderzoek? Voor een nieuw onderzoeksprogramma naar perioperatieve waardegedreven zorg zoeken wij een enthousiaste promovendus die klinisch onderzoek wil combineren met gezondheidswetenschappen, innovatie en zorgorganisatie.

Dit ga je doen
De zorg staat voor een fundamentele uitdaging. De vraag naar zorg neemt toe, terwijl geld, personeel en tijd steeds schaarser worden. Ook binnen de perioperatieve zorg betekent dit dat we voortdurend keuzes moeten maken: welke zorg levert daadwerkelijk waarde op voor patiënten, hoe zetten we onze beschikbare capaciteit zo goed mogelijk in en welke innovaties dragen werkelijk bij aan betere én efficiëntere zorg?

Binnen dit promotietraject onderzoek je hoe we de beschikbare middelen binnen de perioperatieve zorg zo doelmatig mogelijk kunnen inzetten, met behoud of verbetering van uitkomsten die voor patiënten relevant zijn. Het project bevindt zich op het snijvlak van anesthesiologie, perioperatieve geneeskunde, gezondheidswetenschappen en zorgorganisatie.

Een belangrijk onderdeel van het promotietraject richt zich op wachtlijsten voor operatieve zorg. Lange wachttijden worden meestal benaderd als een logistiek probleem, maar kunnen ook directe gevolgen hebben voor patiënten. Je onderzoekt daarom wat er met patiënten gebeurt terwijl zij wachten op een operatie. Wat zijn de gevolgen van langdurig wachten voor hun fysieke functioneren, cognitief functioneren, kwaliteit van leven en maatschappelijke participatie? En zijn er patiëntengroepen bij wie uitstel relatief weinig gevolgen heeft, terwijl anderen juist snel achteruitgaan?

Op basis van deze inzichten onderzoek je vervolgens hoe we wachtlijsttriage slimmer en efficiënter kunnen organiseren. Het doel is om verder te gaan dan prioritering op basis van alleen diagnose en wachttijd en te onderzoeken of patiëntkenmerken en het verwachte risico op achteruitgang kunnen helpen om beschikbare operatiecapaciteit beter te verdelen.

Een tweede onderzoekslijn richt zich op de daadwerkelijke waarde van innovaties in de perioperatieve zorg. Nieuwe technologieën, geneesmiddelen en behandelstrategieën kunnen de zorg verbeteren, maar vragen tegelijkertijd om personeel, tijd en financiële middelen. Je onderzoekt daarom niet alleen of innovaties klinisch effectief zijn, maar ook wat hun bredere impact is op het zorgsysteem

Het uiteindelijke doel is om wetenschappelijke kennis te ontwikkelen waarmee we beter onderbouwde keuzes kunnen maken over welke zorg we wanneer, voor wie en op welke manier moeten leveren.

Als promovendus ben je betrokken bij het volledige traject van klinisch en gezondheidswetenschappelijk onderzoek. Je ontwikkelt onderzoeksprotocollen, bereidt medisch-ethische aanvragen voor, verzamelt en analyseert onderzoeksgegevens en vertaalt de resultaten naar wetenschappelijke publicaties en concrete aanbevelingen voor de klinische praktijk.

Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:
  • Opzetten en uitvoeren van prospectieve studies naar de gevolgen van wachttijd voor patiënten.
  • Onderzoeken van veranderingen in fysiek en cognitief functioneren en kwaliteit van leven gedurende de periode op de operatiewachtlijst.
  • Identificeren van patiënt kenmerken die samenhangen met een verhoogd risico op achteruitgang tijdens het wachten.
  • Ontwikkelen en evalueren van strategieën voor efficiëntere en meer patiëntgerichte wachtlijsttriage.
  • Onderzoeken van de klinische, organisatorische en economische impact van technologische en medicamenteuze innovaties.
  • Uitvoeren en interpreteren van statistische analyses, in samenwerking met ervaren onderzoekers en statistici.
  • Presenteren van onderzoeksresultaten op nationale en internationale congressen.
  • Schrijven en publiceren van wetenschappelijke artikelen in internationale peer-reviewed tijdschriften.

De verschillende studies vormen uiteindelijk de basis voor jouw proefschrift.

jobs.title: PhD position on electrochemical synthesis of ammonia in ceramic membrane reactors
jobs.description_html:
In the Engineering and Technology Institute Groningen (ENTEG), we are looking for a talented and motivated PhD student for the development and evaluation of (electro)catalysts for electrochemical ammonia synthesis from sustainable sources in ceramic electrochemical reactors.

What are you going to do?

Ammonia is not only a key-chemical for sustaining global population, but also an intriguing carbon-free energy carrier. Ammonia, however, is the most energy intensive commodity chemical, responsible for 1-2% of energy consumption and CO2 emissions worldwide. The PhD project will support the efforts for creating innovative electrochemical membrane reactors that produce sustainable ammonia at high efficiency for decentralized applications. The PhD research will be part of the 20.3 Meuros HyNITROGEN project (https://groenvermogennl.org/rd/werkpakket-5/) of the National Growthfund GroenvermogenNL. This unique consortium brings together more than 40 companies, universities and research institutes, covering the entire value chain.

Responsibilities and tasks:


  • Synthesis and characterization of electrocatalysts at intermediate and high temperatures.
  • Fabrication of single cells with targeted characteristics.
  • Characterization of materials and relevant interfaces for their role in the reaction mechanisms.
  • Preparation of scientific articles and conference communications.
  • Teaching activities (10% of total workload), including assistance to courses, as well as supervision of Bachelor and Master students.
  • Contribution to the scientific and collaborative research environment in Chemical Engineering group and the ENTEG institute.

jobs.title: PhD position on materials development for electrically-driven water treatment processes
jobs.description_html:
In the Engineering and Technology Institute Groningen (ENTEG), we are looking for a talented and motivated PhD student for the development and evaluation of advanced electrode materials and cell component development for sustainable electrochemical water purification technologies.

What are you going to do?

In many industrial processes, chemicals are added to treat water, clean installations or separate substances from each other. Before the water can be reused or discharged, those excipients must be removed again. That costs a lot of energy, chemicals and money. The new project ECO (Electrically-driven, Chemical-free Operations) therefore chooses a different approach: prevent those excipients from being needed at all. The project will use electric fields and local pH changes close to electrodes to create the desired conditions in exactly the right place without adjusting the entire liquid.

Within ECO, the PhD candidate will collaborate with 4 other PhD researchers from the University of Twente TU Delft, Wageningen University & Research and the University of Copenhagen. Companies such as Royal Avebe, FrieslandCampina, Nobian, Shell, ISPT, Ecolab and VNP are also involved in the consortium. With five PhD candidates, the consortium will investigate in the coming years how electrically driven process technologies can contribute to cleaner and more energy-efficient industrial processes.

 

Responsibilities and tasks:

 

  • Fabrication of materials and electrochemical cells with targeted characteristics.
  • Characterization of materials and relevant interfaces for their role in the reaction mechanisms.
  • Preparation of scientific articles and conference communications.
  • Teaching activities (10% of total workload), including assistance to courses, as well as supervision of Bachelor and Master students.
  • Contribution to the scientific and collaborative research environment in Chemical Engineering group and the ENTEG institute.
  • A team player and open to collaborating in a consortium of other researchers and industrial partners, with regular consortium meetings.
  • Ability to communicate their research to people with a broad, technical background.
  • Handling the ‘uncertainty’ that the details of the project still need to be defined.
  • Contribution to defining their own research, in concerted agreement with the consortium.

jobs.title: PhD PFAS removal with activated carbon in drinking water treatment
jobs.description_html:
PFAS are among the most challenging contaminants facing drinking water utilities worldwide. Although granular activated carbon (GAC) is widely applied for PFAS removal, utilities face challenges with rapid PFAS breakthrough and as a consequence more frequent re-activation of activated carbon filters. The factors controlling breakthrough under realistic drinking water conditions remain insufficiently understood, particularly in the presence of natural organic matter (NOM) in the water matrix.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how water composition, natural organic matter, and activated carbon properties influence PFAS removal in drinking water treatment. You will combine laboratory experiments, column studies, and data analysis to identify the factors governing PFAS breakthrough at environmentally relevant conditions and concentrations.

Working closely with drinking water company Evides, you will study PFAS adsorption in realistic drinking water matrices and evaluate how differences in NOM composition affect filter performance. The insights obtained in this project will support the development of improved operational strategies for activated carbon filtration and help drinking water utilities better predict and manage PFAS breakthrough in practice.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • investigating the mechanisms governing competitive adsorption of PFAS and natural organic matter on granular activated carbon;
  • designing and conducting batch and column experiments at environmentally relevant PFAS concentrations;
  • analysing experimental data and developing predictive tools for activated carbon filter performance;
  • identifying key water quality parameters that can serve as indicators for PFAS breakthrough;
  • publishing your results in international scientific journals and presenting your work at conferences.

You will work here
The research is embedded within the Chair Group of Environmental Technology at Wageningen University & Research. The Environmental Technology group develops scientific understanding and technologies for sustainable water treatment, resource recovery, and environmental protection.

You will be part of the Electrified Interfaces team, a research group studying transport, adsorption, reactions, and selectivity at environmental interfaces. Within this team, you will contribute to research on adsorption and separation processes for water treatment and environmental applications. The team is led by dr. Jouke E. Dykstra.

The project is carried out in close collaboration with Evides, one of the largest drinking water companies in the Netherlands, providing unique opportunities to connect fundamental research with real-world drinking water challenges.

The project will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Ir. A. van der Wal and co-supervised by Dr. Ir. Jouke E. Dykstra.

jobs.title: PhD position in Communication Science: Explaining Susceptibility to Health Hacks
jobs.description_html:
Social media are full of "health hacks": short, practical tips promising quick improvements in health, wellbeing, or appearance. While many are harmless, others are misleading or even hazardous, ranging from extreme detox regimens and homemade sunscreen recipes to unproven remedies promoted as alternatives to medical treatment.

This PhD position is part of Hooked by the Health Hack, a four-year research project funded by NWO (Open Competition SSH) and carried out by Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and Erasmus University Rotterdam. The project examines how young adults encounter and evaluate health hacks, and why some hacks are so persuasive, focusing on the interplay between individual characteristics, features of the online context, and cognitive processing during exposure.

The project focuses on young adults aged 18–25. In this life stage of growing independence and identity exploration, health beliefs, routines, and self-perceptions are actively taking shape. This makes young adults a particularly relevant group for understanding both the appeal and the consequences of online health hacks.

The project will generate knowledge to inform user-centred strategies that strengthen resilience to misleading and harmful health advice online. These strategies aim to support critical evaluation while respecting people's autonomy in making their own health decisions.

The project brings together communication science, health psychology, and behavioural and cognitive science in an integrated mixed-methods design. Two closely aligned PhD tracks follow a shared three-stage research route: (1) identifying key individual and contextual factors, (2) examining the cognitive processes through which these factors shape evaluations during exposure, and (3) translating these insights into intervention strategies.

Track A uses participatory research methods; Track B uses survey and experimental research. The two PhD candidates work closely together to develop a shared conceptual model and co-create interventions. This vacancy concerns Track B, based at the Communication Science department of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.

Your duties

Your project: Track B — Survey and experimental research
Track B provides the explanatory, mechanism-testing perspective within the project: it examines how and why individual and contextual factors make people susceptible to hazardous health hacks, by testing the cognitive processes at work during actual exposure to these hacks. Your work draws on dual-process theories of reasoning, distinguishing fast, intuitive processing from slower, reflective evaluation.

Your work will include:
  • Conducting a multimodal content analysis of hazardous online health hacks.
  • Designing and fielding a large-scale panel survey on individual and contextual susceptibility factors.
  • Conducting controlled online and/or laboratory experiments on intuitive and reflective processing during exposure to health hacks.
  • Experimentally evaluating intervention strategies co-developed with Track A.
  • Integrating quantitative findings with Track A’s participatory research in a joint mixed-methods synthesis.
  • Publishing research, presenting at conferences, and contributing to knowledge exchange with practice partners.

jobs.title: PhD on natural visual patterns, mental wellbeing, and overheating resilience
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by the influence of nature on our emotions and behaviour? Passionate about nature-inspired facade design and its influence on occupant comfort and wellbeing? Eager to embark on a multidisciplinary research project and collaborate with industry partners? If so, then this PhD position might be perfect for you.

Information
Can we reduce stress, thermal discomfort and energy consumption for cooling in homes by harnessing visual exposure to nature-inspired facade designs? Can we disentangle the beneficial effects of daylight and nature exposure through windows? How can we best navigate the trade-off between access to view and the amount and quality of daylight and nature content provided by a nature-inspired façade? These are some of the scientific challenges you will work on in this PhD project.

This PhD position is part of the wider ΝWO KIC project “Nature4Homes: Nature-driven building skin interventions for energy efficiency, occupant comfort, health, and biodiversity in dwellings”, which brings together the domains of building engineering, building physics, environmental psychology, meteorology, and thermophysiology to develop nature-driven building skin solutions that enhance occupant health and comfort while reducing cooling demand. This PhD project focuses specifically on the domains of environmental psychology, lighting research, and building physics.

You will conduct your research within the Human-Technology Interaction group (HTI) at TU/e, which has a long history in lighting research and environmental psychology, with a secondment at the Environmental & Climate Design section at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), which has extensive expertise in building physics and indoor environmental quality.

In this PhD, you will investigate whether visual patterns from nature across different layers of the building skin (e.g., the façade itself, the view to the outside) within an occupant’s field of view can support mental wellbeing, increase acceptance, and enhance tolerance to visual and thermal discomfort indoors, particularly during periods of summer overheating. To address these questions, you will review the literature, perform experiments in virtual reality and real conditions, co-create nature-inspired façade elements, and test them in field studies. Your work would include collecting self-reported, physiological, and environmental data, and apply building simulation, computer vision, and advanced statistical methods for their analysis. The project also involves close collaboration with industry partners such as shading system manufacturers to develop nature-inspired façade interventions. These will be tested at the “Green Village” living lab housing of TU Delft. Throughout your PhD, you will be supervised by Dr. Kynthia Chamilothori (main supervisor) and Prof. Yvonne de Kort (promotor) at the Human-Technology Interaction group of the Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), as well as Dr. Eleonora Brembilla (co-promotor) at the Environmental & Climate Design section at TU Delft. You will be based at TU/e with a secondment at TU Delft.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Agentic AI-Driven Experiments for Materials Discovery
jobs.description_html:
PhD candidate who will join the Autonomous Energy Materials Discovery (AMD) group at DIFFER, working with researchers and engineers who are developing autonomous laboratory technologies.

The project is carried out in close collaboration with an industrial partner developing generative AI for materials discovery. The position suits a candidate with strong programming skills, from computer science, AI, physics, chemistry or materials science, who wants to work at the interface of agentic AI, laboratory automation and materials science, and who is happy to spend a substantial part of the project in the lab.

Roughly one third of your time will go to the digital workflow and two thirds to experimental work. Training and technical support are provided for all instruments. AI methods can propose material candidates far faster than they can be synthesized and validated. You will help close this gap by building an agentic AI workflow that turns AI-proposed alloy compositions into executable synthesis and characterization plans, and by generating the experimental evidence that shows which candidates can actually be made. You will produce material libraries with a high-throughput nanoparticle printer and characterise them with micro-XRF and SEM. Successful, partial and failed outcomes will be captured in a structured, machine readable dataset to support AI model development and give feedback on material realizability.

jobs.title: PhD Grip op health hacks: Onderzoek naar gezondheidsadvies op sociale media
jobs.description_html:
Waarom kan een snelle gezondheidstip op sociale media zo overtuigend klinken, ook als die misleidend of mogelijk zelfs schadelijk is? Sociale media staan vol met ‘health hacks’: korte, praktische adviezen die snelle verbeteringen beloven voor gezondheid, welzijn of uiterlijk. Sommige zijn onschadelijk, maar andere zijn misleidend of potentieel gevaarlijk. Denk aan extreme detox-kuren, recepten voor zelfgemaakte zonnebrandcrème of alternatieve behandelingen die worden aangeprezen als vervanging van wetenschappelijk onderbouwde zorg.

Deze promotieplaats maakt deel uit van het ‘Hooked by the Health Hack’-project, een vierjarig, door de NWO gefinancierd onderzoeksproject onder leiding van de Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam en de Erasmus Universiteit Rotterdam (https://www.nwo.nl/en/researchprogrammes/open-competition-ssh/granted-projects). Het project onderzoekt waarom deze ‘health hacks’ zo overtuigend kunnen zijn. Daarbij staat de wisselwerking centraal tussen individuele kenmerken, kenmerken van de online context en cognitieve processen tijdens de blootstelling.

Het project richt zich op jongvolwassenen (18-25). Deze levensfase wordt gekenmerkt door toenemende zelfstandigheid, identiteitsverkenning en groeiende verantwoordelijkheid voor gezondheidsgerelateerde keuzes. Juist omdat gezondheidsopvattingen, routines en zelfbeelden actief worden gevormd tijdens deze levensfase, is deze groep bijzonder relevant voor onderzoek naar de aantrekkingskracht en mogelijke gevolgen van deze online ‘health hacks’.

Het interdisciplinaire project verbindt communicatiewetenschap, gezondheidspsychologie en gedrags- en cognitiewetenschap in een geïntegreerd ‘mixed-methods’ design. Het project levert kennis op die kan helpen bij het ontwikkelen van strategieën die jongvolwassenen weerbaarder maken tegen misleidend en mogelijk schadelijk gezondheidsadvies op sociale media. Deze strategieën zijn erop gericht om jongvolwassenen te ondersteunen bij het kritisch beoordelen van informatie, terwijl hun zelfstandigheid en keuzevrijheid in het nemen van gezondheidsbeslissingen gerespecteerd blijven.

De twee promotietrajecten (Traject A: participatief onderzoek en Traject B: enquête- en experimenteel onderzoek) doorlopen beiden drie fasen: het identificeren van belangrijke individuele en contextuele factoren, het onderzoeken van de cognitieve processen die beoordelingen tijdens blootstelling beïnvloeden, en het vertalen van deze inzichten naar interventiestrategieën. Elk traject heeft zijn eigen methodologische focus, terwijl beide promovendi samenwerken om een gezamenlijk conceptueel model te ontwikkelen en gezamenlijk interventies te ontwerpen.

Functieomschrijving
Ben je geïnteresseerd in de vraag waarom jongvolwassenen zich aangetrokken voelen tot snel gezondheidsadvies op sociale media, hoe ze de informatie die ze online tegenkomen beoordelen, en hoe we hen kunnen helpen hun weg te vinden in mogelijk misleidende informatie? Dan is dit promotieproject wellicht iets voor jou.

Het PhD traject Begrijpen van ‘health hacks’: Een participatief onderzoek naar snel gezondheidsadvies in dagelijks mediagebruik (Traject A) biedt het ervaringsgerichte, praktijkgerichte perspectief binnen het grotere project: het onderzoekt hoe jongvolwassenen in hun dagelijkse digitale leven in aanraking komen met ‘health hacks’, deze interpreteren en ermee omgaan. Je maakt gebruik van een participatieve onderzoeksbenadering en werkt samen met sociale media-gebruikers in de leeftijd van 18–25 jaar als medeonderzoekers in plaats van als passieve onderzoeksparticipanten.

Je werkzaamheden omvatten:
  • Het uitvoeren van een multimodale inhoudsanalyse van gevaarlijke online ‘health hacks’
  • Het ontwerpen en begeleiden van participatieve workshops met jongvolwassen gebruikers van sociale media en ‘content creators’

jobs.title: PhD student - From brain circuits of threat to neurofeedback in humans
jobs.description_html:
The Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience and Maastricht University Medical Center are looking for an enthusiastic and ambitious PhD student to join a collaborative translational neuroscience project investigating how the brain controls responses to threat and stress. The project is part of a new programme aimed at strengthening the connection between fundamental neuroscience and clinical psychiatry.
Maladaptive responses to threat are an important feature of psychiatric conditions such as anxiety disorders, PTSD and depression. In this project, we will identify brain regions that can regulate threat responses and investigate whether these regions can ultimately be targeted using real-time fMRI neurofeedback.
The project provides a unique opportunity to work across the boundary between fundamental systems neuroscience and human translational neuroscience.

What will you do
You will first work at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) in Amsterdam, in the laboratory of Prof. Alexander Heimel. Using mouse models of innate defensive behavior, you will identify a brain region that can regulate defensive behavior. You will use state-of-the-art approaches including behavioral analysis of innate defensive responses, activity-dependent neuronal tagging using TRAP2, viral and monosynaptic rabies tracing, optogenetic manipulation of neural circuits, fiber photometry and quantitative analysis of neural and behavioral data.
In the second part of the project, you will work with Prof. David Linden and colleagues at Maastricht UMC+, translating the circuit identified in mice to humans. You will use 7T fMRI to translate the findings from the first part and develop a real-time fMRI neurofeedback paradigm through which participants learn to regulate the identified brain region.
The ultimate aim is to develop a biologically grounded approach to neurofeedback in which targets are selected because they have a demonstrated causal role in controlling threat circuitry. The work may provide a foundation for future neurofeedback interventions in patients with stress-related psychiatric disorders.

What will you contribute
We are looking for a candidate who:
  • has, or will soon obtain, a master's degree in neuroscience, biomedical sciences, medicine, psychology, cognitive neuroscience, or a related discipline
  • has a strong interest in how neural circuits generate behavior
  • is enthusiastic about working at the interface between animal and human neuroscience
  • is interested in learning a broad range of experimental and computational techniques
  • enjoys quantitative analysis and has or is willing to develop data-analysis skills
  • wants to interact with psychiatrists and clinical psychologists to develop new paradigms
  • has good communication skills and enjoys working collaboratively
  • has a good command of spoken and written English

Experience with animal behavior, optogenetics, viral approaches, microscopy, programming/data analysis, MRI or human experimental research would be an advantage, but we do not expect applicants to already have expertise in all these areas. More important is a strong scientific curiosity and willingness to learn techniques from both animal systems neuroscience and human neuroimaging.
Because part of the project involves experimental work with mice, the candidate should be comfortable working with laboratory animals.

What we offer
You will join two complementary and highly interactive research environments. At the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience, you will receive training in causal circuit neuroscience and the neural mechanisms underlying innate behavior. At Maastricht UMC+, you will gain expertise in human neuroimaging, high-field 7T MRI and real-time neurofeedback within a clinical neuroscience environment. The project includes regular interaction with both research groups and joint supervision throughout the PhD.
The project is funded for four years. The first two years will primarily focus on circuit discovery and causal experiments in mice, followed by human circuit validation and neurofeedback experiments during years three and four. Some travel or/and movement allowance is budgeted for making the collaboration between Amsterdam and Maastricht smooth.
You will have opportunities to present your work at international conferences, collaborate with researchers across neuroscience, psychiatry and neuroimaging, and develop a profile as a genuinely cross-species translational neuroscientist.

Research environment
The project is a collaboration between the group of Prof. Alexander Heimel at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam and the group of Prof. David Linden at Maastricht UMC.
The Heimel group investigates the neural circuits that transform sensory information and internal state into behavior, with particular expertise in visual and innate behaviors, circuit tracing and causal manipulation in mice.
The Maastricht team has extensive expertise in fMRI neurofeedback, high-field imaging and clinical neuroscience, including subcortical neurofeedback targets. The project will also involve interaction with researchers experienced in real-time and 7T fMRI.

Information
For questions about the position, please contact Alexander Heimel (a.heimel@nin.knaw.nl) or David Linden (david.linden@maastrichtuniversity.nl). There is no deadline for the application, the vacancy will be closed if a suitable candidate has been found.

jobs.description_html:
Team
A PhD position is available in the Neurogenesis & Neurodegeneration group at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam. The Neurogenesis & Neurodegeneration laboratory led by Evgenia Salta employs transcriptomics and other molecular and cellular approaches to map the cellular and molecular complexity of the adult human hippocampus and dissect the biological pathways that are deregulated in dementia. The team employs primarily human postmortem brain tissue and iPSC reprogramming.

Project
The project is funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) Open Competition and is a collaboration between the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) and the Swammerdam Institute of Life Sciences (SILS) at the University of Amsterdam.
Repeated mild head injuries, the kind sustained by athletes, veterans, and victims of domestic violence, are increasingly linked to long-term memory problems and a higher risk of dementia later in life. Strikingly, these lasting effects can occur even when no visible brain damage is present. Yet, we still don't understand how repeated injury leads to memory decline, and there are currently no treatments that address these long-term cognitive consequences.

Beyond helping high-risk groups, this work may also shed light on Alzheimer's and other dementias that share similar underlying processes.

The research will be performed at the Salta lab at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam. This is a joint project with the group of Carlos Fitzsimons at the SILS, University of Amsterdam.
This study is a follow up of our previously published work:
https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00142-6
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49299-6

What you will do
In this project, you will investigate what happens in the brain after repetitive mild traumatic brain injury, focusing on the hippocampus, the brain region central to memory. We are particularly interested in long-lasting inflammatory and neurogenic alterations and the cells involved in them, including microglia, astrocytes and immature neurons. By uncovering these mechanisms, you will help us to identify cellular or molecular targets that could guide the development of future therapies.

As a PhD candidate in our group, you will use state-of-the art single-nucleus RNA sequencing pipelines to process postmortem human brain from donors with a record of traumatic brain injury. You will be in charge of sample collection and stratification and apply advanced computational pipelines to identify cellular and molecular programs involved in the hippocampal response to injury and the downstream cognitive effects. Ultimately, you will establish in vitro human cell models to probe causal relationships between candidate targets and cellular phenotypes.

jobs.title: PhD position in genome evolution and architecture in unicellular eukaryotes
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by how eukaryotic genomes evolve? Do you want to look beyond model organisms and point mutations to uncover the complexity of genome evolution? Are you excited to use computational approaches to explore how genome architecture shapes evolution in a collaborative and stimulating environment? We offer a PhD position in our diverse research team in the Laboratory of Microbiology at Wageningen University & Research. As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how 3D chromosome folding influence how the genomes of unicellular eukaryotes evolve.

What will you do?
In this PhD project, you will study the genome evolution and architecture – including 3D folding - of understudied unicellular eukaryotes, using the latest computational approaches.

As PhD candidate in our lab, you will:
  • utilize cutting-edge bioinformatics tools to trace the evolution of genomes, genes and proteins, including phylogenetic analyses and reconstructions;
  • use new genomic data to characterize the large-scale and small-scale genome architectures of understudied eukaryotic microbes;
  • deepen our understanding of eukaryotes’ diversification and origins;
  • have the opportunity to pursue your own research questions and implement your ideas;
  • work independently and develop your own research questions within the project;
  • contribute to teaching in our courses and supervising BSc and MSc thesis students;
  • work in a stimulating environment that combines evolutionary and cellular research on eukaryotes and prokaryotes, in a team operating at the forefront of unravelling the deep origins of eukaryotic cells, and we are expanding our explorations of the understudied world of eukaryotic microbes.

Even though this is a computational project, it offers possibilities to work on eukaryotic microbes in the wet lab.

Why?
Understanding how genomes evolve is fundamental to explaining species diversity and adaptation. Compared with prokaryotes, eukaryotic genomes show a greater structural and functional plasticity, with a larger genome size, a higher proportion of non-coding regions and a more complex 3D chromosome organization. Notably, genome evolution is not only driven by small mutations, but also by larger changes, including chromosome rearrangements and horizontal gene transfer. How and why such changes occur is still an open question, in particular for eukaryotic microbes, which dominate the eukaryotic tree of life but remain poorly studied. Recent studies, conducted in model organisms, suggest that these changes are induced by how chromosomes are folded in 3D. This 3D folding of the chromosomes typically allows distant genomic regions to interact. To gain a deeper understanding of genome evolution, including in non-model organisms, taking 3D chromosome folding into account is a promising direction.

You will work here
This PhD position is embedded within the Laboratory of Microbiology, and part of the Genome Evolution and Dynamics in Eukaryotes (GEDE) group, which is led by Dr. Jolien van Hooff. You will be co-supervised by Dr. Ursula Oggenfuss. We aim to get this position filled by March 2027.

jobs.title: PhD Position Indoor Thermal Natural Variation for Heat Resilience
jobs.description_html:
How do residents experience changing indoor temperatures? As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will combine citizen science, field data and modelling to help develop healthier and more energy-efficien.


Job description
Hot weather events are increasing, making adaptation of existing dwellings increasingly important to protect residents from unhealthy indoor conditions and limit future energy use for cooling. While we are instinctively drawn to natural conditions, residents are most of the time exposed to static environmental indoor conditions. Hot weather events can even amplify static conditions, for example through constant mechanical cooling. To support health and to lower energy use, current guidelines and standards allow for some variation. Yet we still know too little about how residents perceive and accept natural variation in indoor thermal conditions, and how this relates to building characteristics and resident behaviour.

As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will conduct research within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes project. Your research will address how natural variation in thermal conditions influences residents’ perceptions, acceptance and interactions with the building envelope under current and future Dutch conditions. This a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today: adapting existing dwellings to climate change while enhancing quality of life.

Using a citizen science approach, you will investigate indoor and outdoor thermal and ventilation conditions in existing dwellings in different regions of the Netherlands. You will combine measurements of environmental conditions with information about residents’ perceptions and behaviour and relevant building characteristics. A key part of your research will be developing new methods to characterize natural variation of indoor conditions in relation to outdoor conditions, and predicting this variation using climate scenarios and data collected in dwellings, in co-creation with residents, housing corporations and industy partners.

You will join the Architectural Engineering + Technology (AE&T) Department at the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, TU Delft, under the supervision of AnneMarie Eijkelenboom and Philomena M. Bluyssen and Gert-Jan Steeneveld of the Meteorology and Air Quality Section at Wageningen University and Research. Join us in developing the next generation of climate-resilient building envelopes.


Job description
As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will explore how nature-based building skins can transform existing homes into healthier, cooler and more sustainable living environments. Working at the intersection of building physics, architecture, ecology and user-centered design, you will develop innovative façade solutions that combine vegetation, circular materials and smart ventilation strategies to improve indoor comfort without relying on energy-intensive cooling systems.

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today: adapting existing housing to climate change while enhancing biodiversity and quality of life. Your work will move beyond theory. Through co-creation with residents and industry partners, full-scale prototyping and real-world testing, you will help bring innovative solutions from concept to demonstration.

While green façades and other nature-based solutions have demonstrated their potential to reduce surface temperatures and improve urban microclimates, limited knowledge exists on how integrated nature-based building skins can simultaneously deliver indoor heat resilience, ventilation performance, biodiversity enhancement, circularity and long-term user acceptance within affordable retrofit solutions for existing housing. As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will conduct research within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes project. Your research will focus on developing and demonstrating natural building skins for the heat-resilient retrofit of existing dwellings. The ambition is to create an affordable and easy-to-install building-envelope solution that integrates nature-based solutions and passive cooling strategies to mitigate overheating and regulate indoor conditions, while supporting biodiversity and circular renovation.

jobs.title: PhD position Agentic AI for Resource Management and Resilient Operations in 6G
jobs.description_html:
Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications!

To view all our current PhD vacancies within this project visit: 6G Flagship.

Job description
Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge.

Future 6G infrastructures will involve multiple specialized AI agents that manage radio, transport, computing, and service resources across different domains and vendors. Although individual agents may optimize local objectives, their actions can interact, conflict, or compete for shared resources. This PhD will develop learning methods for coordinating such agentic systems under changing network conditions, incomplete information, and operational constraints. The research will build on constrained and optimistic online learning, distributed learning, and online game-theoretic methods. The developed framework will be studied in two main application areas: multi-domain resource management for AI-enabled services, and resilient network operation, including fault diagnosis, root-cause analysis, and autonomous remediation. The methods will be validated through FNS use-cases, network data, and experimental infrastructure in collaboration with industrial partners.

You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Groundwater Care and the Politics of Transformation (Peru)
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to pursue a PhD in political ecology, development studies or environmental humanities? Are you interested in (ground-)water? This PhD project – that examines the practices that individuals and communities in Peru engage in to care for, protect, rejuvenate and/or recharge the groundwaters they rely on for irrigating their crops – might be of interest to you.

Caring for groundwater
The PhD study is part of a larger project funded by an ERC Advanced Grant: “Aquiverse: a collaborative study of groundwater care to re-think, improve and support its governance”. The project aspires to learn from what irrigators and other water users do to protect and share the aquifers that they depend on for their livelihoods. Acknowledging how the over-exploitation of aquifers is linked to neo-liberal processes of agricultural intensification, the project is interested in exploring whether such caring practices can form part of a politics of transformation.

The project engages in collaborative studies of six organized initiatives of caring for aquifers – of recharge, conservation, recovery - in three countries (India, Peru and Morocco). How do these initiatives shape people’s connections with aquifers and with each other, and how do they (re-)configure possibilities for living and relating? The Peru cases centre around so-called pozas used for aquifer recharge on the desert coast and on the revival of traditional rainwater harvesting techniques in the high Andes mountains.

Connecting thick empirical description with methodological-theoretical engagement, the project aims to contribute to (among others) reflections on transformational politics, human-environment interactions and collective action (or communing). A central notion in the project is “aquiverse” – a combination of the words ‘aquifer’ and ‘pluriverse’ – . It denotes both a novel transdisciplinary understanding of groundwater and a new method to compare groundwater governance across cases.

The PhD project will have to be completed in 4 years. You will work closely with your supervisors, including Margreet Zwarteveen, as well as with the rest of the Aquiverse research team which includes another PhD fellow and 2 postdoctoral researchers (Carolina Dominguez-Guzman and Lisa Bossenbroek).

What are you going to do
As part of your PhD project, you are expected to engage in two or more of the following activities:
  • a detailed ethnographic description of the everyday practices of people involved in the selected initiatives of caring for groundwater.
  • A precise institutional and hydro-geological documentation and assessment of the functioning and performance of these initiatives.
  • An in-depth historical and political-ecological analysis of how the depletion of groundwater is related to neo-liberal processes of water-based agrarian change and the politics of water (re-)allocation.
  • An identification, documentation and analysis of how irrigators navigate pressures – to individualize, intensify or indeed over-exploit – in the study sites.

What do you have to offer
You are someone who:
  • Has a (research) master’s degree in human Geography, Development Studies, Anthropology, or a closely related field.
  • Is interested in (the role of water in) processes of agrarian change.
  • Would like to contribute to (feminist) theorizations of human/society-environment relations (political ecology, environmental humanities).
  • Has some familiarity with agrarian Peru and looks forward to spending time in remote rural areas.
  • Has experience with ethnographic research methods but is not afraid of quantification.
  • Has some understanding of or is curious to learn about hydrogeology.
  • Enjoys engaging in inter-and transdisciplinary collaborations.
  • Possesses excellent academic writing and communication skills in English
  • Can communicate well in Spanish and preferably also in Quechua. Some knowledge of French, Arabic (Darija) or Hindi is an advantage.
  • Cares for their colleagues and collaborators.
  • Likes experimenting with creative methods of research and engagement.

What else do we offer you
We offer a temporary employment contract of 38 hours per week for a maximum term of four years. The initial employment is for one year. Following a positive assessment, this term will be extended by a maximum of three years, which should result in the conferral of a doctorate. You will attend courses offered by the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research (AISSR) and the Graduate School of Social Sciences as part of the PhD programme.

For this position the University Job Classification profile “Promovendus” applies. Your salary will be €3.204,00 gross per month in the first year and will increase to €4.051,00 in the final year, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week and in keeping with the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities. We additionally offer an extensive package of secondary benefits, including 8% holiday allowance and a year-end bonus of 8.3%. The UvA offers excellent possibilities for further professional development and education.

In addition, we offer:
  • a position in which initiative and input are highly valued
  • an enthusiastic and warm team that is open to new colleagues
  • an inspiring academic and international working environment in the heart of Amsterdam.

In this department, you will work
Through research, education and social engagement, members of the GID group set out to foster a more just, sustainable and inclusive world. We do this by engaging with, examining and challenging dominant patterns and understandings of ‘development’, as a contested notion, and its relationship to (in)justice. We critically examine what has been done in the name of ‘development’ in the past and the present, and how the impacts of ‘development’ have been distributed among people and places. These insights allow us to (re)imagine the future of development as more just, sustainable and inclusive. As a team, GID advances academic excellence, contributes to methodological innovation and focuses on impact. We work across academic disciplines and engage with social actors in sectors beyond academia and integrate diverse knowledges into our work.

Since its inception in the 1990s, the GID group has responded to and set research agendas for understanding the ever-changing field of International Development Studies. Transformations in political, environmental, economic, social, cultural and technological contexts can contribute to progress, but also perpetuate injustices within and between population groups. As an interdisciplinary team, we scrutinise the underlying assumptions and premises of those transformations that exacerbate inequality and injustice, from diverse perspectives and using different research methods. Our work focuses on linking up a range of themes to governance and inclusive development within and across the Global South and North, East and West. In addition, our research applies relational perspectives, highlighting the transnational, translocal and inter-scalar nature of development processes and their impacts.

If you recognize yourself in this profile and are interested in the role, we look forward to receiving your application that should include (in one pdf document):
  • An application letter (max 2 pages) describing your motivation and qualifications
  • Your CV
  • One writing sample of no longer than 25 pages. If you want to include a longer text (such as a master’s thesis), please provide an excerpt.
  • Contact information for two academic references. Letters of recommendation are not necessary.

You can apply via the red button until 2 November 2026.

In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be given preference over external candidates.

For questions about the vacancy, you can contact: Prof. Margreet Zwarteveen m.z.zwarteveen@uva.nl
