jobs.title: PhD: Moss traits and fire ignition in high-latitude peatland & tundra ecosystems
jobs.description_html:
Are you intrigued by interactions between vegetation and fire? Are you passionate about lab-, field-, and remote sensing-based research? Do you like solving scientific puzzles? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to explore how moss traits affect fire ignitability in high-latitude ecosystems.

Northern ecosystems, including boreal peatlands and tundra, are warming faster than almost anywhere else on Earth, which is changing their structure and functioning. Permafrost thaw and increasing fire frequency threaten to turn these ecosystems from carbon sinks into carbon, further accelerating climate change. Bryophytes (including mosses) dominate the vegetation across much of these carbon-dense ecosystems. Because of their unique water-retention and insulating properties, they largely determine how susceptible these regions are to severe wildfires. This PhD project examines the relationship between bryophyte functional traits and fire dynamics at the plant, ecosystem, and biome scales, combining lab experiments, fieldwork, and remote sensing. Building on the PEN research line on vegetation-climate feedbacks, your work will advance our understanding of the functional role of bryophytes in fire dynamics and help improve fire risk assessments for these vulnerable systems.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Developing methods and designing and executing experiments to test moss ignitability
  • Conducting fieldwork in high-latitude ecosystems, including vegetation surveys, monitoring environmental conditions during and after fires, and possibly drone-based observations
  • Analysing remote sensing data and global vegetation databases
  • Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting it at national and international conferences
  • Co-supervising BSc and MSc students

You will work here
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation group, specifically within the Vegetation-Climate Feedbacks team. You will be co-supervised by Dr. Thomas Janssen, Dr. José van Paassen and Dr. Juul Limpens.

jobs.title: PhD position in-Operando Neuromorphic OptoElectronics
jobs.description_html:
As a PhD student, you will work on a project focused on developing in-situ optical sensing for polymer-based electronics: using light to non-invasively inspect, understand, and improve their stability and performance, with the aim to develop energy-efficient optoelectronic devices. You’ll select and design conductive polymers, fabricate electronics devices, then build in-situ UV-Vis/Raman/surface enhanced Raman spectroscopies platform to reveal hidden processes such as interfacial charge transfer, redox switching, doping and dedoping, morphology dynamics, and local electric field effects. You’ll model electrical and optical inputs and responses for energy-efficient computing as a proof of concept.

What sets this opportunity apart:

World-class facilities: Conduct your research at the University of Twente, a vibrant campus in the east of the Netherlands equipped with state-of-the-art facilities.

Expert guidance: Work alongside leading experts Dr. Ivana Qianqi Lin and Prof. Christian Nijhuis in the Hybrid Materials for Opto-electronics group, as well as renowned expert Prof. Frederik Wurm in the Sustainable Polymer Chemistry group, all within the Department of Molecules and Materials.

Interdisciplinary collaboration: You’ll be part of the MESA+ Institute embedded in the world-class NanoLab infrastructure, and collaborate closely with Department of Applied NanoPhotonics, and Centre for Brain-Inspired Computing.

This is your chance to contribute to a more sustainable future while advancing your research career at a leading European university. Join us in shaping the future of hybrid materials and forefront technologies!

jobs.title: PhD to study shelled zooplankton in a changing Arctic Ocean
jobs.description_html:
Do you have a passion for the ocean and would like to join expeditions to the Arctic to explore how deep-sea life is connected to our climate? Do you enjoy working in an interdisciplinary research setting? Pursuing a PhD at Naturalis in Leiden (the Netherlands) means working on research with a global impact — contributing directly to biodiversity. And you'll be well supported every step of the way. With 3,200 m² of state-of-the-art lab facilities, housed in a museum with more than 40 million natural history objects, dedicated mentorship, and access to our broad international network, this position offers everything you need to thrive as a scientist.

As a PhD student ...

  • you will find yourself in a unique research environment, inspired by passionate scientists from a wide range of disciplines (e.g., taxonomy, evolution, ecology, and oceanography).
  • You will receive dedicated supervision from an experienced researcher and work closely with several international experts and collaborators with whom you’ll regularly exchange ideas about your research. This will help you to develop a strong academic profile.
  • You will build valuable connections by participating in both the academic and social activities of our PhD community.


This is what you'll be doing
In this PhD project, you will investigate the role of shelled zooplankton (planktonic snails or pteropods) in the biological carbon pump in a changing Arctic Ocean. You will assess the contribution to carbon fluxes and the tropic role of shelled pteropods by collecting depth-stratified samples on expeditions to the Arctic Ocean with a large scientific vessel and analyzing time series samples from the Long-Term Ecological (LTER) observatory HAUSGARTEN operated by the German Alfred-Wegener Institute (AWI). You will use a combination of state-of-the-art morphological and molecular techniques to quantify carbon fluxes as well as the ecology of current and past populations of shelled pteropods.

You will be working within an international team of Dutch research institutes (University of Amsterdam, Naturalis Biodiversity Center, and the NIOZ Royal Netherlands Institute of Sea Research) and the German Alfred-Wegener Institute (AWI) for Polar and Sea Research on an ambitious larger project including three positions (two PhD students and one Post-Doc): Plumbing the biological pump: Linking missing carbon flows between pelagic and benthic ecosystems in a changing Arctic Ocean (C-CONNECT).

The global biological carbon pump mediates the cycling and storage of carbon in our ocean and helps to regulate Earth’s climate. Arctic waters are amongst, if not the most, rapidly changing in terms of temperatures, sea-ice cover, and acidification. However, our understanding of climate-change impacts that affect the Arctic carbon pump’s size and speed of flows remains incomplete.

The main aim in C-CONNECT is to perform plumbing to the Arctic biological carbon pump by connecting important missing parts, e.g., shelled zooplankton and benthic faunal communities to the carbon cycle. C-CONNECT will improve the ability to project how future Arctic carbon cycling evolves under continued climate change and will provide essential information on Arctic ecosystem services to aid (policy and management) decision making.

This PhD position in the C-CONNECT project is funded by NWO (Dutch research council).

Here's what we have to offer

  • A gross monthly starting salary of € 3,567.00 for a full-time contract (36 hours).
  • A contract of one year, to be extended by 3 years after successful evaluation.
  • End-of-year bonus of 3.4% of your gross annual salary and 8% holiday pay.
  • 27 days of leave per year with full-time employment. Plus 1 extra day that you can use for a holiday that is important to you.
  • Commuting allowance depending on your means of transport.
  • Pension scheme via PFZW, where Naturalis pays 60% of your premium.
  • Plenty of development opportunities. We support your growth and give you unlimited access to the online training platform Goodhabitz.
  • Fascinating knowledge events. These help you stay up to date on the latest developments in both your own field and outside it, such as our lectures and gatherings on various (scientific) topics. You can also attend – or take part in – the fascinating internal information session Naturalis Draait Door.
  • Nice extras such as discounts on software and hardware for private use, collective health insurance plans, and a bicycle scheme. You’ll also enjoy discounts in our museum restaurant and unlimited free access to our award-winning museum for you and your family.
  • Fun team outings. We also get together for drinks every month, organize an annual BBQ and a fantastic New Year's party. Not your scene? That's fine too, of course. All team activities are voluntary.
  • A unique work environment in a state-of-the-art building where you will feel proud to work every single day – we guarantee it!


The World Lies at Your Feet!
Literally. Whatever your role may be, you contribute to the preservation of our planet on a daily basis. Naturalis Biodiversity Center ...

  • is the national research and knowledge institute and a key player in biodiversity data and infrastructures.
  • houses one of the largest natural history collections in the world.
  • welcomes 500,000 museum visitors per year.
  • collaborates with universities, expertise centers, and museums around the world.
  • has a staff of diverse colleagues in various functions and with many different nationalities, with whom you will work together in an informal atmosphere.


This is your team
Within your research group Marine Evolution and Ecology at Naturalis, you will work closely with Dr. Katja Peijnenburg. The project C-CONNECT will consist of collaborators from the University of Amsterdam (UvA) and the Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research (NIOZ), as well as from the German Alfred-Wegener Institute (AWI) for Polar and Sea Research. You will also be part of the Naturalis PhD community — a close-knit group of around 50 PhD candidates and postdocs with whom you can share experiences and participate in training sessions, workshops, and peer review meetings.

What you bring to the table
You are capable of working independently while also proactively seeking collaboration — whether with your supervisors, fellow researchers, or external partners. You're known for your systematic and accurate approach, driven by strong perseverance. You are confident in asking critical questions to further your research and you identify opportunities, effectively engaging others with your ideas. You are a team player and eager to disseminate your research findings, whether through public lectures or publications.

In addition, you possess:

  • A completed Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as biology, oceanography, (molecular) ecology.
  • Experience with genetic methods (DNA barcoding, metabarcoding) and/or sampling on oceanographic expeditions.
  • Some knowledge of statistics and computer language, like R.
  • Strong proficiency in English.


Become Our New PhD student

  • Upload your CV (max 3 pages) and motivation letter (max 1 page), including the contact details of two referees in one PDF via the application button no later than October 29 CET, 2026.
  • Want to know more about the position before you apply? Contact Katja Peijnenburg via email to katja.peijnenburg@naturalis.nl.
  • For more information about the application procedure, you can send an email to our colleagues in the HR department via sollicitaties@naturalis.nl.


We are managing the recruitment for this vacancy ourselves; unsolicited acquisition is therefore not desired.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Understanding Cellular Mechanisms Driving Traumatic Brain Injury-Associated Dementia
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about uncovering what happens to the brain during impact, subsequent injury, and how the injury evolves, or resolves, afterwards? Then we are inviting you to join our interdisciplinary research teams to explore the long-term effects of repetitive mild traumatic brain injury (rmTBI) in both humans and mouse models.

Join Us!
Repeated mild head injuries, the kind sustained by athletes, veterans, and victims of domestic violence, are increasingly linked to long-term memory problems and a higher risk of dementia later in life. Strikingly, these lasting effects can occur even when no visible brain damage is present. Yet, we still don't understand how repeated injury leads to memory decline, and there are currently no treatments that address these long-term cognitive consequences.

In this project, our main goal is to dissect the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying traumatic brain injury (TBI)-associated neurodegeneration, memory decline and dementia. To this end we will study how rmTBI triggers long-term neuroinflammation and cellular and functional changes in the hippocampus, leading to memory impairment, as TBI may weaken the brain’s resilience, accelerating hippocampus-related memory decline.

This project is a collaboration between the Fitzsimons lab at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences, University of Amsterdam (UvA) and the Salta lab at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN). The complementary expertise and conceptual understanding of brain insult models, specifically TBI mouse models, transcriptomics, detailed analysis of cell morphology, advanced microscopy techniques, neurodegenerative diseases, adult neurogenesis analysis in human brain samples and human iPSC culture and derivation, establish an ideal conceptual and technical synergy, making our team very well-suited to identify disease mechanisms involved in neurodegenerative diseases associated with repetitive TBI.

This project is funded by the Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO), Open Competition Domain Science – M2 grant and will be performed at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences, University of Amsterdam. It is a follow up of our previous published work on traumatic brain injury and adult hippocampal neurogenesis:

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49299-6

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41590-022-01208-z

https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00142-6?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS1934590926001426%3Fshowall%3Dtrue

https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00037-8?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS1934590926000378%3Fshowall%3Dtrue

We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

This is what you will do
As a PhD candidate in our group, you will characterize the short- and long-term effects of rmTBI on the fate of resident neural stem cells in the hippocampus, including neurogenesis, astrogliogenesis, reactive astrogliosis, production of inflammatory mediators and, microglia activation, hippocampal function and memory impairment in a mouse model of repetitive TBI. Moreover, you will contribute to the identification of conserved cell populations, transcriptional programs and intercellular communication networks affected by TBI in the mouse and human hippocampus.

For this, you will use an established mouse model of closed head rmTBI in combination with single-nucleus/spatial transcriptomics, cellular morphology, electrophysiology, behavioural testing, and molecular assays to identify mechanisms linking rmTBI to persistent hippocampal dysfunction and neuroinflammation. All the necessary techniques, expertise and training opportunities are available in our labs.

Tasks and responsibilities:
  • complete a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration (four years);
  • systematically and independently designing, performing and documenting experiments;
  • setting up and running bioinformatic pipelines to complement experimental work;
  • be an active and responsible member of both our research groups and discuss work with group members during departmental meetings and incorporate their feedback;
  • taking a leading role in writing manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals;
  • participating in PhD training programme of the University of Amsterdam and The Graduate School Neurosciences Amsterdam Rotterdam (ONWAR);
  • assist teaching and supervision of Bachelor and Master students at the UvA.

You will get the opportunity to:
  • present results at (inter)national scientific conferences;
  • expand your academic, professional and personal skills;
  • contribute to science communication and outreach activities;
  • thrive in a team that values impactful research and mutual support;
  • combine the advantages that a collaborative project offers, such as access to state-of-the art research facilities at both the Swammerdam Institute, and to those at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience.

What we ask of you
Your experience and profile:
  • a master’s degree in biomedical sciences with a neuroscience specialization or similar;
  • a strong affinity and hands-on experience with experimental work with laboratory animals and/or molecular and cellular biology. Having an Article 9 certificate to work with laboratory animals is a pre-requisite;
  • a strong (proven) interest in bioinformatics analysis of complex datasets
  • fluent in English, both written and spoken.

You are dedicated, accurate, stress-resistant, a pleasant colleague, well organized and prepared to, and capable of working at 2 different locations.

This is what we offer you
We offer a temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is January 2027. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

Based on a full-time appointment (38 hours per week) the gross monthly salary will range from €3.204 in the first year to €4.051 (scale P) in the last year. This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD candidate is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

Curious about our extensive secondary benefits package? You can read more about it here.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The position is located within the team of Dr. Carlos Fitzsimons (https://www.fitzsimonslab.eu), part of the Brain Plasticity group of the Swammerdam institute of the Faculty of Science.

The Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences (SILS) is located at the vibrant Amsterdam Science Park. SILS is one of eight institutes of the University of Amsterdam's Faculty of Science (FNWI). With around 240 employees, SILS carries out internationally high-quality life science research and provides education within various university programs. Research is also carried out in close cooperation with the medical, biotech, chemical, flavor, food & agricultural, and high-tech industries, and revolves around 4 main themes, Cell & Systems biology, Neurosciences, Microbiology and Green Life Sciences.

Within the Brain Plasticity group of SILS we study how our brain adapts to changes in an (often challenging) environment. We try to understand how plasticity is 'programmed', and how external factors like (early life) stress, nutrition, drugs, exercise or enrichment) can modify plasticity, and what role it plays in cognition and disorders, such as depression and dementia.

Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the red button. We accept applications until and including 30 November 2026. Evaluation of candidates will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

If you have any questions or do you require additional information? Please contact:
  • Dr. Carlos Fitzsimons, c.p.fitzsimons@uva.nl

Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file):
  • a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience;
  • a letter of motivation;
  • a list of specific courses and possibly publications, highlighting your training and expertise;
  • the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation.

A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure.
(for details: national knowledge security guidelines)

Only complete applications received within the response period via the link below will be considered.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Implementatie van matched care voor angst voor terugkeer van kanker in oncologiezorgnetwerken'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Krijg jij energie van onderzoek op het snijvlak van wetenschap, zorgpraktijk en regionale samenwerking? En wil jij bijdragen aan de duurzame implementatie van psychosociale zorg die echt aansluit bij de behoeften van mensen met en na kanker?

Als PhD-kandidaat / promovendus onderzoek je hoe mensen met en na kanker tijdig toegang kunnen krijgen tot passende, evidence-based psychosociale zorg. Centraal staat de implementatie van een matched-care model voor angst voor terugkeer van kanker binnen regionale oncologiezorgnetwerken. Binnen dit model wordt de intensiteit en vorm van psychosociale ondersteuning afgestemd op de aard en ernst van de klachten en op de behoeften en voorkeuren van de patiënt.

Het doel van de functie is om samen met patiënten, zorgprofessionals en andere betrokkenen te onderzoeken wat nodig is om dit matched-care model duurzaam in de dagelijkse oncologische zorg te implementeren. Je brengt in kaart hoe angst voor terugkeer van kanker momenteel wordt gesignaleerd, getrieerd en doorverwezen, welke factoren de implementatie binnen en tussen organisaties beïnvloeden en welke rollen, verantwoordelijkheden en samenwerkingsmechanismen nodig zijn om passende psychosociale zorg toegankelijk te maken. Op basis hiervan ontwikkel en test je samen met stakeholders implementatiestrategieën en praktische tools, die vervolgens in een regionaal oncologiezorgnetwerk (Friesland) worden toegepast en geëvalueerd.

Je werkt vanuit het Radboudumc in een unieke samenwerking tussen wetenschappelijke onderzoekers, zorgprofessionals en regionale en landelijke partners in de psychosociale oncologie (NVPO, LOPPSOZ). Je werkt nauw samen met onderzoekers binnen de POCON-werkgroep Implementatie, collega's van het Radboudumc, UMCG en IKNL, en met professionals, netwerkcoördinatoren en andere stakeholders binnen de oncologiezorgnetwerken in Friesland. Ook patiënten en vertegenwoordigers van relevante organisaties worden actief betrokken bij de ontwikkeling en evaluatie van de implementatieaanpak.

Wat deze functie bijzonder maakt, is de combinatie van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, implementatiewetenschap en directe impact op de zorgpraktijk. Je onderzoekt niet alleen óf psychosociale interventies werken, maar vooral hoe je ervoor zorgt dat patiënten deze zorg ook daadwerkelijk op het juiste moment en in de juiste vorm kunnen krijgen. Je werkt daarbij over de grenzen van disciplines en organisaties heen en draagt bij aan een aanpak die uiteindelijk ook buiten de deelnemende regio toepasbaar is. De ontwikkelde implementatiestrategieën, tools en inzichten zijn bedoeld als basis voor bredere, landelijke implementatie van evidence-based psychosociale zorg.

Belangrijkste taken en verantwoordelijkheden:
  • Uitvoeren van promotieonderzoek naar de implementatie van matched care voor angst voor terugkeer van kanker binnen oncologiezorgnetwerken;
  • In kaart brengen van bestaande signalering, triage, verwijzing en zorgpaden voor angst voor terugkeer van kanker;
  • Uitvoeren van kwalitatief onderzoek, waaronder interviews met zorgprofessionals en andere stakeholders;
  • Identificeren en analyseren van barrières en bevorderende factoren voor implementatie op patiënt-, professional-, organisatie- en netwerkniveau;
  • Toepassen van implementatiewetenschappelijke methoden en kaders, waaronder het CFIR-raamwerk en de CFIR-ERIC matching tool;
  • Samen met patiënten, zorgprofessionals, implementatie-experts en netwerkpartners ontwikkelen van implementatiestrategieën en praktische tools;
  • Bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling van een contextgevoelig implementatieplan voor regionale oncologiezorgnetwerken;
  • Voorbereiden, uitvoeren en evalueren van een regionale pilot in Friesland;
  • Vertalen van onderzoeksbevindingen naar concrete aanbevelingen voor de zorgpraktijk en naar een overdraagbare implementatieblauwdruk;
  • Publiceren van onderzoeksresultaten in internationale wetenschappelijke tijdschriften en presenteren op nationale en internationale congressen.

jobs.title: PhD position in “Water Footprint Assessment and Water Credit Design in Egypt’s Horticulture Sector”
jobs.description_html:
The Challenge

Egypt’s horticulture sector operates under growing pressure from limited water availability, salinity, and rising competition over finite water resources. At the same time, the sector is economically important for food security, rural livelihoods, and export earnings, which means that improving water productivity is not only an environmental protection measure but also a strategic development and trade challenge.

These pressures call for better evidence on current and future water use, stronger metrics for identifying good performance, and more robust ways to link farm-level improvements to wider policy and investment decisions. They also raise questions about how private-sector actors can support and scale water-smart change, including through credible incentive and financing mechanisms.

The position
You will join the Water Footprint in Action programme, a multi-partner initiative funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and focused on advancing water-smart agriculture in Egypt’s horticulture sector. The programme brings together three complementary lines of work: building a strong scientific and evidence base, strengthening advisory and knowledge systems, and supporting business innovation and investment in water-smart solutions. Within this wider setting, your PhD work will mainly sit in the research and knowledge component, while also helping connect scientific insights to shared knowledge resources, decision-support tools, stakeholder learning, and new financing approaches.

A preliminary research plan looks as follows.

First, you will develop and apply quantitative approaches to analyse the present and future water consumption (i.e., the water footprint) of Egypt’s horticulture sector. This includes crop modelling using our in-house ACEA model, designing climate and socio-economic scenarios, and linking analyses across scales to local intervention settings, national policy priorities, and trade dynamics.

Next, you will work on water footprint benchmarks and performance indicators. In this part of the PhD, you will compare different ways of defining good performance, for example by looking at producer performance based on Best Available Technology and Best Available Practice, and relate these to broader sustainability and efficiency indicators.

A third part of your research will focus on how water savings and other water-smart improvements can be measured in a way that is credible, transparent, and useful in practice. You will help develop a science-based method that can underpin incentive or finance mechanisms for improved water performance, working closely with project partners and engaging with wider debates around environmental credits and integrity.

You will be embedded in an international consortium and work closely with partners in the Netherlands and Egypt, including Egyptian water and agricultural research centres. The position includes intensive interaction with stakeholders, frequent visits to project locations and case-study sites in Egypt, and an active role in a broader knowledge exchange programme through joint research, data exchange, publications, and learning activities.

jobs.title: PhD position: PFAS free membranes for use in electrolysers
jobs.description_html:
Why apply?
This multidisciplinary project integrates electrochemistry, metal–organic framework-based materials, and membrane chemistry to develop the next generation of high-performance membranes and unlock new possibilities for advanced molecular separation and transport.

Can you design the membrane that powers the next generation of electrolysers?
Electrolysis and electrocatalysis have a key role to play in creating a more sustainable chemical industry. At the heart of these technologies are membranes that control the transport of protons and other species—but today’s proton exchange membranes rely heavily on PFAS-based materials such as Nafion®. We are looking for a PhD candidate to develop a new generation of high-performance, PFAS-free proton-conductive membranes. In this project, you will combine the unique properties of proton-conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with those of proton-conductive polymers to create innovative membrane materials. You will systematically investigate how molecular structure, composition, and membrane architecture determine proton transport and overall performance. Your research will span materials chemistry, membrane science, and electrochemistry. You will establish design principles for high-performance proton-conductive membranes and put your materials to the test in different electrolyser configurations. This is an opportunity to work at the interface of fundamental materials science and real-world energy technology, with the ambition to develop membrane materials that can help enable a cleaner and more sustainable chemical industry. The PhD students will be supervised by Dennis Hetterscheid (Leiden Institute of Chemistry).

What you bring
We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated candidate who is excited to pursue an interdisciplinary PhD at the interface of electrochemistry, materials chemistry, and membrane science. The project combines electrochemistry, MOF synthesis and characterization, physical measurements, and electrolysis studies, offering the opportunity to develop expertise across multiple fields.

You hold an MSc degree in Physical Chemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline, with a background in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, membrane chemistry, MOF synthesis, or materials characterization. Most importantly, you are curious, eager to learn, and motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries.

You will join a highly collaborative and international research team of PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers, MSc students, and scientific staff. We collaborate extensively with research groups both locally and internationally, and work closely with industry partners to translate fundamental scientific discoveries into technologies with real-world societal impact.

We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive. Our lab values diversity, accessibility, and inclusion in all their forms, and we strive to foster a safe and supportive workplace that encourages personal and professional growth, well-being, scientific integrity, and responsible research.

If you are excited by the opportunity to combine fundamental materials chemistry with electrochemical energy technologies and help develop the membranes of the future, we would love to hear from you.

Skills:
  • Hands-on experimental experience, with co-authorship of one or more scientific publications considered an advantage.
  • A strong interest in fundamental science and a genuine curiosity about understanding the principles underlying new materials and technologies.
  • High motivation for research, combined with a solid theoretical understanding of relevant scientific principles.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to plan your work, work independently, and communicate your progress clearly.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • A collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively as part of a diverse, interdisciplinary team.

What we offer
Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organization is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organize through Healthy University.

The position will be for a maximum of 4 years, and the candidate is expected to complete a PhD thesis at the end of this period. A contribution to classroom teaching (maximum 10% of the time) will be part of the responsibilities of the candidate, as well as supervision of BSc and MSc research projects that contribute to the goals of this PhD project.

We offer a stimulating and interactive research environment, free use of all state-of-the-art facilities, and a competitive salary.

We also offer:
  • An employment contract for 12 months initially, to be extended for 3 more years upon satisfactory performance. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
  • A salary between € 3.204,- and € 4.051,- gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours - PhD student);
  • A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
  • Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
  • Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.
  • Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;
  • If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
  • A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces.

For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

Where you will work

Leiden University is one of Europe’s leading international research universities.

Thanks to its committed and inspired employees, the university enjoys a leading role in academic research and education. Every year, Leiden University scores very well in prominent rankings. This means that, to maintain our position, the bar is set very high. Regardless of the work you do at our university, you are always encouraged to broaden your horizons, develop your talents and reach your full potential.

Faculty of Science & Leiden Institute of Chemistry
The Faculty of Science at Leiden University is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to contribute to addressing the major societal challenges of the future.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Population-Scale Network Science (1.0 FTE, 4 years)
jobs.description_html:
About this position. In this 4-year fully funded PhD position, the focus is on devising new network science approaches for analyzing longitudinal, population-scale social network data on the Dutch population data, sourced from Statistics Netherlands. Such data presents distinctive methodological challenges: their scale and temporal character require fast algorithms and careful tailoring of commonly used network measures and algorithms.
One particular challenge for the candidate applying for this position, is to develop novel measures of structural (in)equivalence in social networks for obtaining an interpretable understanding of how social network structure differs between different subgroups of a population. Moreover, when applied to two entirely different populations, these methods of comparing network structure should facilitate cross-country comparative analyses of population-scale social network structure, enabling an understanding of similarities and differences in the social fabric of countries.
In addition to the above, there is also space for the candidate to pursue a direction of research related to network science that fits both the candidate and the broader aims of the group.

Embedding. The PhD candidate will be employed at the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), which is the computer science and AI institute of the Faculty of Science of Leiden University. More in particular, the candidate will become part of 1) the interdisciplinary inter-university PLANET-NL initiative, which is a collaboration of the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University rooted in computational social science and network science, and 2) the Leiden Network Science group.
Both the research groups and the institute are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinal and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society. The candidate will be asked to engage in (limited) BSc and MSc student (co-) supervision, small teaching assistance tasks, and potentially minor roles in scientific organizational activities.

What you will do
  • Conducting research in the area of network science;
  • Writing an article-based PhD thesis;
  • Engaging in collaborative research as a member of the PLANET-NL inter-university research group;
  • Membership of and engagement with the Leiden Network Science research group;
  • Co-supervising BSc and MSc students on topics related to data science and network science;
  • Engaging in minor scientific organizational organizing activities.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. Our people are driven by curiosity to expand fundamental knowledge and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from mathematics, artificial intelligence, computer science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences.
The faculty is home to more than 2,700 staff members and over 6,000 students enrolled in nine bachelor's and fifteen master's programs. We are located at the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry come together.
You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. According to an independent research assessment, LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. We offer a clear and welcoming career path for young and talented scientists with the ambition to grow. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: http://www.cs.leiden.edu

What you bring
  • A MSc* in computer science or a related field (e.g., mathematics, physics or computational social science), showing affinity with network science (or complex networks / social network analysis);
  • Good writing skills, demonstrated through a writing sample (typically the MSc thesis) to be submitted with the application;
  • Good proficiency of the English language, demonstrated by the ability to have a near fluent in-person conversation in English;
  • Curious and open-minded attitude to successfully collaborate across disciplines, preferably with an interest in translating insights from computer science to the social sciences, and vice versa;
  • Experience with programming in Python, or otherwise in R and/or C++;

*: excellent candidates not (yet) past the MSc phase, but with graduation in early Spring 2027 well in sight, are also invited to apply.

What we offer

  • A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;

Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in the research project 'Entangled with Seaweed', case studies in South Africa
jobs.description_html:
The The Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University is looking for an ambitious PhD-candidate to study the impacts of economization of seaweed as part of ‘blue economy’ strategies in South Africa. Research focuses on the impacts on coastal communities, considering that in South Africa colonial and apartheid legacies still influence patterns of access to coastal areas. You will work within the project ‘Entangled in seaweed: The politics of economizing nature in Scotland and South Africa’ funded by an NWO Open Competition grant.

Project Description
The project investigates the impacts of economisation of seaweed as part of a global drive to develop ‘blue economy’ strategies. Seaweed harvesting and cultivation (as food, or fertilizer- and bioplastic ingredient) are increasing considerably and promoted as contributing to sustainable development. The project focuses on coastal communities in Scotland, which has developed a comprehensive blue economy strategy. Building on insights from political ecology and valuation studies and inspired by the multispecies turn in anthropology, this project aims to study local impacts of new forms of economisation of seaweed, and the possible contestations these may entail. It seeks to incorporate the ideas, interests, and knowledge from local groups who live from, in and with seaweed ecologies, examining how new versions of economisation affect local social relations, including the entanglements with non-humans these ecologies and economisations depend on. It does so by focusing on valuations of seaweed ecologies, based on an understanding of values as enacted through practices by all (human and non-human) stakeholders. The project employs a collaborative approach vis-à-vis research participants and a wider audience through a visual storytelling approach.

What you will do
You will work in a project team consisting of PhD-candidates and researchers at Leiden University, collaborating with project partners in South Africa. You will:
  • Develop a research proposal in the context of the overall project theme, and conduct twelve months of ethnographic research in South Africa. An ethics review and contribution to the data management plan are included in the proposal development. Research includes document/policy analysis, participant observation, interviews, and the application of participatory visual storytelling methods.
  • Analyse research findings and write a dissertation that contributes to the objectives of the ‘Entangled with Seaweed’ project.
  • Actively contribute to the output and dissemination of the research project, which includes collaborating with the other team members on academic and non-academic publications, science communication, and the organization of workshops, seminars and an exhibition.
  • Participate in relevant PhD-courses and masterclasses, organized in accordance with the guidelines of the Faculty of Social Science and the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology. PhD-courses at Stellenbosch University, our partner in the project, can be included in the individual training and supervision plan as well.
  • Participate in the PhD programme and other academic activities of the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University. During your stay in South Africa you will also be able to participate in the PhD-programme at the Department of Sociology and Social Anthropology at Stellenbosch University.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences consists of five institutes: the Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, Education and Child Studies, Political Science, and Psychology. The faculty is home to approximately 7,000 students and 1,000 staff members. Our institutes are dedicated not only to education but also to groundbreaking research that expands our understanding of human behavior and societal structures. What makes our faculty unique is the diversity of research topics, the variety of teaching approaches, and the structure of professional support. This provides you with the opportunity to explore and develop your interests and expertise. For an introduction to our faculty, visit our website: Welcome to the Leiden Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences – Leiden University.

Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology (CADS)
Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology concentrates on 'global vulnerability and social resilience'. The institute has three main themes: diversity, sustainability, and digitalisation. CADS is dedicated to making a real-world impact, not just studying change, but also working with communities to promote positive change through education and research. We use a unique approach that blends qualitative, quantitative, audiovisual, and digital methods based on ethnographic fieldwork.

With our unique blend of interdisciplinary interests, comparative regional studies, and social science research methods, we emphasize our role in the extensive collaborative network within Leiden University. In both our research and education, we engage in extensive interdisciplinary and international networks.

The project team
The project team at Leiden University works closely together with colleagues at the University of Edinburgh, the Scottish Association for Marine Science, and Stellenbosch University. The PhD-students will be jointly supervised by Leiden University and Stellenbosch University, and Leiden University and the University of Edinburgh respectively. A project assistant will assist with training and dissemination activities.

What you bring
  • A Master’s degree in Anthropology, Sociology, Environmental Humanities or another relevant discipline within the social sciences or humanities.
  • Demonstrable excellent qualitative research skills and experience with ethnographic fieldwork.
  • Affinity with the topics of sustainability and environmental justice.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Strong command of English;
  • Knowledge of one of the other official languages of South Africa is a bonus.
  • Excellent social and organisational skills and the ability to work independently as well as in a team.

What we offer
Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University.

We also offer:
  • PHD: An employment contract for 38 hours per week as a PhD candidate, initially for a period of 1 year, with the possibility of extension for 3 years after a positive evaluation. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
  • A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student);

  • Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
  • Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.
  • Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;

For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

What we value

We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

As part of your application we ask you to submit:

Miriam Waltz, project member, by email: m.h.a.waltz@fsw.leidenuniv.nl. You can apply until 7 November 2026; applications will be processed immediately. jobs.title: PhD Position in Space Law and Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description_html:
You will conduct doctoral research within EO-TRUST, a €1 million multidisciplinary project funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO), led by Dr Ioana Bratu. Your research will examine the legal and ethical dimensions of AI-enabled Earth Observation, focusing on how space law, AI regulation and related legal frameworks address questions of resilience, responsibility and trustworthy use of satellite data. You will work in a multidisciplinary environment connecting law with Earth Observation, artificial intelligence and computer science.

Your duties
  • conduct independent doctoral research on the legal and ethical governance of AI-enabled Earth Observation
  • map and analyse applicable legal frameworks, including international space law, the EU Space Act, the EU AI Act and relevant security and military law
  • conduct doctrinal and empirical research, including interviews and engagement with governmental, regulatory, academic and industry stakeholders
  • contribute to academic publications, policy outputs, conferences, workshops and the development of principles for responsible and explainable AI-enabled Earth Observation
  • contribute to the activities of Amsterdam Law & Technology Institute and Amsterdam Space Law & Sustainability Center.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'preventie van gokschade'
jobs.description_html:
Achtergrond

Gokschade is één van de snelst groeiende uitdagingen voor de volksgezondheid in Nederland. Steeds meer mensen ervaren psychische, sociale en financiële problemen als gevolg van gokken, terwijl slechts een klein deel passende hulp ontvangt. Veel gokkers en hun omgeving kennen het ondersteuningsaanbod niet en het huidige preventieaanbod sluit vaak onvoldoende aan op wat mensen écht nodig hebben. Met dit promotieonderzoek draag je bij aan een preventiesysteem dat werkt: toegankelijk, effectief en afgestemd op de behoeften van verschillende groepen gokkers.
 

Projectomschrijving

Dit project biedt een kans om bij te dragen aan de ontwikkeling, optimalisatie en evaluatie van effectieve preventieve interventies voor mensen met beginnende gokproblemen. Je werkt aan drie samenhangede deelstudies:

  1. Het ontwikkelen, optimaliseren en evalueren van interventies, zoals bijvoorbeeld een gokpauze;
  2. Een longitudinaal cohortonderzoek naar gokgedrag, hulpzoekgedrag, het bereik en de impact van preventieve interventies;
  3. De implementatie en kennisdeling om een samenhangend, duurzaam en toegankelijk preventieaanbod te realiseren.

Jouw functie

Als promovendus krijg je de ruimte om wetenschappelijke diepgang te combineren met maatschappelijke relevantie. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het opzetten en uitvoeren van de deelstudies binnen het project. Je vertaalt onderzoeksbevindingen naar wetenschappelijke publicaties, die uiteindelijk samenkomen in een proefschrift. Daarnaast draag je bij aan kennisverspreiding en presenteer je onderzoeksresultaten op nationale en internationale congressen. Je zet een longitudinale cohortstudie op met behulp van vragenlijsten om inzicht te verkrijgen in gokgedrag, hulpzoekgedrag en de acceptatie, het gebruik en de effectiviteit van preventieve interventies onder beginnende gokkers tot mensen die problemen ervaren door het gokken. Daarnaast draag je actief bij aan de doorontwikkeling van preventieve interventies en aan de kwalitatieve deelstudies binnen het project. Eén dag in de week zul je op het Trimbos-instituut In Utrecht werken om de samenwerking met de gokexperts daar vorm te geven.

Tranzo verzorgt ook de mastertrack Health, Wellbeing & Society en de mastertrack Sociaal Werk, in de Sociologie master. Er wordt van alle Tranzo medewerkers verwacht dat men een bijdrage levert aan het onderwijs, bijvoorbeeld in de vorm van verzorgen werkgroepen/colleges of nakijkwerk. Afspraken hierover worden met de leidinggevende gemaakt.

jobs.title: PhD Position 'Why Are the Super-Rich So Tax-Averse?'
jobs.description_html:
The super-rich avoid and evade personal taxation a great deal, but why are they so tax-averse? Is it simply what anyone would do, given the opportunity? Or is it their social environment that makes them think avoiding and evading is appropriate? UvA’s Political Science department has two vacancies for PhD candidates to tackle these questions.

‘Why Are the Super-Rich So Tax-Averse?’
Our NWO-funded project, led by prof. Marlies Glasius, has two vacancies for PhD candidates.

The first position is for a project on legal tax avoidance by means of relocation. Who moves to low tax countries, and what motivates them? Is it simply those super-rich people who stand most to gain financially from such a move, or are other factors at play? What are the barriers to relocating? What are the political and media discourses on super-rich tax flight and do they reflect economic realities? Are they similar across different European countries, and do they change over time? What are the sources of such discourses?

The second position is about (mostly illegal) tax evasion by the super-rich through the use of tax havens. It proposes to use the data of the Offshore Leaks Database in order to better understand who puts their money in tax havens, and what motivates them. Is it the super-rich with the heaviest tax burden? Are super-rich citizens of some European countries more inclined to use tax havens than others? Is such tax evasion associated with luxurious lifestyles and with places where the super-rich gather? And how do the super-rich respond when data leaks expose their secret holdings? The project concerns personal, not corporate taxation, with a focus on European countries. For the full text of the project proposal, see: https://www.uva.nl/en/profile/g/l/m.e.glasius/m.e.glasius.html#Politics-of-the-SuperRich

What are you going to do
You will develop your own PhD project within the broader *Tax Averse* project: while we expect you to build upon its central questions and premises, we also encourage you to introduce new questions, case studies or methods based on your own expertise and interests.

You will:
  • pursue a PhD in the social sciences and participate in the AISSR PhD programme;
  • collect and analyse qualitative and/or quantative research data;
  • work towards a PhD thesis either as a collection of articles or as a monograph;
  • participate in meetings of the project research group and help organise project-related activities such as academic and stakeholder workshops;
  • present your work at national and international conferences;
  • teach (10% of your working time) within the Department of Political Science.

What do you have to offer
If the questions posed above are fascinating to you, and you love academic research and writing, you should apply. The ideal candidate for Project 1 would have
  • a Master’s degree in political economy, political science, sociology or communication science;
  • proven research talent in a relevant field, demonstrated by a Master thesis and/or a published article or research report;
  • qualitative and quantitative research skills.

The ideal candidate for Project 2 would have
  • a Master’s in political economy, political science, sociology or geography;
  • proven research talent in a relevant field, demonstrated by a Master thesis and/or a published article or research report;
  • familiarity with causal inference and quantitative research skills. GIS skills, experience with spatial weighting and/or social network analysis would be desirable.

What else do we offer you
We offer a temporary employment contract of 38 hours per week for a maximum term of four years. The initial employment is for one year. Following a positive assessment, this term will be extended by a maximum of three years, which should result in the conferral of a doctorate.

Based on a full-time appointment (38 hours per week) the gross monthly salary will range from €3,204 in the first year to €4,051 (scale P) in the last year. The UFO profile PhD candidate is applicable.

We additionally offer an extensive package of secondary benefits, including 8% holiday allowance and a year-end bonus of 8.3%.

Salary and conditions in line with the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities.

You will attend courses offered by the AISSR and the Graduate School of Social Sciences as part of the PhD program. In addition to doing research, publicizing your findings, and participating in both national and international academic events, you will be involved in teaching (roughly 10% of your time).

In this team, you will work
You will be part of a small core team centered on the *Tax Averse* project, embedded within the programme group Transnational Configurations, Conflict and Governance and the Department of Political Science. While the two PhD candidates work closely together, each will develop their own academic profile. The composition of the supervisory team will be tailored to the specific thematic focus of the two PhD projects.

In your cover letter, please indicate which position you are applying for — Position 1, Position 2, or both. For more information, contact m.glasius@uva.nl. The intended starting date is 1 January 2027. You can apply via the red button until 26 October. Your application should comprise a CV, a letter of motivation, a writing sample (for instance your Master’s thesis) and a research statement of maximum 2,000 words (not including references), outlining your own research proposal in relation to the broader project. The proposal should include information on relevant literatures, potential research questions and methodological strategies.

jobs.title: Promovendus ‘Sociotherapeutische leefmilieu’s op woongroepen voor jonge mensen met dementie’
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Iedereen is verschillend en heeft een eigen persoonlijkheid. Waar de ene persoon behoefte heeft aan sociale contacten of uitdaging, zoekt de ander juist rust, structuur en veiligheid. Met sociotherapeutische leefmilieu’s (STL’s) stemmen we de leefomgeving binnen een zorginstelling af op de individuele kenmerken en behoeften van mensen met dementie die daar verblijven.

Binnen het landelijke onderzoeksprogramma YOD-INCLUDED zoeken wij een promovendus die onderzoek gaat doen naar STL’s op woongroepen en dagbesteding voor mensen die leven met dementie op jonge leeftijd. Juist voor deze groep sluiten de behoeften vaak minder goed aan bij het traditionele aanbod.

In dit promotietraject onderzoek je hoe STL’s momenteel worden toegepast binnen zorginstellingen met een gespecialiseerd zorgaanbod voor deze doelgroep, welke factoren implementatie bevorderen of belemmeren en hoe naasten hierbij betrokken kunnen worden. Op basis van een landelijke survey, observaties, literatuuronderzoek en interviews ontwikkel en verbeter je het zorgconcept. Vervolgens begeleid en evalueer je de implementatie in meerdere zorginstellingen in een haalbaarheidsstudie en ontwikkel je praktische materialen die implementatie op grotere schaal ondersteunen.

Zo draag je bij aan persoonsgerichte zorg voor mensen met dementie op jonge leeftijd.

jobs.title: PhD position 6G-Native Distributed Intelligence for Physical AI
jobs.description_html:
Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications.

Job description
Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge.

How can 6G enable resource-constrained Physical AI by dynamically distributing and adapting AI workloads across embedded devices, the edge, and the cloud, while jointly orchestrating communication, computation, and sensing under strict latency, reliability, and resource constraints? The project will investigate resource-aware 6G-native distributed AI techniques such as collaborative and split inference, adaptive model partitioning and selection, computation offloading, and cross-layer resource orchestration. A particular focus will be on how 6G can enable Physical AI systems to adapt to changing network, compute, sensor, and energy conditions while maintaining predictable performance.

You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos.

Job requerements

jobs.title: PhD Position in Political Science
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Political Science is looking for a PhD candidate to work in the “Doctoral Network Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe (DIViNE)” project, funded by the HORIZON MSCA action. The candidate will be supervised by Dr. Ursula Daxecker (University of Amsterdam and Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science) and Dr. Hanne Fjelde (University of Uppsala) and join a network of 10 PhD candidates across five universities. At the University of Amsterdam, the PhD candidate will be part of the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research (AISSR) programme group Political Institutions and Identities (PII).

DIViNE brings together leading European research environments — UvA (Amsterdam), UESSEX (Essex), UMIL (Milan), UC3M (Carlos III de Madrid) and UU (Uppsala) — and partner organizations – including the new Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science — to combine complementary strengths in quantitative conflict research, behavioral and experimental methods, historical and archival inquiry, institutional and normative theory, and applied policy engagement.

Join us!
Democracies are commonly seen as able to channel contestation through institutionalized processes and nonviolent action. Yet, democratic polities frequently experience a broad range of political violence — from riots and organized electoral intimidation to extremist mobilization and criminal violence — and violence can test and, at times, erode democratic norms and institutions. Moreover, democracies themselves may respond to perceived threats with measures (e.g., militarized policing, emergency legislation, selective repression) that threaten to undermine core features of liberal democracy such as the rule of law, civil liberties and institutional impartiality. The DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe) consolidates comparative, historical, theoretical and methodological strands to build a coherent new research program on political violence in democracies.

The position is part of WP2 on Democratization and Conflict Resolution, which explores the implications of regime transitions for patterns of violence. The PhD project analyzes endogenous processes through which political violence persists within democracies, focusing on how transitions reshape rent-seeking incentives, decentralization bargains, and relationships between national incumbents and local elites. It theorizes that democratization may inadvertently generate new incentives for electoral, ethnic, or criminal violence, depending on the nature of rents, types of institutional reforms, or elite-local configurations. Empirical work will combine cross-national statistical analysis, subnational mixed-methods studies, and process tracing in Global South contexts. The project will contribute a unified theoretical framework explaining why violence endures despite formal democratic reforms.

The doctoral trajectory includes a three-month secondment at Uppsala University and IDEA in Sweden, which will provide applied exposure to policy debates on democratization, institutional design, and violence prevention, alongside training in comparative policy analysis.

For more information about the network, consult https://divine.unimi.it/

What are you going to do
You will:
  • be affiliated with the AISSR and participate in its organized PhD training. The academic work is to result in a doctoral thesis that will be defended at the Faculty of Social Sciences with the goal of obtaining the degree of PhD.
  • conduct PhD research on democratization and the persistence of political violence, including quantitative analysis of data, surveys and survey experiments, and fieldwork interviews.
  • co-author publications with other project members;
  • take active part in DIViNE training network activities including network training modules, PhD colloquia, research workshops, secondments, and training workshops;
  • take active part of the research environment at the AISSR, including PII research seminars, AISSR center activities, among others.
  • teach Bachelor-level courses, depending upon availability and as suitable for the PhD schedule (for a max. of 10%).
  • assist with administrative responsibilities related to the project, such as the organization of workshops, conferences, or other project events.
  • make Amsterdam (or a location within commuting distance) your primary residence for the initial three years of the PhD project, and Göttingen (or a location within commuting distance) for the one-year extension. We will assist with finding adequate housing and with applying for visa and residence permits.

What do you have to offer
You have the following credentials:

Essential:
  • a Master’s degree or equivalent in political science or closely related discipline. The degree must have been obtained by the start of your employment;
  • an excellent command of social science research methods, including quantitative methodology such as panel regression, analysis of large administrative data, survey data, causal inference design, and statistical programming in Stata/R/etc.;
  • an interest to conduct fieldwork in the Global South;
  • excellent oral and written communication skills in English;
  • independent thinking and critical analytical skills;
  • the ability to work independently and in a team.

Desirable:
  • knowledge of regional contexts of special relevance to project members and supervisors, such as South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa;
  • experience with qualitative methods and mixed-methods approaches;
  • expertise in research on political violence.

What else do we offer you
The position concerns temporary employment of 38 hours per week for a maximum term of three years at the University of Amsterdam, under the MSCA Doctoral Network employment conditions. The initial employment is for one year with an intended starting date of January 2027. Following a positive assessment and barring altered circumstances, this term will be extended by a maximum of two years. A one-year extension at the Max Planck Institute of Political and Social Science in Göttingen is envisioned. The employment should result in the conferral of a doctorate. We will put together a curriculum which will also include the opportunity to attend training courses and both national and international events. You will also be tasked with teaching Bachelor's students.

Please follow the links to learn more about the Department of Political Science and the AISSR at the University of Amsterdam, the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at the University of Uppsala, and the Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science.

In this department, you will work
We offer a challenging work environment with a variety of duties and ample scope for individual initiative and development within an inspiring organisation. The social and behavioural sciences play a leading role in addressing the major societal challenges faced by the world, the Netherlands and Amsterdam, now and in the future.

To work at the University of Amsterdam is to work in a discerning, independent, creative, innovative and international climate characterised by an open atmosphere and a genuine engagement with the city of Amsterdam and society.

The UvA is an equal-opportunity employer. We prioritise diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We value a spirit of enquiry and perseverance, provide the space to keep asking questions, and promote a culture of curiosity and creativity.

Please note that PhD researchers recruited on the project must satisfy the MCSA mobility requirements, which for this position means that they cannot have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Also note that the program will entail mobility across the institutions and partners in the network.

To apply, please submit the following five documents combined into a single PDF document with your name and the vacancy number in the document title:
  • a CV
  • a cover letter that summarizes your preparation and motivation to pursue this degree
  • a two-page proposal outlining a PhD project that fits the above parameters
  • unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts
  • the contact details of two academic references
  • a writing sample of max. 10 pages (this can be an excerpt from longer written material).

Please do NOT include any other materials at this stage. No other materials will be reviewed by the committee.

You can apply online by clicking on link below.

The deadline for applications is November 11, 2026. Additional materials such as recommendation letters will be requested only for shortlisted candidates. The selection committee expects interviews to take place online in the week of November 23. We ask you to ensure availability in this week.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Political Science: Militarization and Democratic Erosion in Latin America
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Political Science is looking for a PhD candidate to work in the “Doctoral Network Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe (DIViNE)” project, funded by the HORIZON MSCA action. The candidate will be supervised by Dr. Abbey Steele (University of Amsterdam) and Dr. Juan Masullo (University of Milan) and join a network of 10 PhD candidates across five universities. At the University of Amsterdam, the PhD candidate will be part of the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research (AISSR) programme group Political Institutions and Identities (PII).

DIViNE brings together leading European research environments — UvA (Amsterdam), UESSEX (Essex), UMIL (Milan), UC3M (Carlos III de Madrid) and UU (Uppsala) — and partner organizations to combine complementary strengths in quantitative conflict research, behavioral and experimental methods, historical and archival inquiry, institutional and normative theory, and applied policy engagement.

Join us!
Democracies are commonly seen as able to channel contestation through institutionalized processes and nonviolent action. Yet, democratic polities frequently experience a broad range of political violence — from riots and organized electoral intimidation to extremist mobilization and criminal violence — and violence can test and, at times, erode democratic norms and institutions. Moreover, democracies themselves may respond to perceived threats with measures (e.g., militarized policing, emergency legislation, selective repression) that threaten to undermine core features of liberal democracy such as the rule of law, civil liberties and institutional impartiality. The DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe) consolidates comparative, historical, theoretical and methodological strands to build a coherent new research program on political violence in democracies.

The position is part of WP3 on Dynamics of Support for Violent Movements and Responses, which examines how democracies respond to violence and how these responses shape democratic quality. Many democratic governments increasingly rely on militarized policing, emergency measures, and “iron-fist” security policies that may temporarily reduce insecurity, but potentially at the cost of weakened accountability and distorted institutional responsiveness and constraints. WP3 analyzes the micro-foundations of public support for repression, the institutional incentives behind securitized policies, and alternative strategies better aligned with democratic principles. The PhD project, Militarization, Public Support, and Democratic Erosion in Latin America, examines the interplay between public support for militarized security, institutional legacies of civil–military relations, and democratic erosion. It investigates when and why citizens endorse the use of armed forces for domestic security, how exposure to violence and distrust in civilian institutions shape these preferences, and how public opinion interacts with institutional militarization and executive aggrandizement. Empirical work will combine survey experiments, cross-national quantitative analysis (drawing on datasets such as LAPOP, V-Dem, and Latinobarómetro), and qualitative fieldwork in selected Latin American contexts. The project will contribute to understanding how coercive governance becomes normalized and how democratic quality is affected by persistent militarization.

The candidate will divide their training between Amsterdam and Milan, acquiring expertise in mixed-methods research, Latin American politics, conflict analysis, and survey experimentation. The doctoral trajectory also includes a three-month non-academic secondment at Fondazione Giangiacomo Feltrinelli in Milan, which will develop skills in policy outreach, public communication, and engagement with human rights and security-sector organizations. The PhD will begin in February 2027.
